reallife_social_drifted: You and {name} have drifted apart. A call would be a start.
reallife_social_memory_crash: You crashed with them in the car
reallife_social_call_acq_1: Oh, hi! It's you. I wasn't sure you'd actually call.
reallife_social_call_acq_2: Hello? Oh, hey. Give me a second, I'll step outside. There. What's up?
reallife_social_call_acq_3: Hi! Good timing, I just put the kettle on.
reallife_social_call_friend_1: Hey you. I was just thinking it had been a while.
reallife_social_call_friend_2: There you are. Talk to me, I've got ten minutes and nothing to do with them.
reallife_social_call_friend_3: Hey! Perfect, I needed an excuse to stop what I was doing.
reallife_social_call_friend_4: Well, look who remembered my number.
reallife_social_call_close_1: I knew it was you before I looked. What's going on?
reallife_social_call_close_2: Finally. I've been saving things up to tell you.
reallife_social_call_close_3: Hey, you. Sit down, this may take a while.
reallife_social_call_love_1: Hi, love. I was hoping that was you.
reallife_social_call_love_2: Hey. I missed your voice today.
reallife_social_call_love_3: There's my favourite person. How's your day?
reallife_social_call_love_4: Hi, you. Tell me something good.
reallife_social_call_mom_1: Hello, sweetheart! Let me turn the radio down.
reallife_social_call_mom_2: There you are. I was starting to think you'd lost your phone.
reallife_social_call_mom_3: Oh, it's you! I was just telling the neighbour about you.
reallife_social_call_again_1: Twice in one day? Something must be up.
reallife_social_call_again_2: Hello again. Did you forget something?
reallife_social_call_again_3: You again! Not that I'm complaining.
reallife_social_call_drifted_1: Oh. Hi. It's been a long time, hasn't it?
reallife_social_call_drifted_2: Wow, hello stranger. I thought you'd deleted my number.
reallife_social_voicemail_1: It rings out. {first} must be asleep.
reallife_social_voicemail_2: "Hi, it's {first}. I'm not picking up, so it's either very late or I'm ignoring you. Leave a message."
reallife_social_ring_open_1: Hey, it's {first}. Have you got a minute?
reallife_social_ring_open_2: Hi, it's me, {first}. I'm not catching you in the middle of something, am I?
reallife_social_ring_open_3: It's {first}. I thought I'd ring instead of texting for once.
reallife_social_chat_again: We covered everything earlier! Unless there was something else?
reallife_social_chat_bye_1: Right, I'd better go. This was nice.
reallife_social_chat_bye_2: I'll let you get on. Don't be a stranger.
reallife_social_chat_bye_3: Okay, go and be busy. Talk soon.
reallife_social_chat_bye_4: Good to hear your voice. Look after yourself.
reallife_social_chat_bye_mom_1: Eat something green, and call me again soon. Love you.
reallife_social_chat_bye_mom_2: Off you go, then. And wear a coat. Love you, sweetheart.
reallife_social_offer_coffee: I could murder a coffee. {place} does a decent one, about {cost} each.
reallife_social_offer_meal: I'm starving just thinking about it. {place}? It's around {cost} a head.
reallife_social_offer_drinks: A proper night out. {place}, drinks, bad dancing. Call it {cost} each.
reallife_social_offer_cinema: There's something on at {place} I've wanted to see. Tickets are about {cost}.
reallife_social_offer_walk: Honestly? Just a walk. Meet me outside {place} and we'll see where our feet go.
reallife_social_offer_drive: Take me for a drive. Pick me up outside {place} and just go, I don't mind where.
reallife_social_offer_workout: Come and train with me at {place}. It's {cost} to get in and I'll go easy on you.
reallife_social_offer_business: I still haven't seen your place properly. Show me round {place}?
reallife_social_offer_lift: I'm stuck outside {place} and I need to get to {to}. Any chance you could run me over there?
reallife_social_offer_moving: I'm moving my things from {place} round to {to}. It's only a few boxes, but I've only got two hands. Could you help?
reallife_social_when_two: When suits you? I could do {a}, or {b}.
reallife_social_when_one: I could do {a}. Does that work?
reallife_social_plan_yes_3: It's a plan. {time}, {place}. I'm looking forward to it already.
reallife_social_plan_busy_1: I'd love to, but I haven't got a free hour for the next couple of days. Ask me again?
reallife_social_plan_busy_2: This week is impossible, honestly. Try me in a day or two.
reallife_social_plan_mood_1: Not today. I'm not good company right now. Another time, I promise.
reallife_social_plan_mood_2: I can't face going out. It's been one of those days. Soon, though.
reallife_social_plan_already: Aren't you already meeting {other} at {time}? Sort that out first and then ask me.
reallife_social_plan_off: Let's just talk today. (Outings are switched off on the options page.)
reallife_social_plan_nowhere: I can't think of anywhere near you that would do. Ring me when you're somewhere livelier.
reallife_social_plan_reminder: We're still on for {outing}, aren't we? {place}, {time}.
reallife_social_plan_too_late: Cancel? I'm standing right here waiting for you!
reallife_social_plan_cancelled_1: Oh. All right. These things happen. Another time.
reallife_social_plan_cancelled_2: Really? I was looking forward to that. Fine, we'll find another day.
reallife_social_plan_remind: Within the hour: {outing} with {name}, outside {place} at {time}.
reallife_social_plan_lost: {name} could not make it to the place after all. Nobody's fault: the plan is off.
reallife_social_asked_busy: Oh, you've already got plans. Never mind, I'll manage.
reallife_social_asked_sorted: Don't worry about it, I've sorted something out. Thanks for calling back, though.
reallife_social_favour_refused: That's all right. I'll ask around.
reallife_social_lift_nocar: You haven't got the car with you? Never mind, I'll get the subway. Thanks anyway.
reallife_social_lift_coming: You're a lifesaver. I'm outside {place}. I'll look out for you.
reallife_social_moving_agreed: You're the best. Outside {place}, {time}. I'll owe you a pizza.
reallife_social_loan_ask_1: This is awkward. I'm short this month. Could you lend me {amount}? I'll have it back to you in a week or so.
reallife_social_loan_ask_2: I hate asking, but could I borrow {amount}? Something came up and payday is a week off.
reallife_social_loan_thanks_1: Thank you. Really. You'll have it back, I promise.
reallife_social_loan_thanks_2: You have no idea how much that helps. I won't forget it.
reallife_social_loan_refused_1: No, of course. I shouldn't have asked.
reallife_social_loan_refused_2: That's fine. Forget I said anything.
reallife_social_loan_short: Oh, you're short too? Then we're both in trouble. Don't worry about it.
reallife_social_loan_written_off: {name} never did pay back the {amount}. It is not coming.
reallife_social_borrow_yes_1: {amount}? Sure. I'll send it now. Get it back to me within {days} days, yes?
reallife_social_borrow_yes_2: I can do {amount}. It's on its way. No rush, but not never, okay? Say {days} days.
reallife_social_borrow_no_1: I don't think we know each other well enough for that yet. Sorry.
reallife_social_borrow_no_2: Money and friends... I'd rather not, if that's all right.
reallife_social_borrow_toomany: Again? That's the third thing you've asked me for this week. No. And I'm a bit annoyed you asked.
reallife_social_repay_thanks: Got it. Thanks for not making me chase you.
reallife_social_repay_short: You haven't got it on you? Then why bring it up? Soon, please.
reallife_social_birthday_thanks_1: You remembered! That's made my day.
reallife_social_birthday_thanks_2: Aw, thank you. I was pretending not to care whether anyone called.
reallife_social_birthday_thanks_3: Thank you! Another year older and none the wiser.
reallife_social_gift_thanks: You didn't have to do that! Thank you. I love it already.
reallife_social_gift_short: Save your money, you're broke! The call is present enough.
reallife_social_askout_yes_1: I was wondering when you'd ask. Yes. I'd like that a lot.
reallife_social_askout_yes_2: Like a date? ...Yes. Yes, all right. Don't make it weird.
reallife_social_askout_no_1: Oh. I'm flattered, I am. But I don't see us like that. Not now, anyway. Still friends?
reallife_social_askout_no_2: I like what we have. Let's not complicate it yet, okay?
reallife_social_official_yes: Official? Then officially: yes. I'm yours.
reallife_social_official_no: I'm happy with how things are going. Let's give it a little longer before we put a name on it.
reallife_social_movein_yes: Move in with you? I've had a bag half packed for a month. Yes!
reallife_social_movein_no: Not yet. It's a big step and I want to be sure. Ask me again in a while.
reallife_social_introduce_yes: You should meet {other}. Next time I see you out and about I'll bring them over.
reallife_social_introduce_no: Everyone I know is either away or boring right now. Maybe later.

reallife_social_topic_crash_1: I heard you had a smash on {street}. Are you in one piece?

reallife_social_topic_arrest_rb: Fine. I only asked because I was worried. Forget it.

reallife_social_topic_accident_2: There was a bad one on {street}, did you hear? Ambulance, police, the lot.
reallife_social_topic_accident_ra: You were? That must have been horrible to watch. I hope everyone walked away.
reallife_social_topic_accident_rb: Ha, tell me about it. I cross the road like it's a video game.
reallife_social_topic_crime_1: Did you hear about {what} on {street}? Unbelievable.
reallife_social_topic_crime_2: There was {what} on {street}. The whole street was talking about it.
reallife_social_topic_crime_ra: No! Were you all right? I'd have run a mile.
reallife_social_topic_crime_rb: I know, I know. I still jump when I hear a siren.
reallife_social_topic_shopgood_1: How's {shop} doing? I walked past and it looked busy.
reallife_social_topic_shopgood_2: So, {shop}. Is it making you rich yet?
reallife_social_topic_shopgood_b: I don't talk shop with friends
reallife_social_topic_shopgood_ra: Look at you! I always said you had a head for it. I'm proud of you.
reallife_social_topic_shopgood_rb: All right, keep your secrets. I was only being nice.
reallife_social_topic_shopbad_1: How's {shop}? You sounded tired last time.
reallife_social_topic_shopbad_ra: Ouch. Thanks for telling me. Every business has days like that. It'll turn.
reallife_social_topic_shopbad_rb: If you say so. You know you can tell me when it isn't.
reallife_social_topic_work_1: Were you working today? You've got that look about you, even on the phone.
reallife_social_topic_work_2: I heard you've been picking up shifts. How was it?
reallife_social_topic_work_ra: Honest money. Put your feet up tonight, you've earned it.
reallife_social_topic_work_rb: That good? Then I won't. Next subject!
reallife_social_topic_goodday_1: I've had the best day. Everything just went right for once.
reallife_social_topic_goodday_2: Guess who got good news today? Me. It was me.
reallife_social_topic_goodday_3: I'm in such a good mood. Even the subway was on time.
reallife_social_topic_goodday_ra: I knew you'd want to hear it. That's why I like telling you things.
reallife_social_topic_goodday_rb: Oh. Well. I'll keep it to myself, then.
reallife_social_topic_badday_1: Honestly? Today was awful. Everything that could go wrong did.
reallife_social_topic_badday_2: I'm having a rotten day. The rent, the bills, all of it at once.
reallife_social_topic_badday_3: Don't ask how I am. Or do. It's been one of those days.
reallife_social_topic_badday_ra: Thanks. I didn't need it fixed. I just needed somebody to hear it.
reallife_social_topic_badday_rb: Right. Thanks for that. Very helpful.
reallife_social_topic_theirjob_1: Work is work. Did I ever tell you what it's really like being {job}?
reallife_social_topic_theirjob_2: You would not believe what happened at work. Being {job} is never dull.
reallife_social_topic_theirjob_ra: Nobody ever asks! Right, so... and that's the short version.
reallife_social_topic_theirjob_rb: Fine. Your loss. It was a good story.
reallife_social_topic_rain_1: Is it raining where you are? It's coming down in sheets here.
reallife_social_topic_rain_2: This rain! I got soaked just crossing the street.
reallife_social_topic_rain_b: A bit of rain never hurt
reallife_social_topic_rain_ra: That's the plan. Blanket, tea, and I'm not moving.
reallife_social_topic_rain_rb: Says the one who's indoors. Come and stand in it with me.
reallife_social_topic_fine_1: It's a lovely day out. It seems a waste to be inside.
reallife_social_topic_fine_2: Have you looked outside? The city almost looks pretty today.
reallife_social_topic_fine_a: We should get out in it
reallife_social_topic_fine_ra: We should! Say the word and I'll put my shoes on.
reallife_social_topic_fine_rb: Such a cynic. I'm going to enjoy it anyway.
reallife_social_topic_memory_1: I was thinking about the other day. You know: {outing}. That was good.
reallife_social_topic_memory_2: Remember: {outing}. I keep smiling about that.
reallife_social_topic_memory_ra: Yes! Soon. You pick the day.
reallife_social_topic_memory_rb: All right? I thought it was more than all right. Never mind.
reallife_social_topic_birthday_1: It's my birthday soon, you know. Days to go: {days}. I'm only mentioning it.
reallife_social_topic_birthday_2: Days until I'm a year older: {days}. Not that I'm counting.
reallife_social_topic_birthday_ra: Good. A call on the day would be plenty. But a call.
reallife_social_topic_birthday_rb: Yes, already. Write it down this time.
reallife_social_topic_rich_1: You're doing well for yourself these days, aren't you? People have noticed.
reallife_social_topic_rich_2: Look at you, moving up in the world. What's it like?
reallife_social_topic_rich_b: It's every bit as good as it looks
reallife_social_topic_rich_ra: I know you are. That's the only reason I can stand it.
reallife_social_topic_rich_rb: Hm. Don't forget who knew you before, that's all.
reallife_social_topic_sick_1: You sound dreadful. Are you ill?
reallife_social_topic_sick_2: Is that a cough? You're not looking after yourself.
reallife_social_topic_sick_ra: Good. Do it today, not when it's worse. And drink something hot.
reallife_social_topic_sick_rb: That's what everybody says. Rest, at least. Promise me.
reallife_social_topic_breakin_1: I heard about the break-in at {shop}. That's awful. Did they take much?
reallife_social_topic_breakin_2: Somebody broke into {shop}? I'm so sorry. You must be furious.
reallife_social_topic_breakin_ra: That's the spirit. If you need a hand clearing up, I'm there.
reallife_social_topic_breakin_rb: Get two. And a camera. And a very large dog.
reallife_social_topic_knocked_1: Somebody said you were knocked down in the road! Are you hurt?
reallife_social_topic_knocked_2: Is it true a car hit you? You can't keep doing this to me.
reallife_social_topic_knocked_ra: Thank goodness. Look both ways. I'm being serious.
reallife_social_topic_knocked_rb: You're impossible. Take it easy for a day or two, at least.
reallife_social_topic_district_1: It's been noisy round {district} this week. They're digging the road up again.
reallife_social_topic_district_2: You should come over to {district} some time. It's changed since you last saw it.
reallife_social_topic_district_ra: Then come! I'll show you the good bits and hide the rest.
reallife_social_topic_district_rb: Big words. We'll compare notes one day.
reallife_social_topic_quiet_1: Nothing much to report, to be honest. Quiet week. You?
reallife_social_topic_quiet_2: Same old, same old. Tell me something interesting.
reallife_social_topic_quiet_3: I've got no news at all. I just like hearing from you.
reallife_social_topic_quiet_ra: It is, isn't it? I'll take a boring week over an eventful one.
reallife_social_topic_quiet_rb: Two dull people on the phone. We should do something about that.
reallife_social_greet_acq_1: Hi! You found it. I wasn't sure you'd come.
reallife_social_greet_acq_2: Hello again. It's good to see you outside of... well, wherever we met.
reallife_social_greet_acq_3: Hey! Right on time. I only just got here myself.
reallife_social_greet_friend_1: There you are! I've been looking forward to this all day.
reallife_social_greet_friend_2: Hey, you. You look well. Come on, let's do this.
reallife_social_greet_friend_3: You made it! I saved us a spot. Well, I stood on one.
reallife_social_greet_close_1: Come here, you. It's been too long.
reallife_social_greet_close_2: Finally! I've got so much to tell you.
reallife_social_greet_close_3: Look who it is. My favourite bad influence.
reallife_social_greet_love_2: There you are. I've been counting the minutes.
reallife_social_greet_love_3: Hey, you. I missed you today.
reallife_social_greet_late_1: You're late. I was about to give up and go home.
reallife_social_greet_late_2: Oh, there you are. I've been standing here long enough to know this pavement personally.
reallife_social_greet_late_3: I've been waiting ages. A text would have been nice.
reallife_social_greet_late_easy_1: You're late! Good. That makes two of us, I only just got here.
reallife_social_greet_late_easy_2: Don't apologise, I'm never on time either. Come on.
reallife_social_they_late_1: Sorry, sorry! The subway sat in a tunnel for ten minutes. Have you been waiting long?
reallife_social_they_late_2: I know, I'm late. I couldn't find my keys. Forgive me?
reallife_social_they_late_3: Sorry! I left on time, I swear. The city had other ideas.
reallife_social_part_1: This was good. Let's not leave it so long next time.
reallife_social_part_2: Right, I'd better head off. Thanks for today.
reallife_social_part_3: I needed that. Get home safe!
reallife_social_part_4: Same again soon? Good. See you!
reallife_social_part_love_1: I'll call you tonight. Go on, before I change my mind and keep you.
reallife_social_part_love_2: Today was perfect. See you soon, love.
reallife_social_after_bad_1: Well. That could have gone better. Another time, maybe.
reallife_social_after_bad_2: I think I'll call it a day. No hard feelings.
reallife_social_after_bad_3: Not our best outing, was it? Never mind.
reallife_social_after_coffee_1: That hit the spot. They do know how to make a coffee at {place}.
reallife_social_after_coffee_2: Nothing beats a coffee out in the fresh air. Thanks for this.
reallife_social_after_coffee_3: I feel human again. Good coffee, good company.
reallife_social_after_meal_1: I'm stuffed. That was exactly what I wanted.
reallife_social_after_meal_2: Good food, and you didn't steal my fries. A perfect meal.
reallife_social_after_meal_3: I won't need to eat until Thursday. That was great.
reallife_social_after_drinks_1: What a night! My ears are still ringing.
reallife_social_after_drinks_2: I haven't danced like that in years. Don't tell anyone.
reallife_social_after_drinks_3: That was a proper night out. I'll regret it in the morning and I don't care.
reallife_social_after_cinema_1: I did not see that ending coming. Did you?
reallife_social_after_cinema_2: Great film. You jumped at the loud bit, I saw you.
reallife_social_after_cinema_3: I could watch that again tomorrow. Thanks for coming with me.
reallife_social_after_walk_1: I needed that. A walk fixes most things.
reallife_social_after_walk_2: My feet say stop but my head feels clear. Thank you.
reallife_social_after_walk_3: We should do this more often. It costs nothing and I feel better.
reallife_social_after_drive_1: That was lovely. You see the city differently through a windscreen.
reallife_social_after_drive_2: Smooth driving! I nearly fell asleep, and I mean that as a compliment.
reallife_social_after_drive_3: Thanks for the ride. Next time I'm choosing the music.
reallife_social_after_workout_1: Good session! You kept up better than I expected.
reallife_social_after_workout_2: I'll feel that tomorrow. Worth it.
reallife_social_after_workout_3: That's the best I've trained in weeks. You're a good gym partner.
reallife_social_after_business_1: So this is what you've built. I'm impressed. Really.
reallife_social_after_business_2: You did all this? It's a proper business. Look at you.
reallife_social_after_business_3: I like it. It feels like you. Thank you for showing me.
reallife_social_after_lift_1: You're a star. I'd never have made it without you. Here, for the petrol.
reallife_social_after_lift_2: Door to door! Thank you. I owe you one, and here's something towards the fuel.
reallife_social_after_lift_3: That saved my day. Thanks. Take this for your trouble.
reallife_social_after_moving_1: That's the lot! I couldn't have done it alone. Pizza's on me.
reallife_social_after_moving_2: All done. You're a true friend. Take this and get yourself something to eat.
reallife_social_after_moving_3: Last box! Thank you, thank you. I'll remember this.
reallife_social_closed_1: Oh no, {place} is shut. Never mind. Let's just walk instead.
reallife_social_closed_2: Closed! Typical. Come on, a walk will do us just as much good.
reallife_social_pay_ask: Shall we? It'll come to about {cost} for the two of us, {half} each.
reallife_social_pay_ask_offer: Shall we go in? About {cost} for both. Let me get this one.
reallife_social_pay_covered: You've not got it on you? Don't worry, I'll cover it. You get the next one.
reallife_social_walk_talk_1: {first}: "I never notice this street when I'm rushing. It's nice."
reallife_social_walk_talk_2: {first}: "Can I tell you something? I've been thinking about changing jobs."
reallife_social_walk_talk_3: {first}: "You walk fast. Are we late for something?"
reallife_social_walk_talk_4: {first}: "I love this time of day. Everybody's going somewhere."
reallife_social_walk_talk_5: {first}: "This is better than sitting indoors. Good idea."
reallife_social_walk_behind_2: {first}: "Where are you going? I thought we were walking together."
reallife_social_left_1: {first} has given up and gone home. "I suppose you had somewhere better to be."
reallife_social_left_2: {first} waited, then left. "Call me when you've got time for me."
reallife_social_ride_talk_1: {first}: "I never get driven anywhere. This is the life."
reallife_social_ride_talk_2: {first}: "Turn here! No, go on, you choose."
reallife_social_ride_talk_3: {first}: "The city looks smaller from a car, doesn't it?"
reallife_social_ride_talk_4: {first}: "You drive better than I thought you would."
reallife_social_ride_jolt_2: {first}: "I'd like to arrive in one piece, please."
reallife_social_ride_jolt_3: {first}: "That was my coffee. It's on your seat now."
reallife_social_ride_crash_1: {first}: "What was that? Are you trying to kill us both?"
reallife_social_ride_crash_2: {first}: "That's it. I'm never getting in a car with you again."
reallife_social_moving_talk_1: {first}: "Mind your back! That one's all books."
reallife_social_moving_talk_2: {first}: "Just there is fine. You're a machine."
reallife_social_moving_talk_3: {first}: "One more like that and I'll buy you two pizzas."
reallife_social_moving_nothing: {first}: "There's no room to put anything down out here. Forget the boxes, I'll get a van. Thanks for coming, though."
reallife_social_meet_coming: Somebody is walking up to you
reallife_social_dropby_coming: {first} has spotted you and is coming over
reallife_social_intro_coming: {first} is coming over, and has brought somebody
reallife_social_meet_gym_1: Hey! You were in the gym just now, weren't you? You've got good form. I'm {first}.
reallife_social_meet_gym_2: Sorry to chase you down the street. I see you training in there all the time. I'm {first}.
reallife_social_meet_work_1: Hey, you were on shift today too, right? I'm {first}. I thought I'd say hello while we're both standing still.
reallife_social_meet_work_2: You work round here as well, don't you? I've seen you at it. {first}. Good to finally meet you.
reallife_social_meet_cart_1: You again! We keep ending up at that coffee cart at the same time. I'm {first}.
reallife_social_meet_cart_2: I know that face. The cart, most mornings. I thought I should introduce myself: {first}.
reallife_social_meet_neighbour_1: Hello! I think we're neighbours. I've seen you coming and going. I'm {first}, from along the hall.
reallife_social_meet_neighbour_2: Excuse me, you live in my building, don't you? I'm {first}. I thought it was time I said hello.
reallife_social_meet_helped_1: Wait! You're the one who stepped in back there. I wanted to say thank you properly. I'm {first}.
reallife_social_meet_helped_2: Hey! I've been looking for you. What you did earlier, most people would have walked past. I'm {first}.
reallife_social_meet_customer_1: It is you! You own the shop, don't you? I'm in there all the time. I'm {first}.
reallife_social_meet_customer_2: Sorry to bother you. I shop at your place most weeks and I never see the owner. I'm {first}.
reallife_social_meet_warm_1: Likewise! I'm {job}, I live over in {district}. We should grab a coffee some time.
reallife_social_meet_warm_2: You're friendlier than most people in this city. I'm {job}, by the way. {district} born and bred.
reallife_social_meet_warm_3: I had a feeling you'd be nice. I'm {job}, for my sins. I'm usually around {district}.
reallife_social_meet_cool_1: Not a talker. That's fine. I'm {job}, if you ever wonder. Anyway.
reallife_social_meet_cool_2: Right. Well. I'm {job}, I live in {district}. I just thought I'd say hello.
reallife_social_meet_numbers_1: Great, I've got you. I'll text so you have mine. See you around!
reallife_social_meet_numbers_2: Done. Now you can't say you don't know anyone. Take care!
reallife_social_meet_brushed_1: They shrug and walk away. "Suit yourself."
reallife_social_meet_brushed_2: "All right, all right. Only being friendly." They leave you to it.
reallife_social_meet_gaveup_1: Whoever it was gave up and walked on.
reallife_social_meet_gaveup_2: They waited a moment, thought better of it and left.
reallife_social_meet_no_numbers: You said goodbye without swapping numbers. Maybe you will run into them again.
reallife_social_intro_1: There you are! This is {name}, the friend I told you about. {first}, this is the one I keep going on about.
reallife_social_intro_2: Perfect timing. I want you to meet {name}. You two will get on, I can tell.
reallife_social_intro_3: Hey! Come and meet {name}. I've been meaning to put you two in the same place for weeks.
reallife_social_intro_hello: Hi! I'm {first}. I've heard a lot about you. Mostly good.
reallife_social_dropby_good_1: I was passing and thought I'd see how {shop} is doing. It looks busy in there!
reallife_social_dropby_good_2: So this is {shop}. People were queueing when I walked past. You must be raking it in.
reallife_social_dropby_quiet_1: I thought I'd come and see {shop} for myself. Quiet today, is it? It'll pick up.
reallife_social_dropby_quiet_2: I was in the area, so here I am. So this is {shop}. I like it.
reallife_social_dropby_street_1: I saw you from across the road. What are you up to out here?
reallife_social_dropby_street_2: Of all the streets in this city! I was just on my way home.
reallife_social_obj_early: You are early: {first} will be here about {time}
reallife_social_obj_park: Park up and walk over to {first}
reallife_social_obj_bring_car: Bring your car round: {first} is waiting
reallife_social_obj_no_room: No room for {first} to reach a door: move the car a little
reallife_social_obj_no_room_out: No room for {first} to get out here: move up a little
reallife_social_cut_short: Your time with {name} was cut short. No harm done.
reallife_social_cut_short_left: You left {name} standing there. They will remember that.
reallife_transaction_social_moving: A thank-you for helping with a move
reallife_social_invite_coffee: Coffee some time soon? I'm buying if you say yes quickly. Call me!
reallife_social_invite_meal: I'm hungry and I hate eating alone. Dinner? Ring me and we'll pick a time.
reallife_social_invite_drinks: It's been a week. I need a night out. Are you in? Call me.
reallife_social_invite_cinema: There's a film on I want to see and nobody to see it with. Call me?
reallife_social_invite_walk: Fancy a walk one of these days? Nothing fancy. Give me a ring.
reallife_social_invite_drive: Take me out for a drive some time? I never get out of this neighbourhood. Call me.
reallife_social_invite_workout: Gym this week? I need somebody to stop me skipping it. Call me and we'll fix a time.
reallife_social_invite_business: When do I get the tour of your business? I keep hearing about it. Ring me.
reallife_social_invite_lift: Any chance of a lift? Call me if you can.
reallife_social_invite_moving: I've got some boxes to shift. Call me if you've got an hour.
reallife_social_text_news_1: Just saw a dog on the subway wearing a raincoat. Thought you should know.
reallife_social_text_news_2: Long day. The coffee machine at work broke and nobody survived.
reallife_social_text_news_3: My landlord finally fixed the heating! Only took him a month.
reallife_social_text_news_4: I walked past a place that smelled like fresh bread and nearly cried. How's your day?
reallife_social_text_news_5: Guess who got a parking ticket this morning. Don't laugh.
reallife_social_text_news_6: I've decided to learn to cook. Wish my smoke alarm luck.
reallife_social_text_news_7: Work let us go early today. I don't know what to do with myself.
reallife_social_text_news_8: The lift in my building is stuck again. Seven floors. I'm counting it as exercise.
reallife_social_text_news_9: Somebody on my street is learning the trumpet. Pray for me.
reallife_social_text_news_10: Found twenty dollars in an old coat. Today is a good day.
reallife_social_text_news_11: It's {first}. Nothing to report, I just hadn't said hello in a while. Hello!
reallife_social_text_news_12: My boss said "good job" today. I'm having it framed.
reallife_social_text_badday_1: Rough day. Don't mind me. I just needed to tell somebody.
reallife_social_text_badday_2: Everything went wrong today. Tell me yours was better.
reallife_social_text_badday_3: Not my day. I'm going to bed early and starting again tomorrow.
reallife_social_text_cancel_1: I'm so sorry, I have to cancel. Work has kept me late. Can we do it another day? Call me.
reallife_social_text_cancel_2: Bad news: I can't make it. Something's come up at home. I'll make it up to you, call me.
reallife_social_text_cancel_3: I feel awful about this but I'm not going to make it today. Rain check? Ring me.
reallife_social_text_cancel_4: Don't hate me. I have to bail, my day has fallen apart. Call me and we'll rearrange.
reallife_social_text_cancel_rain_1: Have you seen the weather? I'm not walking in that. Another day? Call me.
reallife_social_text_cancel_rain_2: It's pouring. Let's not. Ring me when it's dry and we'll try again.
reallife_social_text_stoodup_1: I waited over an hour. You could at least have sent a message.
reallife_social_text_stoodup_2: So you're not coming. Good to know where I stand.
reallife_social_text_stoodup_3: I've gone home. I felt like an idiot standing there on my own.
reallife_social_text_stoodup_4: Is everything all right? You never showed up. I hope it was something serious, because I'm quite upset.
reallife_social_text_thanks_1: Home now. Thanks for today, I had a really good time.
reallife_social_text_thanks_2: That was fun. Let's do it again soon.
reallife_social_text_thanks_3: Still smiling. Thank you for today.
reallife_social_text_birthday_own_1: It's my birthday today! No pressure. (A little pressure.)
reallife_social_text_birthday_own_2: Guess what day it is. I'll give you a clue: there's cake. A call would be nice!
reallife_social_text_birthday_mom_1: Sweetheart, don't forget it's {name}'s birthday tomorrow. A call costs nothing.
reallife_social_text_birthday_mom_2: A little bird tells me {name} has a birthday tomorrow. I raised you to remember these things.
reallife_social_text_birthday_missed_1: It was my birthday yesterday. I suppose you were busy.
reallife_social_text_birthday_missed_2: Everyone called yesterday but you. It's fine. It's a bit not fine.
reallife_social_text_rich_kind_1: I hear business is booming. I'm so pleased for you. You've worked for it.
reallife_social_text_rich_kind_2: Look at you go! Don't forget us little people. Seriously though, well done.
reallife_social_text_rich_sour_1: Must be nice, having money to burn. Some of us are still counting coins.
reallife_social_text_rich_sour_2: I see you're doing very well for yourself. Don't go changing your number.
reallife_social_text_arrest_kind_1: I heard what happened. Are you okay? If you need anything, anything at all, call me.
reallife_social_text_arrest_kind_2: Whatever they say you did, I'm on your side. Ring me when you can.
reallife_social_text_arrest_stern_1: Arrested? Really? I don't know what to say to that.
reallife_social_text_arrest_stern_2: I heard about the police. I thought you were smarter than that.
reallife_social_text_arrest_mom_1: The police? I nearly dropped the phone. Call your mother this minute.
reallife_social_text_arrest_mom_2: I didn't raise you to see the inside of a cell. Are you eating? Call me.
reallife_social_text_crash_1: Somebody said you crashed on {street}. Tell me you're all right!
reallife_social_text_crash_2: I just heard about the accident on {street}. Are you hurt? Call me.
reallife_social_text_breakin_1: I just heard {shop} was broken into. I'm so sorry. Is there anything I can do?
reallife_social_text_breakin_2: A break-in at {shop}? That's horrible. Let me know you're okay.
reallife_social_text_missed_1: Tried to call you. Nothing urgent. Ring me back when you get a minute.
reallife_social_text_missed_2: You didn't pick up! Call me back, I've got something to ask you.
reallife_social_text_drift_1: Are you alive? It's been ages. Call me.
reallife_social_text_drift_2: I feel like I haven't heard from you in forever. Everything okay?
reallife_social_text_drift_3: Remember me? Your friend {first}? Pick up the phone some time.
reallife_social_text_loan_back_1: I've sent you the {amount} I owed. Thanks again for bailing me out.
reallife_social_text_loan_back_2: {amount}, back where it belongs. You're a good friend.
reallife_social_text_loan_excuse_1: About the {amount}. I haven't got it yet. A few more days, I promise.
reallife_social_text_loan_excuse_2: I know I owe you {amount}. Things are tight. Bear with me a bit longer?
reallife_social_text_debt_1: Hi. About the {amount} you borrowed. It's been a while now.
reallife_social_text_debt_2: I don't like to nag, but I do need that {amount} back.
reallife_social_text_home_1: I'll be home before you. Shall I put something on for dinner?
reallife_social_text_home_2: The flat feels empty without you in it. Come home soon.
reallife_social_text_home_3: We're out of milk. Also I love you. Mostly the milk, though.
reallife_social_text_love_1: Thinking about you. That's all. Carry on.
reallife_social_text_love_2: I saw something today that reminded me of you and now I can't stop smiling.
reallife_social_text_love_3: Hello, you. I hope today is being kind to you. Call me later?
reallife_social_text_breakup_1: I can't do this any more. We want different things, and I'm tired of waiting for you. I'm sorry.
reallife_social_text_breakup_2: This isn't working. You know it and I know it. Take care of yourself.
reallife_social_text_intro_1: You have to meet my friend {other}. Next time I catch you out on the street I'm bringing them over.
reallife_social_text_intro_2: I've told {other} all about you. You two should meet. I'll find you when you're out and about.
reallife_social_text_lift_1: I'm stranded. Any chance of a lift across town? Call me if you can come.
reallife_social_text_lift_2: My ride fell through. Could you drive me somewhere? Ring me, I'm outside now.
reallife_social_text_loan_1: Can I ask you something awkward? Call me when you've got a second.
reallife_social_text_loan_2: I need a small favour. A money one. Ring me?
reallife_social_text_moving_1: I'm moving a few boxes to my new place and I could use another pair of arms. Call me?
reallife_social_text_moving_2: Moving day is coming and I've nobody to help carry. I'll pay you in pizza. Ring me.
reallife_news_none: No paper has come yet. The City Ledger arrives every morning after 06:00.
reallife_news_end: That is all the news for today.

reallife_news_accident_minor_3: Low-speed bump on {street}: police attended a minor collision at {time}. No injuries were reported.

reallife_news_accident_moderate_2: Traffic on {street} stood still for some time after a crash around {time}. Paramedics saw to the injured before the road reopened.
reallife_news_accident_moderate_3: Police taped off part of {street} at {time} after a collision. One driver was taken away for a check-up.

reallife_news_accident_severe_2: {street} was closed for much of the hour after a severe crash around {time}. Witnesses spoke of wreckage across both lanes.
reallife_news_accident_severe_3: A violent collision on {street} at {time} left a vehicle wrecked and a casualty in the care of paramedics. Police are asking witnesses to come forward.

reallife_news_ped_hurt_2: A pedestrian was knocked down on {street} around {time}. They were conscious when the ambulance arrived.
reallife_news_ped_killed_1: FATAL COLLISION ON {street}. A pedestrian died after being struck by a vehicle on {street} at about {time}. The road was closed while officers examined the scene.
reallife_news_ped_killed_2: A person on foot was killed on {street} around {time}. Police have appealed for anyone who saw the collision.
reallife_news_hitrun_1: HIT AND RUN. A driver fled the scene of a collision on {street} at about {time}, with a patrol car in pursuit.
reallife_news_hitrun_2: Police gave chase after a motorist drove away from a crash on {street} around {time}.
reallife_news_crime_1: Police were called to {what} on {street} at about {time}.
reallife_news_crime_2: Residents of {street} reported {what} around {time}. Officers attended.
reallife_news_crime_3: {street}, {time}: {what}. "You don't expect it on your own street," said one passer-by.
reallife_news_arrest_1: ARREST ON {street}. Officers made an arrest at about {time} following {what}.
reallife_news_arrest_2: One person was taken into custody on {street} around {time} in connection with {what}.
reallife_news_arrest_3: A suspect was led away in handcuffs on {street} at {time} after {what}.

reallife_news_tally_2: The day's count: collisions {accidents}, arrests {arrests}, other incidents {crimes}.
reallife_news_quiet_1: A QUIET DAY. Police report no incidents of note since yesterday's edition. Enjoy it while it lasts.
reallife_news_quiet_2: Nothing to report from the streets: no crashes, no arrests, no sirens. The desk sergeant is said to have finished a crossword.
reallife_news_quiet_3: For once, the news is that there is no news. The city behaved itself yesterday.
reallife_news_quiet_4: A calm day and night across the city. Our crime reporter went home early.
reallife_news_rain_now_1: WEATHER: Rain this morning. Take an umbrella, and take the corners gently.
reallife_news_rain_now_2: WEATHER: Wet streets and grey skies to start the day. It should pass.
reallife_news_rained_1: WEATHER: Dry this morning after yesterday's rain. Mind the puddles.
reallife_news_rained_2: WEATHER: The rain has moved on. A brighter day is expected.
reallife_news_dry_1: WEATHER: Dry and settled. A good day to be out.
reallife_news_dry_2: WEATHER: No rain in sight. Clear skies over the city this morning.
reallife_news_dry_3: WEATHER: Fine and dry again. The umbrella sellers are not pleased.
reallife_news_shop_good_1: BUSINESS: {shop} on {street} took {amount} yesterday, a good day by any measure.
reallife_news_shop_good_2: BUSINESS: Trade was brisk at {shop}, {street}, where the tills rang up {amount} in a day.
reallife_news_shop_good_3: BUSINESS: One to watch: {shop} on {street} reports takings of {amount} for the day.
reallife_news_shop_loss_1: BUSINESS: A hard day for {shop} on {street}, which ended {amount} out of pocket.
reallife_news_shop_loss_2: BUSINESS: {shop}, {street}, lost {amount} on the day. Its owner will hope for better.
reallife_news_shop_none_1: BUSINESS: Shop rents held steady this week. Agents say good corners are still hard to find.
reallife_news_shop_none_2: BUSINESS: Wholesalers report steady demand. Small shopkeepers say the margins are as thin as ever.
reallife_news_shop_none_3: BUSINESS: Empty units are filling up downtown. "Somebody always thinks they can make it work," says one landlord.
reallife_news_breakin_1: BREAK-IN AT {shop}. Thieves forced their way into {shop} overnight. The damage is put at {amount}.
reallife_news_breakin_2: {shop} was broken into during the night. The repairs alone will cost {amount}, its owner says.
reallife_news_carbreakin_1: A parked car was broken into on {street} overnight. Police advise leaving nothing on the seats.
reallife_news_carbreakin_2: Car crime: a vehicle left on {street} was found with a window smashed in the morning.
reallife_news_playercrash_1: A motorist came to grief on {street} at about {time}. The vehicle looked the worse for it.
reallife_news_playercrash_2: One driver's day ended early on {street} around {time}, after an argument with something solid.
reallife_news_playerarrest_1: A local resident was taken into custody on {street} at about {time}. Police would not say more.
reallife_news_playerarrest_2: Police detained a member of the public on {street} around {time}, who then spent some hours as their guest.
reallife_news_playerknocked_1: A pedestrian was struck by a passing vehicle on {street} at about {time} and, by all accounts, got up again.
reallife_news_playerknocked_2: Traffic on {street} knocked a person off their feet around {time}. They are said to be recovering.
reallife_news_person_birthday_1: PEOPLE: Many happy returns to {name}, {job} from {district}, who has a birthday today.
reallife_news_person_birthday_2: PEOPLE: {name} of {district} is a year older today. Cards may be sent to the usual address.
reallife_news_person_job_1: PEOPLE: Our "faces of the city" column this week: {name}, {job}, who says {district} is the only place to live.
reallife_news_person_job_2: PEOPLE: Asked what the city needs, {name}, {job} from {district}, said: "Fewer car horns. More benches."
reallife_news_person_job_3: PEOPLE: {name}, {job}, tells us business is "the same as ever, which is to say busy".
reallife_news_person_seen_1: PEOPLE: Spotted about town yesterday: {name} of {district}, in good company.
reallife_news_person_seen_2: PEOPLE: {name}, {job} from {district}, was seen enjoying a day out. We approve.
reallife_news_noun_parking_ticket: a dispute over a parking ticket
reallife_news_filler_1: The pigeons of the financial district have learned to recognise lunch hour, a study of nobody in particular has found.
reallife_news_filler_2: A reader writes to ask why the hot-dog cart on his corner is never there when he is hungry. We have no answer.
reallife_news_filler_3: ON THIS DAY: nothing in particular happened, as far as our archive can tell.
reallife_news_filler_4: The city's oldest lift attendant retires this week after forty-one years. "It had its ups and downs," he said.
reallife_news_filler_5: LETTERS: "Sir, the benches in the park face the wrong way. I have said so before."
reallife_news_filler_6: A lost umbrella was handed in at our front desk. The owner may claim it by describing the handle.
reallife_news_filler_7: The subway authority promises the trains will run on time this week. We will let you know.
reallife_news_filler_8: RECIPE OF THE DAY: toast. Bread, heat, butter. Do not overthink it.
reallife_news_filler_9: A street musician on the avenue was asked to move on, then asked to come back. The crowd had followed him.
reallife_news_filler_10: HOROSCOPE: Today favours those who look both ways. Tomorrow also.
reallife_news_filler_11: The mayor's office denies that the new traffic lights are slower than the old ones. Drivers remain unconvinced.
reallife_news_filler_12: CLASSIFIED: For sale, one exercise bike, hardly used. Buyer collects. Seller will hold the door.
reallife_news_filler_13: A coffee cart on the east side claims the strongest cup in the city. Our reporter has not slept since.
reallife_news_filler_14: The annual count of city squirrels has been abandoned again. They would not stand still.
reallife_news_filler_15: LETTERS: "Madam, when I was young a sandwich cost a quarter. I do not know what else to tell you."
reallife_news_filler_16: A window cleaner on the thirtieth floor says the view is wasted on the people inside.
reallife_news_filler_17: CROSSWORD CLUE, 7 across: "What everybody is, in this city" (4). Answer tomorrow.
reallife_news_filler_18: The corner kiosk reports that sales of maps are down and sales of umbrellas depend entirely on the sky.
reallife_news_filler_19: A man who has fed the same pigeon for nine years admits he cannot be sure it is the same pigeon.
reallife_news_filler_20: THE LEDGER ASKS: what is the best street in the city? Answers on a postcard. Our own will not be considered.
reallife_news_filler_21: Road crews say the hole on the avenue will be filled by the weekend. They did not say which weekend.
reallife_news_filler_22: A doorman of thirty years' standing shares his secret: "Remember names. Forget everything else."
reallife_news_filler_23: CLASSIFIED: Wanted, a quiet flat. Present neighbour learning the trumpet.
reallife_news_filler_24: The chess players in the square have been at the same game since Tuesday. Neither will say who is winning.
reallife_news_filler_25: HOROSCOPE: A stranger may speak to you today. Consider speaking back.
reallife_news_filler_26: The parks department reminds citizens that the flowers are for looking at.
reallife_news_filler_27: LETTERS: "Sir, I was nearly run down on a crossing by a man eating a sandwich. Both hands."
reallife_news_filler_28: A cab driver claims to know every street in the city. Asked for the shortest route, he said: "There isn't one."
reallife_news_filler_29: The bakery on the corner sold out by nine again. The owner refuses to bake more, on principle.
reallife_news_filler_30: ON THIS DAY, some years ago, a reader found a parking space on the first attempt. A plaque is planned.
reallife_news_filler_31: A sweeper on the west side says the street is cleanest at six in the morning and it is all downhill from there.
reallife_news_filler_32: CLASSIFIED: Lost, one glove, left hand, sentimental value. Right hand lonely.
reallife_news_filler_33: The library reports that the most borrowed book this month is the one about getting rich. It is overdue.
reallife_news_filler_34: A florist says business rises sharply the day after a row. "I ask no questions," she adds.
reallife_news_filler_35: HOROSCOPE: Money comes and goes today. Mostly goes.
reallife_news_filler_36: The gym on the avenue reports its busiest week of the year. It expects to be quiet again by the next.
reallife_news_filler_37: LETTERS: "Madam, your weather forecast was wrong again. I enclose my wet hat."
reallife_news_filler_38: A courier claims a record: eleven floors, no lift, one parcel, under two minutes. The parcel was a pillow.
reallife_news_filler_39: The city's taxi drivers have voted, by a narrow margin, that the best time to drive is when nobody else is.
reallife_news_filler_40: THOUGHT FOR THE DAY: call somebody you have not spoken to in a while. They may be wondering.

reallife_travel_day_hamptons_1: Saturday at the cottage. The tide is out, the gulls are loud, and nobody knows where you are.
reallife_travel_day_hamptons_2: Sunday. Fog on the dunes first thing, burning off by ten. One more day before the city.
reallife_travel_day_cruise_1: First day at sea. The coast slides by to port; the deck chairs are filling up.
reallife_travel_day_cruise_2: The ship anchors off a harbour town. Launches run to the quay every half hour.
reallife_travel_day_cruise_3: Last day aboard. The captain's dinner is tonight, and the casino deck never closed.
reallife_travel_day_ski_1: First morning. Fresh snow overnight, blue sky, the lifts already humming.
reallife_travel_day_ski_2: Your legs remember yesterday. The mountain doesn't care; the top runs are open.
reallife_travel_day_ski_3: Cloud in the valley, sun above it. From the summit the world is a white sea with islands.
reallife_travel_day_ski_4: Last day. The snow is soft by noon and the terrace bars are doing good business.
reallife_travel_day_miami_1: First morning. The beach is thirty steps from the lobby and the sea is the colour of a swimming pool.
reallife_travel_day_miami_2: Already hot at nine. Pastel hotels, palm shadows, somebody's radio playing salsa.
reallife_travel_day_miami_3: Midweek. You have stopped checking your phone before breakfast.
reallife_travel_day_miami_4: A breeze off the water today. Kites up, pelicans working the shallows.
reallife_travel_day_miami_5: Last full day. The city back home feels like something you read about.
reallife_travel_day_europe_1: London, grey and enormous. Jet-lagged, you are on the pavement by seven with a paper cup of tea.
reallife_travel_day_europe_2: London still. Rain on and off; every second building has a plaque on it.
reallife_travel_day_europe_3: The train under the sea, and Paris at the other end: wide boulevards, tiny coffees.
reallife_travel_day_europe_4: Paris. The light on the river in the morning is the kind people paint.
reallife_travel_day_europe_5: South through the mountains to Florence. Terracotta roofs, bells, scooters.
reallife_travel_day_europe_6: On to Rome. Ruins in the middle of the traffic as if that were normal.
reallife_travel_day_europe_7: Last day in Rome. You throw the coin in the fountain like everybody else.
reallife_travel_day_tradefair_1: Day one. A hall the size of an airfield, a thousand stands, and a floor plan you can't fold back up.
reallife_travel_day_tradefair_2: Day two. Your feet hurt, your bag is full of brochures, and the good conversations happen in the coffee queue.
reallife_travel_ev_relax_1: A whole afternoon in a chair with a book you'd been meaning to read for a year.
reallife_travel_ev_relax_2: You fall asleep after lunch and wake up with no idea what day it is. Perfect.
reallife_travel_ev_relax_3: A long, slow breakfast that turns into lunch.
reallife_travel_ev_relax_4: You do nothing so thoroughly that you surprise yourself.
reallife_travel_ev_relax_5: You try to relax and catch yourself doing sums about work in your head. It takes most of the day to stop.
reallife_travel_ev_relax_6: A massage from somebody who clearly knows where shoulders keep their secrets.
reallife_travel_ev_relax_7: You order one drink with a little umbrella in it, then another. The bill has umbrellas on it too.
reallife_travel_ev_relax_8: An hour watching the light change. You can't remember when you last watched anything that slow.
reallife_travel_ev_relax_9: You stay out in the sun too long and spend the evening the colour of a lobster.
reallife_travel_ev_relax_10: A stranger at the next table tells you their life story. It's a good one.
reallife_travel_ev_relax_11: You sleep nine hours and wake up before the alarm you didn't set.
reallife_travel_ev_relax_12: For one whole day, nobody needs anything from you.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_1: You walk until the tourist streets run out and find where the locals actually eat.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_2: A wrong turn takes you up a hill to a view that isn't in any of the guidebooks.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_3: A market stall, an old man who won't haggle, and something small and handmade that had to come home with you.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_4: Somewhere in a crowd a hand finds your pocket. You notice an hour later.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_5: You pay for a guided tour. The guide is funnier than the sights.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_6: You get thoroughly lost and walk twice as far as you meant to.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_7: You stumble into a street festival: music, food on sticks, children with sparklers.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_8: A little shop down three steps sells exactly the thing a friend of yours has always wanted.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_9: It pours. You shelter in a doorway for an hour and your shoes take two days to dry.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_10: You find a banknote on the pavement and nobody near to have dropped it.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_11: You rent a bicycle and remember, wobbling, that you can ride one.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_12: A taxi takes the long way round and the meter takes the liberty.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_13: You talk your way on to a rooftop for the sunset. Worth every stair.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_14: A museum with an entrance fee and, it turns out, one good room.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_15: A cat adopts you for the length of a street and then has other business.
reallife_travel_ev_explore_16: You find a bench with a view and eat lunch out of a paper bag like a local.
reallife_travel_ev_splurge_1: You walk out of a shop with a bag that has rope handles and tissue paper in it. No regrets.
reallife_travel_ev_splurge_2: The tasting menu: eleven courses, each the size of a thumbnail, each astonishing.
reallife_travel_ev_splurge_3: Presents for everyone back home. Your bag will barely close.
reallife_travel_ev_splurge_4: You tip like a film star and are treated like one for the rest of the evening. It adds up.
reallife_travel_ev_splurge_5: A day at the spa: you are steamed, scrubbed and wrapped like something precious.
reallife_travel_ev_splurge_6: The famous restaurant turns out to be famous mostly for being famous.
reallife_travel_ev_splurge_7: You buy the absurd hat, and something nearly as absurd for a friend.
reallife_travel_ev_splurge_8: A flutter at the tables after dinner, and for once the house loses.
reallife_travel_ev_splurge_9: You hire the convertible for the day. Sunglasses, radio, coast road.
reallife_travel_ev_splurge_10: The bar with the view charges for the view. Separately.
reallife_travel_ev_splurge_11: A shop that wraps everything beautifully. You buy things for the sake of the wrapping, and one for somebody at home.
reallife_travel_ev_splurge_12: Front-row seats for a show you will be telling people about for years.
reallife_travel_ev_companion_1: {name} makes you laugh so hard at dinner that the next table asks what the joke was.
reallife_travel_ev_companion_2: {name} gets you both hopelessly lost and insists it's a shortcut. It somehow is.
reallife_travel_ev_companion_3: You and {name} stay up talking until the bar closes around you.
reallife_travel_ev_companion_4: You and {name} have a stupid argument about a map. It's forgotten by lunch, mostly.
reallife_travel_ev_companion_5: {name} takes forty photographs of you looking at things. Two are good.
reallife_travel_ev_companion_6: {name} says, out of nowhere, that this is the best trip they have ever had.
reallife_travel_ev_companion_7: {name} dares you to try the local speciality. You dare them back.
reallife_travel_ev_companion_8: Walking back late, {name} takes your arm, and neither of you says anything for a while. It's a good quiet.
reallife_travel_ev_hamptons_1: A farm stand on the back road: corn, tomatoes and a pie still warm.
reallife_travel_ev_hamptons_2: The sunset over the bay goes on for an hour and you watch every minute of it.
reallife_travel_ev_hamptons_3: A village shop sells you a striped jumper at a price that suggests the stripes are gold.
reallife_travel_ev_hamptons_4: You fall asleep on the porch to the sound of the surf.
reallife_travel_ev_cruise_1: Dolphins off the bow before breakfast. Half the ship is at the rail in dressing gowns.
reallife_travel_ev_cruise_2: A night of heavy swell. You discover which of your organs can float.
reallife_travel_ev_cruise_3: You are invited to the captain's table and he turns out to be very funny.
reallife_travel_ev_cruise_4: Bingo night in the lounge. You shout at the right moment.
reallife_travel_ev_ski_1: One perfect run, top to bottom without stopping, the snow hissing under you.
reallife_travel_ev_ski_2: You catch an edge and slide thirty yards on your back, collecting snow down your collar.
reallife_travel_ev_ski_3: Hot chocolate on a sun terrace two thousand metres up.
reallife_travel_ev_ski_4: A lesson with an instructor who fixes in an hour what you'd been doing wrong for years.
reallife_travel_ev_miami_1: You swim out past the breakers at sunrise and have the whole ocean to yourself.
reallife_travel_ev_miami_2: An afternoon thunderstorm clears the beach in ninety seconds flat.
reallife_travel_ev_miami_3: A pavement cafe, a tiny strong coffee and a sandwich pressed flat. You go back for a second.
reallife_travel_ev_miami_4: You sleep on the sand with a hat over your face and nobody wakes you.
reallife_travel_ev_europe_1: You turn a corner and there is the thing from every postcard, bigger than you imagined and entirely real.
reallife_travel_ev_europe_2: You board the wrong train and pay a fine in a language you don't speak.
reallife_travel_ev_europe_3: A bookshop by the river with a cat on the till. You buy something small for a friend.
reallife_travel_ev_europe_4: You climb four hundred steps to the top of a dome and the whole city is laid out underneath.
reallife_travel_ev_tradefair_1: A supplier you've been chasing for months turns out to be standing next to you in the coffee queue.
reallife_travel_ev_tradefair_2: A keynote that runs an hour over. You learn one thing, in the last five minutes.
reallife_travel_ev_tradefair_3: The exhibitors' dinner costs extra. Everyone who matters is there.
reallife_travel_ev_tradefair_4: You see a competitor's whole product line laid out on a stand and take very careful notes.
reallife_travel_ev_rough_1: Somebody nearby snored like a chainsaw until dawn. You barely slept.
reallife_travel_ev_rough_2: A group came in at three in the morning, singing. They did not stop singing.
reallife_travel_ev_rough_3: You wake up itching. Bedbugs. You wash everything you own twice.
reallife_travel_ev_rough_4: The radiator clanked all night like a ghost with a wrench.
reallife_travel_ev_rough_5: Your bag was open when you woke. A little cash is gone.
reallife_travel_ev_rough_6: The mattress has a spring with a grudge. You found it with your back.
reallife_travel_ev_rough_7: A fire alarm at four. False, but nobody tells your heartbeat that.
reallife_travel_ev_rough_8: The couple through the wall argued until two and made up until four.
reallife_travel_ev_rough_9: The neon sign outside the window buzzed and flickered on your eyelids all night.
reallife_travel_ev_rough_10: Half the floor was up talking until late, and one of them told a story so good you didn't mind.
reallife_travel_ev_fine_1: A newspaper outside the door and a handwritten card wishing you a good morning.
reallife_travel_ev_fine_2: Fresh coffee and warm pastries are sent up without your asking.
reallife_travel_ev_fine_3: Housekeeping has left a chocolate on the pillow and turned the lamps down just so.
reallife_travel_ev_fine_4: The manager sends up a bowl of fruit and a note thanking you for staying.
reallife_travel_ev_fine_5: Your shoes, left outside the door on a whim, have come back polished like mirrors.
reallife_travel_ev_fine_6: The doorman remembers your name. It should not matter, and it does.
reallife_travel_ev_beach_1: A mile of empty sand and the sea talking to itself.
reallife_travel_ev_beach_2: You find a whole sand dollar at the tide line, and it comes home in your pocket.
reallife_travel_ev_beach_3: A seal watches you from the surf for a while, deciding about you.
reallife_travel_ev_beach_4: The wind gets up and you walk back leaning into it, sand in your teeth.
reallife_travel_ev_beach_5: A folded banknote in the dune grass, soft with salt.
reallife_travel_ev_beach_6: The sun goes down red over the water and you stay until the last of it.
reallife_travel_ev_beach_7: Somebody's dog decides you are its friend and brings you a stick the whole length of the beach.
reallife_travel_ev_beach_8: A wave you didn't see coming soaks you to the knees.
reallife_test_career_sign_on: Sign on with the next employer
reallife_test_career_shift: Work a shift at my rank, off the record
reallife_test_career_gig: Book a set at a nearby venue
reallife_contact_career_desc: Your employer, your rota and your CV
reallife_text_career_welcome: This is where work reaches you: shift reminders, letters from your employer, your rota and your CV. Employers hire in person, at the offices where the help-wanted boards stand. Call any time.
reallife_career_promo_pitch: Hi! Tasha, Brightline Promotions. We put paper in hands and smiles on faces, and we are always, always hiring. You'd start as a {title}: the flyer round you may know from the Gig Line, but on a rota, with {wage} an hour basic on top of what each flyer pays. Do well and you run a street team for me. {status}
reallife_career_promo_welcome: Love it! Welcome to Brightline. Your rota is {rota}. Clock on from your phone or right here, and bring the energy!
reallife_career_promo_review: Review time! Don't look so worried, I do these with a smile. Let's see how the streets have been treating you.
reallife_career_promo_notice: Oh, I'm sorry to lose you! Work {shifts} more shifts for me and you leave with my blessing and a proper reference.
reallife_career_promo_walkout: Just like that? Wow. Okay. I can't write anything nice about somebody who leaves me a team short. Bye.
reallife_career_cleaning_pitch: Dolores Whitlock. I run Brightside, and my floors are the cleanest in this city because I check every one. A {title} with us mops clients' floors, as on the Gig Line, but on a rota, with {wage} an hour basic on top of the pay per patch. The careful ones I make crew leads. {status}
reallife_career_cleaning_welcome: Good. Your rota is {rota}. Be on time, dear, and do the corners. I will know if you don't.
reallife_career_cleaning_review: Sit down, dear. I've been keeping notes, as I do for everybody. Let's go through them together.
reallife_career_cleaning_notice: I'm sorry to hear it, but thank you for telling me properly. {shifts} more shifts, done as well as the first, and I'll write you a reference I can stand behind.
reallife_career_cleaning_walkout: Mid-rota, with clients waiting? I'm disappointed. I write honest references, dear, and yours will be an honest one.
reallife_career_food_pitch: Lou! Everybody calls me Uncle Lou. I got carts all over town and not enough hands. You start as a {title}: my cart, my drinks, {wage} an hour basic and a wage for every customer you serve, tips are yours. Show me you can run a queue and I'll put you up for a licence: then you rent the cart by the day and what you take, you keep. Your first little business! {status}
reallife_career_food_welcome: Ha! Welcome to the family. Rota's {rota}. Smile at them, get the order right, and never, ever run out of lids.
reallife_career_food_review: Come here, come here, sit. I been watching the takings. Let's talk about how you been doing, eh?
reallife_career_food_notice: Ah, you're leaving your Uncle Lou. It happens. Give me {shifts} more shifts and I tell everybody in this town you're good people.
reallife_career_food_walkout: You walk off with the lunch rush coming? No, no, no. That I remember. Go on, get out of here.
reallife_career_retail_pitch: Good day. Anand Rao, area manager for Fairway Markets. We have a vacancy for a {title}: deliveries carried in from the kerb and shelved, on a fixed rota, at {wage} an hour basic in addition to the rate per box. There is a path from the stockroom to shift lead and to assistant manager for those who merit it; time at a shop till elsewhere is counted as experience. {status}
reallife_career_retail_welcome: Welcome to Fairway Markets. Your rota is {rota}. Punctuality is recorded, as is everything else. I trust we will not need to discuss it.
reallife_career_retail_review: Please, take a seat. This is your scheduled performance review. I have your figures in front of me.
reallife_career_retail_notice: Noted, with regret. Company policy is {shifts} further shifts. Complete them satisfactorily and a reference will be provided.
reallife_career_retail_walkout: That is a breach of your notice period. It will be recorded as such, and reflected in any reference we are asked for. Good day.
reallife_career_courier_pitch: Kowalski. I run this depot. I need a {title}: the parcel rounds you know, on a rota, {wage} an hour basic on top of the pay per door. Bring your own wheels or hire a van. Don't crash, don't get pulled over, don't be late. Seniors get the firm's van and the big rounds. After that there's the dispatch desk, and after that my job, if you live that long. {status}
reallife_career_courier_welcome: Fine. You're on. Rota's {rota}. Parcels don't deliver themselves and I don't chase people. Be here.
reallife_career_courier_review: Shut the door. Review. I don't do speeches, I do numbers. Here are yours.
reallife_career_courier_notice: Leaving. Right. {shifts} more shifts and I'll put my name to a reference. Miss one and I won't.
reallife_career_courier_walkout: With a van loaded? Get out. And don't put my name on anything.
reallife_career_cab_pitch: Sal DeMarco, Five Borough Cabs, talk fast because the meter's running. I take drivers with references, nobody else. {title}: four fares a shift off my dispatch, {wage} an hour basic on top of the fare, tips are yours. Keep them comfy, keep it clean, and I move you to the premium list: luxury car, picky riders, tips like you wouldn't believe. Top of the tree you're an owner-operator and most of the fare stays in your pocket. {status}
reallife_career_cab_welcome: Beautiful. Rota's {rota}. Smooth on the brakes, easy on the corners, and if the cops light you up it's on your file, not mine. Go, go.
reallife_career_cab_review: Sit, sit, two minutes, I got a radio going. Review. I got your sheet right here, let's go.
reallife_career_cab_notice: You're leaving me? Okay, okay, no hard feelings. {shifts} more shifts, clean, and Sal says nice things about you to anybody who calls.
reallife_career_cab_walkout: Now? With fares on the board? Unbelievable. You know what I tell people who call about you? Nothing good. Goodbye.
reallife_career_hire_ready: The job is yours if you want it.
reallife_career_no_off: Careers are switched off on the options page.
reallife_career_no_other: You are on the books at {value}. Work your notice there first.
reallife_career_no_banned: Not after how it ended last time. Days until you may ask again: {value}.
reallife_career_no_references: I can't take you on yet. Good references needed: {value}. A reference letter from gig work counts as one, and so does leaving an employer on good terms.
reallife_career_no_employer: You have no employer. Sign on at an office: look for the help-wanted boards.
reallife_career_rota_offer: Which rota suits you? I can offer {rota}: {time}. You can clock on from two hours before the start. From an hour after the start you are late, which is a mark against you, and three marks and we part company.
reallife_career_status: {employer}. You are our {title}, on {wage} an hour basic plus what the work pays. Rota: {rota}. Next shift: {next}. Marks against you: {marks} of {most}. {note}
reallife_career_note_review: Your performance review is due: come to the office for it.
reallife_career_note_review_here: Your performance review is due: we can do it now.
reallife_career_note_notice: You are working your notice. Shifts to go: {left}.
reallife_career_clocked_on: You're clocked on. Watch the top of your screen.
reallife_career_other_2: Anything else? Your CV, or something about a job?
reallife_career_sick_ok: Sorry to hear it. Stay home: today's shift is excused. No mark against you, and no pay.
reallife_career_sick_no: You sound fine to me. If a doctor has signed you off, that's different; otherwise I expect you on your shift.
reallife_career_sick_excused: {employer}: you were off sick, so the missed shift is excused. No mark, no pay.
reallife_career_no_shift_today: You have no shift left to work today.
reallife_career_too_early: Your shift is {time}. You can clock on from two hours before it starts, not sooner.
reallife_career_too_late: That shift has gone. It is down as a no-show.
reallife_career_at_depot: This work is done at the office. Come to the help-wanted board outside it and clock on there.
reallife_career_leaving_ask: Leaving? Give notice and work {shifts} more shifts, and you go with a reference if your record earns one. Walk out now and the reference is marked down, and you won't be taken back for {days} days.
reallife_career_on_notice: You are working your notice. Shifts left: {left}. After that you leave on good terms, or you can walk out now with a marked-down reference.
reallife_career_review_numbers: Since we last sat down, shifts worked: {shifts}. On time for {ontime} of {due}; late {late}, missed {missed}. Tips from customers: {tips}. Shifts that ended in a complaint: {complaints}. Crashes on the job: {crashes}. Police stops on the job: {stops}.
reallife_career_review_promoted: That comes to {score} out of 100, and that is promotion material. From your next shift you are our {title}, on {wage} an hour basic.
reallife_career_review_raise: {score} out of 100. Solid. There's a raise in it: {wage} an hour basic from now on.
reallife_career_review_steady: {score} out of 100. Steady. Nothing to add, nothing to take away. Keep turning up on time and the next one could go better.
reallife_career_review_warning: {score} out of 100, and that is not good enough. It goes down as a mark against you: {marks} of {most}. Turn it round before the next review.
reallife_career_review_dismissed: {score} out of 100, on top of what was already on your file. We are letting you go, and the reference will say why. Don't ask again for {days} days.
reallife_career_review_due: {boss} wants a word: your performance review at {employer} is due. Go to the office.
reallife_career_freelance: You are freelance: no employer, no rota. Employers take you on at their offices, where the help-wanted boards stand, or here on the phone. References to your name: {references}.
reallife_career_gig_offer: A venue wants live music out front today: a set of eight songs, {fee} from the venue on top of whatever lands in your case, and people tip better at a booked set. Want it?
reallife_career_gig_booked: Booked: {venue}. It is marked on your map. Walk up to the front of it and the set begins. {fee} from the venue if you play at least half of it.
reallife_career_gig_booked_toast: Booked set at {venue}: {fee} from the venue plus the hat. Walk up to its front to begin.
reallife_career_gig_none: Nothing I can book near where you are. Try from another part of town.
reallife_career_gig_pending: You already have a set booked at {venue} today. Go and play it.
reallife_career_gig_no_level: Venues want somebody who can hold a crowd. Get to busker level {level} on the street first.
reallife_career_gig_no_today: One booked set a day. Ask again tomorrow.
reallife_career_gig_missed: You never turned up for your booked set. The venue found somebody else.
reallife_career_cv_letter_no: not yet (level 2 in any gig earns one)
reallife_career_cv_record_stop: stopped by the police while on a job in the last two days.
reallife_career_reminder: Shift at {employer} today, {time} ({title}). Clock on from your phone (Work) or at the office.
reallife_career_text_reminder: Reminder: you are on the rota today, {time}, as {title}. Clock on by calling this number, or at the office. From an hour after the start you are late, which is a mark against you.
reallife_career_late: Late for your shift: an hour's basic pay docked, and a mark against you ({marks} of {most}).
reallife_career_noshow: You missed your shift at {employer}. {boss} has put a mark against you: {marks} of {most}.
reallife_career_text_noshow: {boss} here. You were on the rota and you did not show. That is mark {marks} of {most}. At {most} we are done.
reallife_career_dismissed_noshow: {employer} has let you go: three marks for lateness and missed shifts. {boss} has marked your reference down, and they will not take you back for {days} days.
reallife_career_dismissed_late: Late once too often. {employer} has let you go: three marks. {boss} has marked your reference down, and they will not take you back for {days} days.
reallife_career_text_dismissed: {boss}, {employer}. Your employment with us has ended. Your final pay has been made. Any reference we are asked for will reflect your record. Do not apply again within {days} days.
reallife_career_signed: Signed on with {employer} as {title}. Rota: {rota}. Your first shift is the next rota day.
reallife_career_text_signed: Welcome to {employer}. You start as {title}. Your rota: {rota}. Shift reminders will come to this number. Reviews are held at the office every three shifts.
reallife_career_left_good: You have worked your notice at {employer} and left with a good reference.
reallife_career_left_plain: You have worked your notice at {employer}. Too little on your file for a reference either way.
reallife_career_text_left_good: {employer}: thank you for working your notice. A good reference is on file for whoever asks. Good luck.
reallife_career_text_left_plain: {employer}: your notice is worked and you are off our books. We did not have enough to go on to write a reference.
reallife_career_text_review_due: {boss} here. Your performance review is due. Come to the office when you can; nothing moves on your pay or rank until we have had it.
reallife_career_mate_hello_1: {name} is on with you today. 'Morning! Kettle's just boiled if you're quick.'
reallife_career_mate_hello_2: {name} nods as you clock on. 'Oh good, it's you. Thought I was on my own again.'
reallife_career_mate_hello_3: {name} is already at it. 'There you are. Busy one today, they reckon.'
reallife_career_mate_hello_4: 'Hey, it's {name}. You on this shift too? Good. Makes it go quicker.'
reallife_career_cab_shift_done: That is your four fares. Shift done.
reallife_career_no_luxury: Premium work is done in a luxury car: a Mersaidi S500, a Lytte L6, a Petrolls. Come back at the wheel of one.
reallife_career_cart_no_money: You cannot cover today's rent on the cart. Come back when you can.
reallife_career_cart_rented: Cart rented for the day: {amount}. What you take today is yours.
reallife_career_test_top: Test: you are already at the top rank with this employer.
reallife_job_dispatch_foot_done: Your plan {km} km, best possible {best} km
reallife_job_dispatch_obj_done: Planned: {km} km against a best of {best} km
reallife_job_dispatch_full: That van is full: three parcels a van.
reallife_job_dispatch_left: You walked away from the desk. The vans went out as they were.
reallife_job_dispatch_timeout: Out of time: the rest went on whichever van had room.
reallife_job_dispatch_great_1: A tight plan: hardly a wasted metre. {amount} for that batch.
reallife_job_dispatch_great_2: The drivers will thank you for that one. {amount}.
reallife_job_dispatch_fair_1: It will do: a van or two will double back. {amount}.
reallife_job_dispatch_fair_2: Not bad, not the best. {amount} for that batch.
reallife_job_dispatch_poor_1: Vans crossing each other all over the map. {amount}, and the drivers are muttering.
reallife_job_dispatch_poor_2: That plan burns fuel for nothing. {amount}, and a note on the desk.
reallife_job_lead_obj_round: Go and see how {name} is getting on
reallife_job_lead_obj_wait: Back to it. Something will come up
reallife_job_lead_obj_done: Shift over: the team are heading off
reallife_job_lead_see_fine: Head down, writing up the list: getting on with it, and well.
reallife_job_lead_see_slacking: A cigarette on the firm's time, and not the first by the look of it.
reallife_job_lead_see_stuck: Arms folded, waiting. Stuck on something and not saying so.
reallife_job_lead_right_fine: {name} grins. A word of thanks goes a long way.
reallife_job_lead_right_slacking: {name} stubs it out and gets back to it. Fair, and they know it.
reallife_job_lead_right_stuck: Two minutes of your time and {name} is moving again. That is the job.
reallife_job_lead_wrong_1: {name} gives you a look. That was not what the moment called for.
reallife_job_lead_wrong_2: Wrong call. {name} shrugs and carries on exactly as before.
reallife_job_lead_wrong_3: {name} says nothing, which says plenty. You misread that one.
reallife_job_lead_call_good_1: Handled. Nobody upstairs will ever hear about it, which is the point.
reallife_job_lead_call_good_2: Good call: quick, fair, and it is over.
reallife_job_lead_call_good_3: That is how it should be dealt with. The team noticed.
reallife_job_lead_call_ok_1: It will do. Not the neatest way out, but nobody is complaining.
reallife_job_lead_call_ok_2: Dealt with, more or less. It cost a bit more than it needed to.
reallife_job_lead_call_bad_1: That made it worse. Somebody is going to write that down.
reallife_job_lead_call_bad_2: Bad call. That one goes in the book as a complaint.
reallife_job_lead_call_bad_3: The team saw that, and so did the customer. Not your best moment.
reallife_job_lead_call_none: You said nothing and did nothing, and it sorted itself out badly.
reallife_job_lead_left: You walked off and left the team to it. That is not a shift in charge.
reallife_job_lead_time: End of the shift: whatever was not dealt with is the next lead's problem.
reallife_job_lead_inc_late: A delivery is an hour late and the client is on the phone, furious. What do you do?
reallife_job_lead_inc_row: Two of the team are having a shouting match where the customers can hear every word.
reallife_job_lead_inc_short: Somebody has called in sick and the next two hours are one pair of hands short.
reallife_job_lead_inc_spill: Something has been spilt right by the door, and people are walking straight through it.
reallife_job_lead_inc_count: The cash count is twenty short, and three people have been near the box today.
reallife_job_lead_inc_refund: A customer wants their money back and you are not sure they are owed it.
reallife_business_frequency: How often something comes up (1 to 10)
reallife_test_business_rivals: The next rival move at my business
reallife_test_business_racket: The protection racket makes its demand
reallife_test_business_customers: The next customer complaint or praise
reallife_test_business_resolve: Close every business event and undo its effects
reallife_text_business_welcome: Business desk. Whatever comes up at your businesses is listed here with its deadline: competitors, inspectors, staff, suppliers, the odd piece of good news. Call to see what is open and to decide what to do about it. Nothing is decided for you before its deadline.
reallife_biz_desk_off: Business events are switched off on the options page.
reallife_biz_desk_empty: Nothing is open at your businesses. If something comes up it will be listed here, with its deadline.
reallife_biz_desk_empty_easy: Nothing is open. 'Good news only' is on: only opportunities will come up.
reallife_biz_cannot: That cannot be done right now: not enough money, or what it needs is not in place. Nothing has changed; choose again.
reallife_biz_staff_gone: The person concerned no longer works for you. There is nothing left to decide.
reallife_biz_test_no_business: Business test: you run no business that takes money yet.
reallife_biz_test_busy: Business test: {business} already has an open issue. Deal with it on the Business desk, or use 'resolve all'.
reallife_biz_test_kind_open: Business test: '{issue}' is already open at one of your businesses.
reallife_biz_test_failed: Business test: '{issue}' could not be started (see Player.log).
reallife_biz_test_resolved: Business test: every open issue was closed, every footfall change and closure put back, and the racket forgotten.
