reallife_guide_start: Real Life Overhaul {version} adds everyday life to the city of Big Ambitions: a camera behind your character, cars that drive like their kind, accidents, crime and police, jobs, illness, people to know and a city government. Each part can be switched off by itself on the options page. # First steps - Out of doors the camera sits behind you and the mouse looks around. {key_free_cursor} gives you the mouse cursor back for clicking and takes it again; {key_camera_toggle} switches to the game's own camera. - Your phone has new contacts. Each can be called. # The options page - Open the game's Options and choose the Mods tab. The mod's page starts with a search box, the button for this Guide, the presets, and reset, export and import. Below them is one section per feature: click a name to open or close it. - Type two letters or more in the search box to find options by a word in their name or their feature's. # Presets - A preset sets how much happens to you. The mod starts on Standard. Relaxed leaves you nearly alone; Realistic and Hardcore bring more incidents and more police. The preset now is {preset}, and the page 'Presets' lists what each one sets. # This Guide - It is an app on your phone, called Guide. It also opens from the button 'Open the Guide on your phone' on the options page (when you close the menu), from the contact 'Real Life Overhaul Guide' (there while 'The mod's phone contacts' is on) and from the notice you are shown once for each new version. - The tab 'Pages' lists the pages, one per feature. Click one and the tab 'Reading' shows its text, a line to a row; scroll with the mouse wheel. 'All pages' on the left goes back to the list. - Prices, fines and keys on these pages are read from the mod when a page is opened, so they are the ones in force. # The options page - The mod's options are in ten groups, from 'Start here' to 'Troubleshooting'. A group opens to its sections, and one is open at a time. - Each button says how many of its switches are on. - Rest the pointer on a row for a sentence about it. 'About this section' opens its page in this Guide. - A greyed row says what it needs: switch that on first. - The search box at the top finds a row by any word, and shows the group and section it is in. # The mod's keys, as you have them now - Change them on the options page under 'Controls'. The performance and development keys do nothing while 'Developer diagnostics' is off. {controls}
reallife_guide_presets: A preset sets a group of options in one go. The four buttons are on the options page under 'Start here'. The preset in use now is {preset}; it reads 'Custom' as soon as one of the options below differs from all four. - Relaxed: little is done to you. No crime against you, no police stops or pursuits, no cost or injury from your own crashes, traffic cannot knock you down, no illness, no prison, no driving licence needed, no fuel use or breakdowns, weather without effects, relationships that do not fade, and only the opportunities for your businesses. Fewer incidents; jobs pay a quarter more. (Hitting a person with your car still costs the fine for it.) - Standard: the values the mod ships with. - Realistic: everything on, with more accidents, crime and fires, more police about and more trouble for your businesses. - Hardcore: everything on at the strict end: incidents frequent, police about most of the time, the longest prison term 10 days, jobs pay a fifth less. There is no permanent death in any preset, and the fines are the same in all of them. A preset touches only the options in the table below. Camera, visuals, clothes, keys and performance stay yours. Before a preset is applied, your settings are written to settings_before_preset.txt in {folder}. To undo a preset, rename that file to settings.txt and press Import. Changes take effect at once; something already going on plays out under the old values. # What each preset sets
reallife_guide_camera_about: A camera behind your character on foot, and behind the car when you drive.
reallife_guide_camera: # On foot - The camera follows behind you. With mouse look on, the mouse turns the camera and the cursor is hidden; a small dot marks the middle of the screen. - {key_camera_toggle} switches between this camera and the game's own. {key_free_cursor} frees the cursor and locks it again. - The mouse wheel still zooms. Indoors (if you switch that on) the camera is pulled in front of walls. - Mouse look switches itself off while a menu, the map, a shop window or a dialogue is open, and while the game is not the active window. - {key_interact} (or {key_interact_alt} while the game shows no prompt of its own) near a door or your own car takes you in the way a click would: opening hours and entrance fees apply. The door must be within about 5 m, the car within about 4.5 m. During one of the mod's jobs the key opens no door: click the building instead. # In the car - A chase camera sits behind the car; the mouse looks around and the view swings back behind the car after about a second without mouse movement once you are moving. - Hold {key_look_behind} to look behind. - In garages and car parks, and when you use the game's own look-back, the game's cameras take over. # Map markers - The game's place markers are put at the correct edge of the screen when what they mark is behind the camera. # Other camera mods - While another mod drives the camera, this mod's camera, mouse look and chase camera stand aside. They come back a second or two after the other mod lets the camera go. - A message names the mod once in a session, and the camera's rows on the options page name it for as long as it has the camera. The camera key shows the message again. # Known limits - The chase camera's mouse look is off while the game's own 'vehicle mouse input' setting is on.
reallife_guide_character_about: Your character drawn in the game's detailed version in the city, and clothes and shoes made for the mod.
reallife_guide_character:
# What it does
- In the city the game draws a simplified player. The mod hides it and draws the detailed character the game uses in character creation and the shop mirror instead, moving exactly as you do. If you wear something the detailed set does not have, your normal body is shown while you wear it.
- Hair and beards get a finish with depth, hair gets a hair-coloured scalp underneath, skin gets a finer grain up close, and textures are sharpened.
- Hair keeps its own colour under any light. With a lamp behind or beside your head, dark hair stays dark: the glow and the shine of hair follow its colour and stay below the brightness of lit skin. With the hair option off you see the game's own hair, which glows orange against a lamp whatever its colour.
- Character creation and the previews at the hairdresser, the clothing store and the plastic surgeon get a fill light and a rim light.
- New looks: five styles of shoe in four colours each; T-shirts, a bomber jacket, jeans, chinos, suit trousers, a pencil skirt, a summer dress and an evening dress in up to 32 colours and prints.

# How to wear the new clothes
- In character creation the everyday pieces are in the game's own lists, tagged RLO.
- In a save, pick them on the options page under 'Your character and home', in 'Clothes (men)' or 'Clothes (women)': a garment, then its colour. The first entry of each list is 'Game's own', which shows whatever the game has you wearing.
- With 'Clothes must be bought' on (it is on in a new game), a piece has to be bought first at the Real Life Overhaul rack in a clothing store, for $35 to $260. What you chose in character creation is yours.
- Your picks are kept with the save. They are drawn over the game's clothes; choosing another piece of that kind in one of the game's own screens takes the mod's piece off.

# Checking your hair
- The test tools of the options page have three entries for hair. One writes to Player.log what each layer of your hair is made of. One stands a strong lamp 3 m beyond your head for 20 seconds, so you can turn the camera round and look at your hair against the light. One switches the hair finish off and on, to compare it with the game's own hair.

# Known limits
- The clothes need the mod's files. If they are missing, the new looks are left out and the game's look stays.
- If the detailed character cannot be matched to your character, the mod says so once in Player.log and shows the game's own character until the next load.
reallife_guide_citylife_about: People at work and going about their day on the pavements near you.
reallife_guide_citylife: # What you see - Street sweepers, window cleaners, a road crew, people handing out leaflets, a painter on a ladder, a gardener, a postman on his round, a courier with a sack truck. - Friends talking, two friends on a bench, smokers, people on the phone, somebody eating lunch from a carton or on a doorstep with a mug, tourists with a map, joggers, a chess table, tai chi in the morning, a queue outside a door at night, umbrellas in the rain. - A coffee cart and a hot-dog cart with customers who walk up, queue, are served and walk off. - {city_count} different activities in all, each with its own hours. At most {city_sites} of them are out at once with {city_people} people in all, 45 to 95 m from you, and they are set up and taken away only where you are not looking. # What you can do - Buy a coffee: stand at the counter of the coffee cart and press {key_interact}. It costs {coffee_price} and gives a little energy (5 of 100). - Otherwise they are there to be seen. Drive into them and they fall like anyone else. # When it is quiet - Nothing is out between 02:00 and 05:00, little before 07:00 and after 22:00. - While an accident or a crime is going on, nothing new starts. - In the rain everybody is taken in except the people with umbrellas. # Known limits - It needs the mod's animation and model files. An activity whose animation or model is missing does not start.
reallife_guide_crime_about: Crime that happens near you, crime against you, and the police stopping you for your own driving.
reallife_guide_crime: # Crime near you - Now and then something happens within 35 to 80 m: a foot chase, a snatch, a mugging, graffiti, a car break-in, a traffic stop, a shoplifter, a hold-up. There are {crime_count} kinds. An orange marker shows where. - One thing at a time: no crime starts during an accident or while the police have business with you. - You can watch, walk away, or call 911 (the first choice names what is going on): an officer is sent, and if it ends in an arrest you get the 'Did the right thing' mood. - Somebody running for it can be stopped: stay within arm's reach of them. An officer comes, sometimes they try to break free once, and you are thanked, sometimes with cash. - In your own shop you can confront a thief with {key_interact}. - A 911 call about nothing is a warning twice a day; the third and every one after it cost {fine_wasted_call}, and with arrests for serious offences on the fifth puts you in a holding cell. # Crime against you (option: crimes against you) - Pickpocket: takes 6% of your cash, from $10 to $250. Catch them and you get it back. - Mugging, on foot between 21:00 and 05:00: hand over 15% ($20 to $400), or refuse: half the time they run, half the time you lose 7.5% ($20 to $200) and are hurt. Walking away before they reach you also works. - Neither happens while you carry less than $60. - Hold-up in your own shop: 4% of your cash ($40 to $500). - Out of your sight: a break-in at one of your shops overnight (stock, and a repair bill of $60 to $350; good security prevents most), your parked car broken into (repair up to $250), a scam call (hang up and it costs nothing; give the details and you may lose up to $400). - A pickpocket or mugger leaves you alone for at least two days after the last one; break-ins, car break-ins and scam calls rest five to seven days each. # Being pulled over (option: police stop you) - What counts: running a red light, speeding, driving on the pavement, driving against the traffic. Speeding means more than {speed_margin} km/h over the limit ({speed_limit} km/h where the road does not say) for {speed_seconds} seconds. - It only matters if somebody sees it. A patrol car happens to be near {seen_redlight} of the time for a red light, {seen_speeding} for speeding (twice that from {speed_gross} km/h) and {seen_reckless} for reckless driving, scaled by the crime frequency option; an officer on foot with a clear view sees much more. With the option 'Police attend accidents and chase hit-and-run drivers' off, nothing you do at the wheel is seen. - A patrol car then comes up behind you with its lights on. Stop within 15 seconds and stay stopped: an officer walks up and writes the ticket. - Fines: red light {fine_redlight}, speeding {fine_speeding}, reckless or wrong side {fine_reckless}. Each kind is charged once per stop. After two drinks or more, any stop adds $900 for driving after drinking. - If you drive on, it is a pursuit. Lose them (out of sight for ten seconds, or 240 m ahead) and you pay no fine, but your car is known for the rest of the day: it is noticed far more easily and pays half as much again. - If they catch you: the fines, plus {fine_fleeing} for fleeing and {fine_fleeing_step} for every quarter minute it lasted, at most {fine_fleeing_most}, and you are arrested and held at the nearest police station (see the Guide page on custody). With the custody option off, {custody_min} to {custody_max} hours pass and you are let go where you stood. - On foot, crossing on red or walking in the road in front of an officer earns a shout and, one time in five, a fine of {fine_jaywalk}. - Fines are charged in full, even if that takes you below zero. # Known limits - A pickpocket or a mugger cannot be reported to 911. - The crimes on this page never kill you; refusing a mugger can injure you.
reallife_guide_driving_about: Each car gets the acceleration and top speed of its kind, an eased throttle and a speedometer.
reallife_guide_driving: # What changes - In the game every car has the same engine and gearbox and is stopped by a limiter at 50 to 100 km/h. With car tuning on, the car you drive (never traffic) is given a 0-100 time and a top speed for its kind, and air drag instead of a limiter: it pulls hard to 50, steadily to 100 and builds slowly to its top speed. - Examples (0-100 km/h, top speed): Honza Mimic 12.5 s, 170; Vord Tiara Vic 10 s, 190; BIMA 320 8.5 s, 210; Mersaidi S500 6.5 s, 240; Vord Pony 5.8 s, 240; Ferdinand 112 5.0 s, 265; Anselmo AF90 4.5 s, 290; UMC Nunavut 9 s, 190; UMC Desert van 16 s, 140; Freight Truck T1 20 s, 130. Scooters and hand trucks are left alone. - The two sliders scale top speed and acceleration from 70% to 150% of those figures. - Smooth throttle: the throttle key eases the pedal down over {throttle_rise} s and lifts in {throttle_fall} s, so a tap pulls away gently. An analogue trigger keeps its own feel. - Hold {key_gentle_throttle} to keep the pedal at {gentle_throttle} at most. - Brakes are the game's own. From the new top speeds a car needs 66 to 122 m to stop: look ahead. - The speedometer shows km/h or mph, following the game's units setting. - Everything changed on a car is put back when you get out, change car or switch the option off. # Measure this car - The button on the options page times a real run: press it, come to a stop, then hold full throttle for 20 seconds. A message gives 0-50, 0-100 and the speed reached. # After a hospital trip - Your car is brought to a kerb space near where you come out, or towed to a repair shop, for {tow_fee}. # Known limits - A car from another mod is placed by its own data (weight, cargo room, the game's top speed) into one of the kinds above. - A car the sums cannot be done for (no combustion engine or no automatic gearbox) is left as the game made it, with a line in Player.log. - Faster cars mean the police notice speed only when it is well over the limit for a while: see Crime and police stops.
reallife_guide_jobs_about: Seven jobs you do yourself on the street, paid when the work is done.
reallife_guide_jobs: # How to get one - Call the Gig Line on your phone, or walk up to a help-wanted board (outside a few service buildings): the game's own panel appears over it with a Read the board button, and the button shows its key. You are told each job's pay, your level and how much of it is left today; take one or ask what else there is. - To stop, call the Gig Line again and say you are done. Work done so far is paid. Giving up with most of the work undone can count as a failed shift. - A job cannot start indoors, during one of the game's own missions, or with energy below {job_min_energy}. # The jobs - A unit is one piece of the work: a flyer taken, an eighth of a floor cleaned, a box shelved, a customer served, a song, a parcel delivered, a fare. - Every job shows its figures in a copy of the game's job panel at the top right: what to do, how much is done, what could end the shift early, what you have earned and the time on shift. What you can do is a button on the game's panel over the place of work. Each button shows its key and can also be clicked. - Where a job has Let time pass, it hands the rest of the shift to the game's clock, as the game's own job does: its panel shows the time remaining, the game's skip button and Stop. The clock pays {skip_share} of the usual pay for each unit it does, with no tips and no bonus, and takes the game minutes each job says below. Stop at any time and carry on by hand. {job_table} - Flyers: you are dressed as a canvasser. The panel stands over whoever is in reach with an Offer a flyer button. More pay on a busy street and for the whole bundle. With nobody in reach the panel over you has Let time pass: {skip_minutes_flyers} game minutes a flyer. - Cleaner: you wear the cleaner's uniform. A client's floor is dirty with the game's own dirt, the same as in your own shop: Go in at the door, take the mop (it is put in your hands, or Take the mop if you have put it away) and click the dirty patches until the game's cleanliness reads 100%. The job panel shows the cleanliness and the aim of 100%. You are paid by the share of the dirt you took off: the whole fee at 100%, the share done if you leave or time runs out, and half or more is a shift done. Let time pass cleans the rest: {skip_minutes_cleaner} game minutes for each eighth of the floor, and the room really is clean afterwards. - Shelf stocker: carry boxes from the kerb to a shop's shelves: Pick up at the pile, Go in at the door, Put on the shelf at the shelf. Let time pass at the pile: {skip_minutes_stocker} game minutes a box. - Drinks cart: see "Working the drinks cart" below. - Busker: walk on to your pitch. You are turned to face the street and kept there. The panel over the pitch has the three songs, and then Strum each time a strum is called for. More has Step away (after {busker_abandon} seconds away the set is packed up and what is in the case is kept) and Let time pass: {skip_minutes_busker} game minutes a song, paying {skip_share} of what a song usually brings in here and now, taking {busker_average} of the strums to be in time. Tips only, more where and when people are about. The police may move you on. - Courier: the panel over each place has the button for it: Collect the parcels, Load the car, Take a parcel from the car, then Hand over the parcel or Leave the parcel at the door. A bonus for beating the clock. There is no Let time pass: the car would have to be moved. - Ride-hail: pick up fares and drive them smoothly: the tip follows the passenger's comfort, which the job panel shows. {taxi_misses} missed fares end the shift. There is no Let time pass. # No two shifts alike - What a gig pays and how big it is are drawn once, from the day, the hour and the gig. Ask again in the same hour and you get the same offer. The Gig Line says it, and the first line of the job panel repeats it. - The client is tight, fair or generous: {gig_client_low} to {gig_client_high} of the usual fee. A busy day pays {gig_busy_fee}; a day that is not busy pays {gig_normal_fee}, so that over many shifts the average is the usual fee. On average {gig_busy_per_day} of the gigs are busy each day, and about one day in two one gig has nothing on. - The size varies round the usual number of units, as the list above says. Pay is for the work done, so a bigger shift pays more. - Flyers, the cart and the busker can meet a quiet street ({gig_quiet} of the usual crowd) or a rush ({gig_rush}). The panel says which. - Small events are each said in a notification. A big tipper turns up in {gig_tipper_chance} of the shifts of the cart, busker, courier, ride-hail and shelf stocker, and tips {gig_tipper_low} to {gig_tipper_high} units of pay. On flyers, cleaning and shelves a client adds a speed bonus in {gig_speed_chance} of the shifts, {gig_speed_low} to {gig_speed_high} units of pay, if you finish by hand within {gig_speed_time} of the time. A difficult customer, in {gig_redo_chance} of the cart and cleaning shifts, sends a drink back or finds a patch you missed. - Working outdoors in bad weather pays more when the weather option is on: {gig_rain_pay} more in rain, {gig_storm_pay} in a storm, {gig_spell_pay} in a heat wave or a cold snap and {gig_ice_pay} on ice. - The usual fee is the average of a shift played well in fair weather, with its tips and speed bonus. Employers' shifts, booked sets and the test buttons are worked at the usual figures, with none of this. # The rules - Levels: {job_levels} per job. Each level above the first pays {job_level_bonus} more. The 'Job pay' option scales everything. - If you run businesses of your own, every job pays 15% less for each one, down to 55% of the usual pay at the lowest. The pay the Gig Line and the employers quote already includes this. - Ride-hail wants a reference (level {job_reference_level} in any job), no police stop on a job in the last {job_clean_days} days and, while driving licences are switched on, a taxi endorsement from a driving school. - A driving job needs a car within 60 m. With none of your own you are given a hired van for {job_van_fee} a day; it is taken back when the shift is over and you are out of it. - On a driving job a crash costs {job_crash_cut} of that unit's pay and a police stop {job_stop_cut} (twice that on the courier's round). A pay slip never goes below zero. - {job_strikes} failed shifts in a job and it lets you go for {job_sacked_days} days. A good shift takes a strike off. - Work uses energy and trains a skill through the game's own systems. It never takes your energy below 12. - A shift ends by itself, paid, if you sleep, are taken to hospital or into custody, take one of the game's missions, or walk into a building that is not the client's. - A job in progress does not carry on after a load. A save made during a shift remembers what you were owed, and loading it pays you that at once and ends the shift. The work counts towards your level and the day's amount, and nothing is held against you. # Working the drinks cart - The cart is set up on the pavement beside you and is solid: you and everyone else walk round it. An arrow points at your place behind it. - Walk on to that place. You press nothing: you are turned to face the customers, put in the vendor's uniform and kept there. Your own clothes come back when the shift ends. - The job's panel at the top right of the screen stays up for the whole shift: customers served, walk-offs out of three, takings and tips, the time on shift and about how long is left. - A panel over the cart shows each order and the customer's patience, with a button for each of the three drinks. Every button shows its key and can also be clicked. The right drink within {vendor_quick} seconds earns a full tip; a wrong one costs the customer {vendor_wrong} seconds of patience; a customer kept {vendor_patience} seconds walks off, and three walk-offs end the shift. - Let time pass hands the rest of the shift to the game's clock, as the game's own job does: its panel shows the time remaining, the game's skip button and Stop. The clock takes {vendor_minutes_each} game minutes a customer and pays {vendor_skip_share} of a customer's pay, with no tips and no bonus. Stop at any time and serve the rest by hand. - Call out calls to the people walking past within {vendor_hawk_within} m. Each one is tempted, annoyed or takes no notice; the tempted and the annoyed show it with the game's faces over their heads, and up to two of the tempted stop and look at the cart. For each tempted one a customer more comes to the cart, soon, up to {vendor_hawk_extra} more than the shift's own number and never past the day's amount of a gig. It can be used again after {vendor_hawk_cooldown} seconds. - A passer-by is more easily tempted at lunch and from 16:00 to 21:00, on a busy pavement and with a higher customer service skill, and less easily at night, while customers already wait at the cart, and when you have just called out. Each call in the last {vendor_hawk_fade} seconds raises the share who are annoyed. With three such calls and police presence switched on, an officer may warn you; the second warning ends calling out for the shift. - Step away lets you walk again. Customers go on waiting, and after {vendor_abandon} seconds away from the cart the shift is given up. Walk back on to your place to carry on. - When the shift ends the pay slip is one of the game's notifications: what the work paid, the tips, any bonus and, for an employer, the basic wage.
reallife_guide_job_row: {name}: {pay} a unit{metre}{size}, at most {daily} units a day, a level every {level} units
reallife_guide_life_about: Small things that happen to you, a cold now and then, and people to call.
reallife_guide_life:
# Random events
- Every so often something happens (the frequency option is roughly the number of events per game week): a message on screen, a text from Alex or Mom, or a question with two answers. There are {life_count} of them, and none repeats in a save until all that fit your situation have been seen.
- They move small amounts of money, energy, hunger or mood, and a few give you a cold or a minor injury. A loss never puts you in debt, and questions are never asked while you drive.
- Nothing happens while you sleep, sit in a menu or a dialogue, or are otherwise busy.

# Being sick
- A cold lowers your mood and drains a little extra energy for a day or two.
- Call Dr. Patel while you are sick: a consultation costs {doctor_fee} and cures it. So does a hospital stay.

# The phone
- 911: report what is happening near you, or ask for an ambulance for yourself ({ambulance_fee}, plus the game's own hospital bill). If you were driving, your car is brought near the hospital afterwards for {tow_fee}.
- Alex and Mom can each be called once a day for a better mood. They also text you as part of events.

# Moods
- The mod adds its own entries to the game's happiness list (Feeling sick, Injured, Lucky day, Got robbed and so on). They wear off after a few hours to three days.

# Known limits
- The contacts appear only while 'The mod's phone contacts' is on, and that option is read when a save is loaded.
reallife_guide_people_about: Officers on the beat, a patrol car at the kerb, and the crews at accident and crime scenes.
reallife_guide_people:
# What you see
- One or two officers walking a beat near you, a patrol car parked at the kerb with its crew beside it, an officer at a junction. The 'Police on the streets' and 'How often officers patrol' options say how often.
- At scenes: drivers who get out, paramedics with a stretcher, officers who put up tape, direct traffic and take statements. Officers and paramedics wear one uniform each with their equipment.

# Why it matters
- An officer on foot who has a clear view of you is a witness to what you do at the wheel, and to crossing on red: see Crime and police stops.
- At an accident you can walk up to help (within about 9 m, on foot) for the 'Did the right thing' mood.

# Limits the mod keeps to
- Officers, crews and the people at scenes are at most {pool_people} at once, and at most {pool_presence} of them are there only to be seen. An accident or crime scene takes those first, so a parked patrol car may stand empty for a while.
- They appear and leave where you are not looking, and they walk wherever they go.
reallife_guide_phone_about: Contacts you can call, and a modern look for the phone.
reallife_guide_phone: # Contacts - Emergency Services (911): report an accident, a crime or a fire near you, or call an ambulance for yourself ({ambulance_fee}). - Dr. Patel: a phone consultation when you are sick ({doctor_fee}). - Alex and Mom: a chat once a day each, for your mood. - Gig Line: the jobs (it needs 'Jobs' on as well). - Real Life Overhaul Guide: opens this guide. - Most other features add a contact of their own, described on that feature's page. - The contacts and their messages are kept in your save by the game, like its own contacts. - Every contact the mod adds has a picture from the game itself: a person's face from the game's portrait camera, and an organisation's logo from the game's own logo shapes. - The Search contacts box at the top of Contacts shows only the contacts whose name or description has every word you type, in the category you picked. # The phone's look - With 'Modern phone look' on the phone has a modern body, a wallpaper, a clock and a status bar. Phone cases bought in the game keep working. Switching it off puts the game's phone back at once. # Known limits - 'The mod's phone contacts' is read when a save is loaded: switching it on or off takes effect on the next load. It covers every contact the mod adds. Switching it off does not delete contacts already in a save; 'Prepare this save for removing the mod' does.
reallife_guide_ragdoll_about: People hit by a car fall as bodies with weight, and may be hurt or killed.
reallife_guide_ragdoll:
# When you hit someone
- Below about 15 km/h they are knocked over, get up after a few seconds and walk off angry. From 15 to 35 they stay down, hurt. Above that they may die: one in ten at 35 km/h, almost certainly from 90.
- Someone who stays down becomes an accident scene: an ambulance and a patrol car come, and the casualty is taken away.
- You have the same choice as after hitting a car: stop within about 12 seconds and stay near, or drive off. With 'police pursuit' off it is always settled as if you had stopped.
- Stopped: {fine_injury} for an injury, {fine_death} for a death. Fled and caught: {fine_injury_run} and {fine_death_run}. Got away: {fine_injury_escaped} and {fine_death_escaped}, billed some hours later. A death weighs on your mood for three days.
- At the roadside the police take at most 35% of your cash, or $250 if that is more. The rest of the fine goes to court with the case, or is not collected. A fine billed later is charged in full.

# When traffic hits you (option: player knockdown)
- On foot in the road you can be knocked down: shaken at low speed, injured from about 15 km/h, and taken to hospital from about 35. You lie for a few seconds and get up where you landed. You are never killed, and cannot be hit again for a few seconds.

# Pedestrians hit by traffic (option: pedestrians struck by traffic)
- Now and then a traffic car hits a pedestrian near you, and an ambulance and the police come. How often follows the accident frequency option.

# Limits the mod keeps to
- At most {ragdoll_max} people are falling with full physics at once; up to {ragdoll_still} more lie still. When more go down, the one who has lain longest makes room.
reallife_guide_traffic_about: Accidents among the game's own traffic, the emergency response to them, and what your own crashes cost.
reallife_guide_traffic:
# Accidents near you
- Now and then there is an accident near you: one car or two, three in a severe one; minor, moderate or severe (a severe one may roll a car). An orange marker shows where and how far.
- With 'Reckless drivers cause the accidents' on, it happens where a driver went wrong, often in view (see 'Horn and reckless drivers'). With it off, it is set up 45 to 140 m away.
- A patrol car always comes (with 'police' on); an ambulance for moderate and severe ones, and for those the road is closed with tape, barriers and cones. Crews work, the casualty leaves on a stretcher, and the scene clears inside about three minutes (five at the very most).
- Some drivers run for it and are chased.
- You can walk up to help, or call 911 and report it, which sends the units at once. Both earn the 'Did the right thing' mood.
- A road the mod closed is opened again whichever way the scene ends.

# Your own crashes (option: crash consequences)
- Hitting a traffic car at about 25 km/h or more costs damages from $150 to $3,000 by the speed of the impact. Harder hits injure you; the hardest end in hospital.
- With 'police pursuit' on you have about 12 seconds to stop near the crash. Stop, and you pay the damages only.
- Drive off and a patrol car comes after you, at up to {pursuit_least} to {pursuit_most} km/h depending on your car (about 83 km/h while car tuning is off), with a second one after {pursuit_backup} seconds. Caught: damages plus {fine_caught}, and you are arrested: with custody on, 8 to 16 hours in a holding cell. Got away: damages plus {fine_escaped}, billed some hours later (the bill is kept in your save).
- If a person was hurt, the larger fines under 'Ragdolls and people hit by cars' apply instead.

# Options
- 'How often accidents happen' also sets how often traffic hits a pedestrian.
- 'Siren' and 'People at accidents and on the street' are read when a unit or a scene starts; one already out keeps what it had.

# Known limits
- One incident of any kind at a time. A scene that is running when you switch its option off plays to its end.
reallife_guide_visuals_about: Colour grading and detail distance for the whole picture.
reallife_guide_visuals:
# What it does
- Saturation and contrast are added on top of the game's picture and cost nothing.
- Bloom at 0 leaves the game's own bloom alone; raising it costs frames.
- Detail distance above 100% keeps detailed models for longer and costs frames.
- Switching 'Picture adjustments' off puts the game's picture back at once.
reallife_guide_keys_about: Every key the mod listens to, and how to change it.
reallife_guide_keys:
# The mod's keys, as you have them now
{controls}
# Changing a key
- Options page, 'Controls': click a line, then press the new key. Hold Shift, Ctrl or Alt with it for a combination. Esc cancels, and so does waiting 8 seconds. The left mouse button and gamepad buttons are not offered.
- A key the game itself uses is allowed; the line then says which of the game's actions shares it.
- 'Reset the mod's keys to their defaults' puts all of them back.

# Keys for developer diagnostics
- The four lines that end '(developer diagnostics)' only work while 'Developer diagnostics' is switched on, on the options page. While it is off those keys do nothing.

# Fixed keys
- In jobs, choices are 1, 2, 3 (top row or number pad).
- In this guide: Esc, the arrows, Page Up and Page Down, Home, End, and typing to search.
- While this guide or another panel of the mod's is open, none of the mod's keys does anything.

# The game's own keys
- The mod changes none of them. Its interact key ({key_interact}) is the game's own interact key unless you change one of them; the second one ({key_interact_alt}) only acts while the game shows no prompt of its own.
reallife_guide_performance_about: Small changes to how the base game draws the city, and the tools to measure them on your computer.
reallife_guide_performance: # The switches (options page, 'Performance') - On by default, with nothing to see: the refraction effect is off outdoors, where nothing uses it; the sky's reflection and its light on things are refreshed every 2 seconds instead of every frame; street lamps that are off no longer keep their lights switched on. - Off by default: scenery more than 1.3 km away is not drawn; people, cars and small things are drawn only within 300 m in every direction; street furniture and parked cars are not drawn beyond 200 m. The last one can be seen: they appear at 200 m instead of 300 m. - Each switch puts back exactly what it changed when it is turned off. One that meets something unexpected says so once in Player.log and stays off until the city is loaded again. - No gain is promised: what a switch saves depends on your computer. The tools below measure it. # Measuring on your computer - Two buttons at the end of the 'Performance' section. 'Measure performance for 10 seconds' writes RealLifeOverhaul_perf_(time).txt: where the time of a frame goes and what is in the city around you, with a screenshot in the folder RealLifeOverhaul_shots. - 'Run the performance test (about 3 minutes)' switches each item off and on in turn, several times, and writes the table RealLifeOverhaul_bench_(time).txt. It needs you on foot in the street; stand still and leave the mouse alone. Parts of the picture and of the interface go and come back while it runs. - After pressing a button, close the menu: the measurement starts two seconds later. - The keys {key_perf_probe} and {key_perf_bench} start the same two measurements, but only while 'Developer diagnostics' is switched on. While it is off they do nothing. - The files are in {data}, next to Player.log. # What the mod itself costs - Apart from the camera, the mod's features work on timers, not every frame, and wait while nothing is going on. Options that cost frames (bloom, detail distance) are off or neutral by default and say so in their label.
reallife_guide_savetools_about: What the mod leaves in a save, and how to take it out again.
reallife_guide_savetools:
# What the mod puts into a save
- Its own data: what it remembers about this save (life events seen, illness, fines owed, job and career progress, your licence and record, the people you know, the city government and so on) and the mod version.
- Its moods in the happiness list. The game cannot load a mood it does not know, so the mod takes its moods out every time the game saves and puts them back a moment later: an ordinary save already loads without the mod.
- Its phone contacts with their messages, and its lines in the notification list.
- Bank entries for fines, fees and job pay.
- During a job with a hired van: that van, which is one of the game's own job vans.

# Removing the mod
1. Press "Prepare this save for removing the mod" in each save you want to keep.
2. Quit to the main menu and unsubscribe from the mod, or switch it off under Mods.
3. Restart the game.

# What "Prepare this save for removing the mod" does
- It makes two backup copies of the save's files first, and stops if either fails: one in a folder RealLifeOverhaul_backup_(date and time) inside the save's own folder, one under backups in {folder}. The game deletes a save's folder whole when you delete the character or its last save; the second copy is out of its reach.
- It then ends everything the mod has going, stops the mod's features until a save is loaded again, removes the moods, contacts, notification lines and data listed above, saves under the same name and lists what it removed. The list is also written to {folder}.
- Bank entries stay, because the money really moved; without the mod they are listed by a code, not a name.
- You must be on foot, and not in the middle of a hospital trip, police custody, sleep, an activity, a subway ride or a trip on the casino boat.
- It works on the save that is loaded, one at a time. There is no button for all saves at once.

# Reset the mod's data in this save
- Ends what is going on, takes the mod's moods off and removes its stored data, and keeps the mod running: as if the mod had just been added to this save. Contacts stay. A backup copy is made first; the save file itself is not changed until you save.

# Repair
- Puts back the mod's phone contacts and its moods if they are missing from a save.

# After every load
- The mod checks the save for things another version of it left behind. Moods this version does not have are removed, with a line in Player.log for each; anything else it does not recognise is kept.

# The mod's own files
- Settings files, save-tool reports and the second backup copies: {folder}. Performance reports and diagnostic files: {data}. None of them is needed to play.
- Options and key choices are kept by the game with its own settings, not in a save.
reallife_guide_diagnostics_about: Detailed lines in Player.log, the diagnostic keys, and the test buttons.
reallife_guide_diagnostics: # Developer diagnostics - Off unless you switch it on. While it is off the mod writes only warnings and errors to Player.log, and the four diagnostic keys do nothing. - Switch it on to report a problem: the mod's features then also write what they are doing to Player.log (a line per step, never a line per frame). - While it is on, {key_perf_probe} measures performance for ten seconds, {key_perf_bench} runs the performance test, {key_phone_dump} writes the layout of the phone's interface and of the characters to text files with a screenshot, and {key_character_report} writes a report of the characters on screen. The files are in {data}. None of this changes anything in the game. # Test tools - 'Show test tools' is off unless you switch it on. It puts 'Test tools' under Troubleshooting on the options page, with every feature's test buttons: an accident, a crime, a job, a life event and so on, started where you stand. A test that cannot start says why. - Some tests have real effects (a fine if you stop for the test patrol car, stock lost in the test break-in). # Check the mod's set-up - Looks through the options, the presets and the pages of this Guide for anything that does not fit together, and lists it. It changes nothing.
reallife_guide_trouble: # The camera jumps or fights itself - Another camera mod may be on as well. While it drives the camera, this mod's camera, mouse look and chase camera stand aside by themselves, and a message names the other mod. If the picture still shakes, switch one of the two off under Mods, and send Player.log: it has a line that starts with 'Camera:' for each time the camera was given up or taken back. # The mouse cursor is gone - Mouse look hides it. Press {key_free_cursor} to get it back (and again to return to mouse look), or {key_camera_toggle} for the game's own camera. # A key does nothing, or does two things - Look at 'Controls' in this Guide for the keys as you have them, and at 'Controls' on the options page: a line says when the game uses the same key. - {key_perf_probe}, {key_perf_bench}, {key_phone_dump} and {key_character_report} are diagnostic keys. They do nothing unless 'Developer diagnostics' is on. # Something of the mod's is stuck on the street - Switch its feature off and on again, or, with 'Show test tools' on, use the feature's clear or stop test button if it has one. 'Reset the mod's data in this save' ends everything at once. Loading the save also clears it: nothing the mod puts on the street is saved. # Frame rate - See 'Performance'. If in doubt, set bloom to 0 and detail distance to 100% under Visuals, and switch off the high-detail player character under 'Character and wardrobe'. # Where the files are - The game's log is Player.log in {data}. The mod's lines begin [Mod:Real Life Overhaul] (or [Mod:RealLifeOverhaul] for a copy in the ModsLocal folder). - Performance reports, diagnostic files and the folder RealLifeOverhaul_shots with their screenshots are in the same place. - Settings files and save-tool reports are in {folder}. - Backups of a save are inside that save's own folder under SaveGames, and again under backups in {folder}. # Reporting a problem - Switch on 'Developer diagnostics' (options page, Diagnostics) and make the problem happen again, so that Player.log has the detail. - Say what you were doing and what you expected, and attach Player.log from that session (it is overwritten when the game starts again). - For a frame-rate problem, press {key_perf_probe} while it is happening and attach the report it writes. - Export your settings (options page) and attach settings.txt. - Mention the mod version, {version}, and which other mods are on. # Going back - 'Reset every option and key' puts the mod as it came. To remove the mod, see 'Save tools'.
reallife_guide_credits:
# The mod
- Real Life Overhaul {version}.
- Big Ambitions is made by Hovgaard Games. This mod is not made or endorsed by them.

# What is in the mod's files
- The mod's own code and texts.
- Clothes and shoes, 77 street models and 77 animations, all made for this mod with Blender by its own scripts.
- No model, texture, animation or sound of Big Ambitions is in the files, and no third-party model, motion capture or animation library.
- The clothes were shaped around measurements of the game's character. The animations were made to the joint positions and bone names of the game's street character, so that they fit its people. These are measurements: nothing of the game's was copied.
- The lettering on signs and tape is drawn with the font Aileron Regular by Sora Sagano (CC0 1.0).
- 'THE DAILY POST' and 'QUICK BITE' on models are names made up for the mod.
- No sound files: the sirens and the city sounds are generated by the mod's code.

# Tools used (none of them is in the mod's files)
- Blender, Unity 2022.3, UnityPy, Pillow, NumPy and the .NET SDK.

# Licence
- The mod is open source under the MIT licence. Ask the author before you reuse its code, texts, models or animations.

reallife_lic_q_d01: The light ahead turns red as you approach the stop line. What must you do?|Stop behind the stop line and wait for green|Slow down and roll through if nothing is coming|Speed up to clear the junction

reallife_lic_q_d07: The light is green but the junction ahead is blocked by standing traffic. What do you do?|Wait behind the line until there is room to clear the junction|Enter the junction and stop in the middle of it|Drive round the queue on the pavement

reallife_lic_q_d10: A patrol car saw you run a red light and is behind you with its lights on. What should you do?|Pull over and stop: you get a ticket and that is the end of it|Drive on: they give up after a minute|Stop in the middle of the junction and get out

reallife_lic_q_d12: Who decides whether a red-light offence is booked?|An officer who saw it and stopped you: nobody is fined out of thin air|A camera on every lamp post|The driver behind you
reallife_lic_q_d13: What is the speed limit on a city street where no other limit is shown?|50 km/h|90 km/h|30 km/h
reallife_lic_q_d14: You drift to 60 in a 50 for a few seconds. How is that policed here?|It is over the limit, but police act on speeds well over the limit held for several seconds|It is an instant arrest|It is allowed on weekdays
reallife_lic_q_d15: How far over the limit, held for several seconds, gets you booked for speeding?|About 45 km/h over|5 km/h over|Only above 200 km/h
reallife_lic_q_d16: How many penalty points does a speeding ticket carry?|Three|One|Eight
reallife_lic_q_d17: What is the fine on a speeding ticket?|$180|$18|$1,800
reallife_lic_q_d18: From what speed is a patrol car far more likely to notice you, whatever the limit?|150 km/h|60 km/h|90 km/h
reallife_lic_q_d19: Your car can do 240 km/h. What may you do on a street with a 50 limit?|50 km/h|As fast as the car allows|120 km/h if the road is empty
reallife_lic_q_d20: On your practical test, what happens if you hold more than 10 km/h over the limit?|A minor fault each time; far over the limit is a serious fault|Nothing: examiners like confidence|The examiner takes the wheel
reallife_lic_q_d21: Why slow down before a junction even when your light is green?|Others may cross late and people may still be on the crossing|Because the engine needs a rest|You should not: speed up instead
reallife_lic_q_d22: You were booked for speeding today. What should you expect if you carry on like that?|To be stopped again: one ticket does not cover the rest of the day|Nothing more that day|A lower fine each time
reallife_lic_q_d23: The road is wet and it is dark. What should your speed be?|Lower than the limit: the limit is a maximum, not a target|Exactly the limit|Higher, to get home sooner
reallife_lic_q_d24: A truck and a sports car are on the same street. Which limit applies to each?|The same one: the limit belongs to the road, not the vehicle|A higher one for the truck, because it is heavier|Whatever each engine allows

reallife_lic_q_d29: May you drive along the pavement to get past a queue?|Never: it is reckless driving|Yes, slowly|Yes, if you use your horn
reallife_lic_q_d30: How many penalty points does driving on the pavement at speed carry?|Four|None|Two

reallife_civic_test_advance: Advance all construction sites one working day
reallife_civic_test_clear: Clear the council's people and construction sites
reallife_civic_test_reverted: Civic test: every city policy has been taken back. The city runs as it came.
reallife_civic_test_site: Civic test: {project} set out at {address}. Read the notice board beside it.
reallife_civic_test_advanced: Civic test: sites that did a full working day: {count}. Still in progress: {left}.
reallife_civic_test_rally_started: Civic test: a rally is gathering. Its people walk in from out of your sight; give them half a minute.
reallife_civic_test_cleared: Civic test: the street is cleared and the construction programme emptied. New sites start within the hour.
reallife_civic_site_refused_pavement: Test not started: there is no pavement within 8 m of the nearest building's door.
reallife_civic_site_refused_lane: Test not started: there is no traffic lane within 14 m of the pavement here, or only a junction; try the middle of a block.
reallife_civic_site_refused_kerb: Test not started: no kerb was found between the pavement and the lane, or the lane runs right against it.
reallife_civic_site_refused_vehicles: Test not started: vehicles are parked along the kerb where the works would be; try further along.
reallife_civic_site_refused_wall: Test not started: no upright building wall was found behind the nearest door, or it is too low for a scaffold.
reallife_civic_site_refused_room: Test not started: the wall is not flat for long enough, the pavement is too narrow, or something stands in the way.
reallife_civic_site_refused_close: Test not started: the lane runs within 3 m of the kerb and cannot be closed here (a junction in the stretch, or traffic would have no other way to go).
reallife_text_cityhall_welcome: City Hall information line. Call for who governs and what their policies cost or pay you, the next election and its candidates, building works near you, and petitions.
reallife_civic_closed: City Hall's line is closed. (Civic life is switched off on the options page.)
reallife_civic_slogan_safety_3: An officer you know by name.
reallife_civic_slogan_roads_1: Fix the street before the ribbon.
reallife_civic_slogan_roads_2: Green means go. Red means red.
reallife_civic_slogan_roads_3: Potholes don't vote. I fill them anyway.
reallife_civic_slogan_business_1: Open the shutters, lower the bill.
reallife_civic_slogan_business_2: A city that says yes to the corner shop.
reallife_civic_slogan_living_1: A city you can afford to stay in.
reallife_civic_slogan_living_3: Your pay should outlast the month.
reallife_civic_slogan_services_2: You pay for a city. Get one.
reallife_civic_slogan_services_3: The bins, the buses, the basics.
reallife_civic_slogan_growth_1: Build it. Open it. Fill it.
reallife_civic_slogan_growth_2: The city that stays up late.
reallife_civic_policy_policing_up_fx: about 40% more officers and patrol cars about, street crime down about 20%; the city levy rises by {levy} a week
reallife_civic_policy_policing_up_say: I will put four officers where there are three today, and you will see them on foot. It costs every household and business seventy dollars a week on the levy, and I think a street you can walk down is worth it.
reallife_civic_policy_policing_down_fx: about 40% fewer officers and patrol cars about, street crime up about 25%; {levy} a week comes back on the city levy
reallife_civic_policy_policing_down_say: We pay for patrols that drive past. I will trim the force and hand fifty dollars a week back to you. Yes, there will be fewer officers about. I would rather say so than pretend.
reallife_civic_policy_traffic_up_fx: police fines 50% higher, traffic accidents down about 30%
reallife_civic_policy_traffic_up_say: Run a red light in my city and it will cost you half as much again. Fewer crashes is the whole point; if you drive properly it costs you nothing.
reallife_civic_policy_traffic_down_fx: police fines 30% lower, traffic accidents up about 30%
reallife_civic_policy_traffic_down_say: People who drive for a living are fined like a cash machine. I will cut fines by nearly a third. The roads will be a little rougher for it, and I trust adults to cope.
reallife_civic_policy_tax_up_fx: a surcharge of 20% of the income tax your sales run up, billed weekly, where the game charges income tax (a year of sales of $150,000 or more)
reallife_civic_policy_tax_up_say: The services everyone wants have to be paid for. One fifth more on business income tax, billed weekly so nobody gets a shock in the spring.
reallife_civic_policy_tax_down_fx: 20% of the income tax your sales run up is paid back to you, weekly, where the game charges income tax (a year of sales of $150,000 or more)
reallife_civic_policy_tax_down_say: One fifth of what a business owes on its income comes straight back, every week. Shops that keep their money hire people. That is the plan.
reallife_civic_policy_levy_up_fx: 0.5% of your sales is charged weekly; {levy} a week comes off the city levy
reallife_civic_policy_levy_up_say: Half a cent on the dollar at the till, and forty dollars a week off the levy for everybody. Those who trade most carry a little more. I think that is fair.
reallife_civic_policy_levy_down_fx: 0.3% of your sales is paid back to you weekly
reallife_civic_policy_levy_down_say: Sell in this city and the city sends a little of it back: thirty cents on every hundred dollars. It is not much. It is every week.
reallife_civic_policy_grants_up_fx: {grant} a week for each business you run, up to three businesses
reallife_civic_policy_grants_up_say: A hundred and fifty dollars a week to every small business, for up to three premises. The big chains do not need it and will not get more than anyone else.
reallife_civic_policy_grants_down_fx: a licence fee of {grant} a week for each business you run, up to three businesses
reallife_civic_policy_grants_down_say: Sixty dollars a week for a licence to trade, for each business up to three. Nobody likes a fee. Everybody likes a city that works.
reallife_civic_policy_rent_up_fx: 6% on top of every rent you pay, billed weekly; if you let property, 4% more rent comes in
reallife_civic_policy_rent_up_say: Buildings get built when building pays. I will lift the rent rules. Rents will rise by around six per cent.
reallife_civic_policy_rent_down_fx: 6% of every rent you pay comes back to you weekly; if you let property, 4% less rent comes in
reallife_civic_policy_rent_down_say: Six per cent off every rent in the city, by rule. Landlords will tell you the sky is falling. They said that last time.
reallife_civic_policy_parking_up_fx: street parking costs 50% more; each parking ticket costs {ticket} more
reallife_civic_policy_parking_up_say: The kerb is the most valuable land we own and we give it away. Meters up by half, tickets up by sixty dollars.
reallife_civic_policy_parking_down_fx: street parking costs 40% less; each parking ticket costs {ticket} less
reallife_civic_policy_parking_down_say: Customers arrive by car whether we approve or not. Meters down by forty per cent, forty dollars off a ticket. Shops need the kerb more than the treasury does.
reallife_civic_policy_transit_up_fx: each subway ride costs {fare} more; buses run about 30% more often (where the mod runs buses)
reallife_civic_policy_transit_up_say: A bus every few minutes instead of whenever. To pay for it the subway fare goes up a dollar a ride. I would rather pay for a service than save on a timetable nobody believes.
reallife_civic_policy_transit_down_fx: each subway ride costs {fare} less; buses run about 25% less often (where the mod runs buses)
reallife_civic_policy_transit_down_say: A dollar off every subway ride. To pay for it some buses come off the quietest routes. Most people will wait two minutes longer and keep the dollar.
reallife_civic_policy_cleaning_up_fx: street sweepers two and a half times as common, a small lift to your mood; the city levy rises by {levy} a week
reallife_civic_policy_cleaning_up_say: Street sweepers two and a half times as common, and a city that feels cared for. Thirty dollars a week on the levy. Ask anyone who has visited a clean city whether it was worth it.
reallife_civic_policy_cleaning_down_fx: street sweepers rare, litter weighs on your mood; {levy} a week comes back on the city levy
reallife_civic_policy_cleaning_down_say: We sweep streets that are already clean. I will cut the rounds and give you twenty-five dollars a week. It will be grubbier. You will have the money.
reallife_civic_policy_night_up_fx: street crime up about 10%; opening hours do not change
reallife_civic_policy_night_up_say: A proper city does not go to bed at ten. I will have the police ease off the late streets. There will be a little more trouble after dark and a great deal more life.
reallife_civic_policy_night_down_fx: street crime down about 8%; opening hours do not change
reallife_civic_policy_night_down_say: Nothing good happens in a doorway at three in the morning. I will put the police on the late streets and keep them there. People who live above the bars have waited a long time to hear that.
reallife_civic_policy_permits_up_fx: construction sites work 35% faster and until 19:00; noise complaints are noted and nothing more
reallife_civic_policy_permits_up_say: A permit in days, not seasons, and sites allowed to work until seven. Roadworks that take a month will take three weeks. It will be louder while it lasts, and it will last less long.
reallife_civic_policy_permits_down_fx: construction sites work 25% slower and only 08:00 to 16:00; a noise complaint always brings quiet hours
reallife_civic_policy_permits_down_say: Nobody should be woken by a jackhammer at seven. Sites work eight to four, and one complaint brings an inspector. Yes, the works take longer. You will sleep through more of them.
reallife_civic_policy_events_up_fx: street events about 50% more often, a small lift to your mood; the city levy rises by {levy} a week
reallife_civic_policy_events_up_say: Markets, parades, music in the squares: half as many again. Forty dollars a week on the levy buys a city people cross the river to visit.
reallife_civic_policy_events_down_fx: street events about half as often; {levy} a week comes back on the city levy
reallife_civic_policy_events_down_say: A parade is a fine thing and a closed street is a closed street. Half the events, thirty dollars a week back. Celebrate at home; it is cheaper.
reallife_civic_policy_wages_up_fx: a floor of {floor} an hour: for anyone you pay less, counting any raise you agreed, you are billed the difference for their rota hours, weekly
reallife_civic_policy_wages_up_say: Sixteen dollars an hour, at least, for anyone you employ. If your business only works by paying less than that, we should talk about your business.
reallife_civic_policy_wages_down_fx: the city pays 5% of your weekly wage bill back to you
reallife_civic_policy_wages_down_say: Hire somebody and the city pays a twentieth of their wage. It is the cheapest job programme there is, and it leaves the hiring to people who know how.

reallife_civic_news_recall: Recall: voters force the mayor back to the polls

reallife_civic_news_scandal: Campaign embarrassed: its star endorsement has a criminal record
reallife_civic_news_scandal_body: A local business owner's public endorsement turned into a liability when their record came out. The candidate's rivals have not stopped mentioning it.
reallife_civic_news_paytoplay: Pay to play? A donor's building permit jumped the queue
reallife_civic_news_paytoplay_body: A construction permit was fast-tracked days after a call from one of the mayor's campaign donors. City Hall says procedures were followed.
reallife_civic_no_campaign: There is no campaign on at the moment.
reallife_civic_donate_offer: Donate {amount} to {name}'s campaign? You have given {given} so far; the most a campaign may take from one person is {cap}. Donations move the polls a little. If {name} wins, every {per} you gave earns you one fast-track building permit (two at most), which you call in on a site from this line. One time in four, calling one in ends up in the paper as "pay to play", which costs the mayor approval and you your good mood.
reallife_civic_donate_thanks: {name}'s campaign thanks you for {amount}. It will go on posters and leaflets.
reallife_civic_donate_cap: {name}'s campaign has had all it may take from one person in this election.
reallife_civic_donate_broke: You do not have the money for that.
reallife_civic_endorse_offer: Endorse {name} in public? You can endorse one candidate in an election and cannot take it back. Your word is worth more the more businesses you run: with {businesses} now, about {points} points in the polls. If you have a criminal record, the endorsement becomes a story about the record instead and costs them votes.
reallife_civic_endorse_thanks: Your endorsement of {name} is public. Their campaign will make the most of it.
reallife_civic_endorse_already: You have already endorsed {name} in this election. One endorsement is all anybody gets.
reallife_civic_endorse_scandal: You endorsed {name}, and by the afternoon the story was your criminal record, not their platform. Their campaign has stopped returning your calls.
reallife_civic_volunteer_offer: Give {name}'s campaign an afternoon? You stand where you are now and offer leaflets to the people who walk past: 30 leaflets or 4 minutes, between 10:00 and 18:00, on foot, out of doors. Each one taken helps a little. Once an election.

reallife_civic_volunteer_left: You left your pitch. {taken} people had taken a leaflet for {name} by then.
reallife_civic_volunteer_nothing: Your afternoon's canvassing is over. Nobody took a leaflet this time.
reallife_civic_volunteer_done_before: You have already given a campaign an afternoon in this election.
reallife_civic_volunteer_hours: Canvassers are out between 10:00 and 18:00. Call again then.
reallife_civic_volunteer_street: Canvassing is done on foot in the street, and not while you are on another job. Call again from the pavement.

reallife_civic_complain_offer: File a noise complaint about this site? The first complaint is put on file; a second brings an inspector, who puts the site on quiet hours (09:00 to 15:00) for three days. The works take longer for it.
reallife_civic_complain_offer_fast: File a noise complaint about this site? Under the fast-track permits policy in force, complaints are noted and nothing more is done.
reallife_civic_complain_offer_strict: File a noise complaint about this site? Under the strict permits policy in force, one complaint puts the site on quiet hours (09:00 to 15:00) for three days.
reallife_civic_complaint_logged: Your complaint is on file. One more about this site and an inspector comes out.
reallife_civic_complaint_upheld: Complaint upheld: the site is on quiet hours, 09:00 to 15:00, for the next three days.
reallife_civic_complaint_already: This site is already on quiet hours after a complaint. Yours has been added to the file.
reallife_civic_complaint_noted: Your complaint is noted. Under the current permits policy no action follows.
reallife_civic_unsafe_offer: Report this site as unsafe? An inspector will look at it: missing cones or netting, a barrier left flat, an open cover with nothing round it. If you are right the site is stopped for a working day and put right.
reallife_civic_unsafe_right: The inspector agreed with you: the site is stopped until it is made safe, and the contractor has been written to. Thank you for saying something.
reallife_civic_unsafe_wrong: The inspector looked the site over and found it in order. Thank you for the call all the same.
reallife_civic_unsafe_already: You have already reported this site; the inspector has been.
reallife_civic_favour_offer: Call in a fast-track permit for this site? It will then work half as fast again until it is done. You are owed {favours}. The risk, as you were told when you donated: {odds} times in a hundred this becomes a "pay to play" story in the paper.
reallife_civic_favour_done: Done, quietly. The permit office has moved this site to the top of the pile.
reallife_civic_favour_story: The permit went through, and so did a reporter's question about why. It is in the paper. The mayor's approval has taken a knock and so has your day.
reallife_civic_labour_offer: The foreman could use a pair of hands today. Take a day's labouring on this site?
reallife_civic_labour_go: Your hard hat is on the hook by the gate. Get yourself over there.
reallife_civic_labour_no: The foreman has nothing for you right now.

Start a petition for "{policy}"?
It would mean, for you: {effect}.
reallife_civic_petition_started: Your petition for "{policy}" is open, with your own name first. It needs {needed} signatures within two weeks.
reallife_civic_petition_busy: One petition at a time: another is already going round.
reallife_civic_petition_rest: City Hall is not taking new petitions just now (during an election campaign, and for some days after a petition closes).
reallife_civic_petition_in_force: That policy is already in force.
reallife_civic_petition_none: There is no such policy to petition for.
reallife_civic_charge_fine_up: Strict traffic enforcement (city policy): {amount} added to your fine.
reallife_civic_charge_fine_down: A lighter touch on drivers (city policy): {amount} of your fine has been refunded.
reallife_civic_charge_ticket_up: Stiffer parking tickets (city policy): {amount} added to your ticket.
reallife_civic_charge_ticket_down: Cheap parking (city policy): {amount} of your parking ticket has been refunded.
reallife_civic_week_charged: Weekly city account settled: you paid {amount}. The lines are in your transactions; what makes them up is on City Hall's line.
reallife_civic_week_paid: Weekly city account settled: you received {amount}. The lines are in your transactions; what makes them up is on City Hall's line.
