reallife_changes_001: First public release. In it: a camera behind your character and behind the car; cars that drive like their kind; traffic accidents with police, an ambulance and a cordon; street crime, police stops, police stations, custody, courts and prison; driving licences and a driving school; life events; jobs and careers; home life, health and a doctor; people to know, outings and a morning paper; a partner, a wedding and children; buses, the subway as a journey and car ownership; a custom shop, bicycles and motorbikes; hotels and holidays; fires, weather and street events; a city government and building sites; pressure on your businesses; leisure, clothes and photo mode; presets, this Guide, and tools for taking the mod out of a save.
reallife_guide_family_about: A partner who moves in, an engagement and a wedding, children and relatives, lived mostly through your phone.
reallife_guide_family: # A partner - With the social life on, your partner is someone from People: get close to them until they will go out with you. With it off, the Someone special contact has a friend introduce you to someone. Plan evenings out: dinner for two is {family_dinner}. - After {family_move_in_days} days, once you are close enough, ask them to move in from the Family contact. You need a rented flat of {family_sqm} square metres, plus {family_sqm_child} for each child. - At home they stand in the kitchen or the living room, walk between those places, and sit for a minute or two on a chair or a sofa that is free. Face them and the game's panel over them offers Talk on {key_interact}: they get up to talk. Every evening they pay a share of the rent. # Engagement and wedding - A jeweller sells four rings, {family_ring_least} to {family_ring_most}. After {family_propose_days} days together, propose at home or out of doors. - Plan the wedding from the Family contact, or at an event planning agency for {family_planner_fee} more. A venue is {family_venue_least} to {family_venue_most}, of which {family_deposit} is paid as a deposit. Be there between {family_wedding_from}:00 and {family_wedding_to}:00 on the day. A honeymoon is offered afterwards for {family_honeymoon}. If you put it off, ask for it from the Family contact within {family_honeymoon_days} days of the wedding. # Children - Once you live together, talk about children from the Family contact: a pregnancy, or an adoption ({family_adoption_fee} to file). Up to {family_children_most} children. - A scan is {family_scan} and the birth {family_birth}. A month of nursery is {family_nursery} for each child, a nanny {family_nanny}, a private school {family_school}. - A child ages a year every {family_year_weeks} in-game weeks (an option). # Hard times - Chores, arguments, time apart and divorce can be switched off. Counselling is {family_counselling} a session. A divorce settlement is {family_settlement} of your cash, at most {family_settlement_most}. - Your partner hears of every arrest, and of a prison sentence. They take it hard, but it never ends things by itself. While you are locked up, family life waits. # Not shown - Children are never seen as characters: a baby is a cot at home and a pushchair on walks, an older child is messages and appointments. - Your partner sits at home only on a chair, an armchair or a sofa that you have put there and that nobody is using. They never lie down.
reallife_guide_limits:
What is rough, partial or absent in version {version}.

# Little played
- This is the first public release. Courts and prison, the family, buses and two-wheelers have had little or no play from start to finish. If something there goes wrong, see 'Troubleshooting' for how to report it.

# Told, not shown
- The bus ride and the subway journey are a fade to black while time passes. There is no bus or train interior.
- A hotel is a prompt at its door and a panel of choices. Holidays other than the Hamptons weekend are told as messages, one a day.
- On an outing that goes indoors your companion goes in at the door and the screen fades while the time passes. Nobody sits at a table.
- A court hearing and prison are pages of text with choices. Custody, an arrest's or a court's, is served in a police station's holding cell only where the station can be walked into and its room has space for a cell; elsewhere it is a list over a dark screen. A police station can be walked into only where its district has an empty unit for it; elsewhere the front desk answers at the door.
- Life events are text. The people in them do not appear.
- A cooked dish is never an item: you eat one portion when it is done, and leftovers are a count on the cooking list, not something you can take out of the fridge.

# Family
- Children are never seen as characters: a baby is a cot at home and a pushchair on walks, an older child is messages and appointments.
- Your partner sits at home only on a chair, an armchair or a sofa you have put there, and never lies down. In a home with no clear floor they are not shown.
- A wedding is held on the pavement outside the venue, with five guests at most.

# The city
- One incident at a time: no crime starts while an accident, a fire or a street event is on.
- The bus is a minibus. A bus can be late, and a district the roads do not connect may have no route.
- Heat, cold, ice and mist change grip, traffic and energy but have no look of their own.
- The transit policy changes the subway fare but not bus fares, and the night-life policy does not change opening hours.
- Chess is five positions with a choice of moves, not a board you play on.
- Some actions use an animation of the game's own where the mod has none, and can look approximate.

# Vehicles
- The game's own panel still calls a bicycle or a motorbike an electric scooter.
- Parts from the custom shop do not raise what the game pays when you sell the car.
- A car added by another mod gets the performance of the nearest kind of car.

# Work
- A job or a shift in progress does not carry on after a load: you are paid what you were owed when you saved, and the shift is over. A home routine or a leisure activity in progress is simply over, with nothing for the time spent: food that was cooking is used up, and fishing bait and a chess stake are not returned.

# The mod as a whole
- Its models and animations are built for Windows.
- English and Brazilian Portuguese. In any other language the mod is in English.
- While another camera mod drives the camera, this mod's cameras stand aside: the two are never on together.

reallife_guide_trouble_stutter:
# It stutters after a while
- Switch on 'Developer diagnostics' (options page, Diagnostics) and play until it stutters, for ten minutes at least. Once a minute of play the mod then writes a line to Player.log that begins 'Session': how long the frames took, how many took longer than 33 ms and 50 ms, how much memory is in use, and how many things of the mod's are in the city. A frame longer than 80 ms gets a line of its own (12 a minute at most), which says what the mod was doing at the time and where you were (on foot, driving or indoors).
- Send Player.log from that session. Say how long you had played when it began, your processor, graphics card and memory, and which other mods were on.
- To see what the mod adds, play the same save for the same time with the mod switched off under Mods, and say whether it still stutters.
reallife_changes_001_1: Smoother over a long session. The mod's people are now made ready while the city loads, where 0.1.0 made each one in the middle of play, and a passer-by keeps the same look for three outings or ten minutes before it changes. A bus stop is only solid to people on foot while you are on foot within 60 m of it, so driving past stops no longer costs anything; until you walk up, pedestrians may pass through its pole and panels. The first time a kind of worker is wanted, their site can take a few seconds longer to appear. For reports of stutter: with 'Developer diagnostics' on, the mod writes a line a minute to Player.log, and the Guide's Troubleshooting page says what to send. With the Workshop item and a local copy both switched on, the second one now does nothing where it used to run everything twice.
reallife_changes_001_2: The buttons on the options page now say what they do, where they used to read YOUR TEXT HERE, and every slider shows its value.

reallife_guide_planner_about: An app on the phone that lists what you have to do, with reminders and your own notes.
reallife_guide_planner: # What it is - Planner is an app on your phone, beside the game's own. On the phone at the edge of the screen it is on the second page of the home screen: turn the page with the mouse wheel or the dots under the apps. In the phone's full menu it is in the row of apps at the top. - It lists what you have to do: rota shifts, court dates, licence dates, family appointments, plans with friends, a hotel checkout, city events, election day, deadlines at your businesses, the game's tax bill and your own notes. - A feature that is switched off adds nothing to it. # Reading it - Today shows today in time order. Upcoming shows the next {planner_days} days, each under its day. - The last column says where an entry stands: Next, Now, Done, Missed, Over, or Clash when two things you have to attend overlap. - Click a row for its details: when, where, what it costs or pays and what happens if you miss it. Set destination points the game's guide at the place, where the Planner knows it. - A number on the app's button counts what begins within two hours. It goes when you open the app. # Reminders - In an entry's details, choose a reminder: at the time, 1 hour before, or the evening before ({planner_evening}). It arrives as a notification; click it to open the entry. - A reminder is not sent for something that is done, over or gone. One that fell due while time was skipped arrives once, marked late. # Your own notes - New note: pick a title or type one, a day, an hour or all day, and a reminder. Inside a building, This building keeps its address with the note. - A note can be marked as done, edited and deleted. The Planner holds {planner_notes} notes. # Settings - Settings in the app chooses which kinds of entry are shown and the reminder a new note starts with. Times follow the game's own 12 or 24 hour option. - Notes, reminders and these settings are kept with the save.

reallife_changes_001_3: Planner: a new app on the phone that lists what you have to do, with reminders and your own notes. Cooking works: click the cooker at home and choose from the dishes your fridge can make. Coffee, tidying and exercises at home now start when you press Start. Every employer can be applied to by phone. A motorbike needs its own licence. Your partner is someone you have met, and hears when you are arrested. A honeymoon you turned down stays on offer for a while.
reallife_changes_001_4: Buses: nobody waits more than about 20 minutes of the game clock for a bus, and a bus waits at the stop for you instead of leaving after a few seconds. Bus stops are there when you arrive: after loading a save, a taxi ride or the subway, a stop near you is put up at once, and when driving they are put up from further away. The driving school takes its car back: when a lesson or test ends you are asked to step out, and the car can no longer be kept and driven. An officer posted at a junction stands watch and no longer waves at traffic that is following the lights. Bicycles are faster: about 38 km/h for the city bicycle and 50 for the road bicycle.

reallife_guide_nav:
# The minimap
- A small map of the streets around you is on screen while you are out in the city, on foot or driving. It is hidden indoors, on the subway, while the city map or a menu is open, and during scenes that take the screen.
- Under the roads it shows the buildings and the water, in the colours of the game's interface. The city is measured for this once for each version of the game, in the first seconds out in the city, and kept in the mod's folder beside your saves.
- The arrow in the middle is you. The markers are the places the city map marks: your own buildings, the subway stations, the place of a job or a quest, and the places of this mod whose rows are ticked in the city map's list.
- At 100% zoom it shows {nav_view} m of the city from side to side. It shows more while you drive fast.
- It stands at the left of the screen, between the task list and the control hints. When a long task list leaves no room there, it stands beside them at the bottom.

# The GPS
- Set a destination the way the game does it: on a building's card, from a task, or with one of this mod's own destination buttons and map markers. The route appears by itself. A delivery job's destination gets a route as well.
- On the city map, two quick clicks on a spot make that spot your destination.
- The route is the blue line on the minimap and on the city map. Under the minimap is the next turn with its distance, then the distance left and the time on the game's clock at which you should arrive.
- Driving, the route follows the lanes the way traffic may use them. On foot it follows the same streets in either direction. It does not know paths through parks or buildings.
- A street's name comes from the addresses of the buildings along it. Where they do not agree, the turn is given without a name.
- More than {nav_off_car} m from the route in a car, or {nav_off_foot} m on foot, a new route is found from where you are.
- You have arrived within {nav_arrive_car} m of the place in a car, or {nav_arrive_foot} m on foot. The route clears. The destination's marker goes with it.

# Options
- The minimap and the GPS can each be switched off.
- The minimap turns with you or keeps north up. Its size and zoom are sliders.
- Buildings and water on the minimap can be switched off. It then shows roads only.
- If the mod Voogle Route is also switched on, the route is left to it and only the minimap is shown.

reallife_changes_001_6: The rest of the mod's own boxes are replaced by the game's interface. Jobs: every gig and shift has the game's job panel and the game's panel over the place you work at, and most can be left to the game's clock at 85% of the pay. At the drinks cart you take your place by walking behind it, wear a uniform and can call out to passers-by, and carts are solid. The cleaner's spills are all on the floor at once. Shift times show a start and an end. Home: hygiene, stress and home are bars under the game's own, and cooking is a list opened from a cooker or from the fridge's panel. Garage: a repair bay's own panel says what is due and has a Garage button for the service, the custom shop and your vehicles. The Garage key is gone. Hotels, the police station's desk and cell, and the driving school with its theory test use the game's panel and list. The Guide is an app on the phone, and the welcome is a notice. On the map, an unticked row hides its places in the street too.

reallife_guide_taxi: # Calling a taxi - Call City Cabs from your contacts. The dispatcher says how long a taxi will take and what the call-out is. Send one sends it. - The taxi is one of the city's own. It drives to the lane nearest where you stood when you called and stops there, at the kerb where the roadside is free. Click it as you would any taxi: the map opens, you pick where to go and pay the game's fare. - The call-out is {taxi_callout}, or {taxi_callout_night} from {taxi_night_from} to {taxi_night_until}. It is charged when the ride begins, on top of the fare. - In rain or a storm, with Weather affects driving, crime and energy on, the call-out is {taxi_wet_extra} more and the taxi sets out from further off: {taxi_wet_start_least} to {taxi_wet_start_most} m away, where it is {taxi_start_least} to {taxi_start_most} m in the dry. - The minimap marks the taxi while it comes. Call City Cabs again to hear how far it still has to drive. - The taxi waits {taxi_wait} seconds for you, and {taxi_grace} more if you are within {taxi_grace_within} m of it by then. If you are more than {taxi_far} m away when it stops, a notification says so and the game's marker shows where it stands. If you do not get in, it leaves and {taxi_noshow_share} of the call-out is charged. - Cancel it, on a second call, is free while the taxi has more than {taxi_cancel_free} m to drive. Nearer than that it costs {taxi_cancel_share} of the call-out. Getting into a vehicle or another taxi, boarding a bus or the subway, or going indoors while it comes cancels it on the same terms. - The call-out, a cancel and a taxi left standing never take more than the money you have. # Limits - A taxi comes to a street: call on foot, out of doors, within {taxi_road_within} m of a road that cars use. - One taxi at a time. If no taxi is free, or yours gets stuck and no other can be sent, nothing is charged. - The contact is added with The mod's phone contacts on. - A taxi on its way is not kept in a save: after loading, call again.

reallife_guide_economy_about: A credit rating worked out from how you pay, bank terms that follow it, loans from your phone and a Finance app.
reallife_guide_economy: # Your credit rating - One score from {econ_min} to {econ_max}, shown with a grade. A save with no debts and no record starts at {econ_start}. {econ_bands}- It is worked out from what is on your credit file. Nothing in it is left to chance. # The threshold - Under {econ_threshold} no lender lends you anything, on every preset. # What moves it - Payment history, {econ_w_payments}: each daily loan payment taken in full counts for you. One that could not be taken counts against you as much as {econ_miss_weight} paid ones. Both count less each day and stop after {econ_fade_days} days. - What you owe, {econ_w_owed}: your loans against what the city's banks would lend on their own terms, and your daily payments against your daily income. - Length of credit history, {econ_w_length}: it counts in full after {econ_history_days} days. - Legal and public record, {econ_w_legal}: a conviction, a civil judgment, a fine or court debt still owed, each day one could not be taken, and recent entries on your police record. - Recent applications, {econ_w_applications}: each loan you take out counts against you a little for {econ_application_days} days. # What lenders offer - At {econ_threshold} a bank lends {econ_cap_low} of its usual limit at its usual rate plus {econ_rate_low} points. From {econ_best_from} it lends {econ_cap_high} of its limit at its rate less {econ_rate_high} points. Between the two the terms move in a straight line. A rate is never under {econ_rate_floor}. - The terms are the same at the counter, on a call to the bank and in the Finance app. - While the tutorial's first loan or the bankruptcy quest's emergency loan is open, the banks keep their own terms. # Finance - Finance is an app on your phone, beside the game's own. - Overview: cash, what you owe, your daily costs, net worth and your rating. - Credit: the score, how each part stands, what would raise it most, and the last {econ_events_shown} entries on your file. - Borrow: each bank's offer today. Pick one, choose an amount from {econ_loan_least} up, read what it costs, and apply. A loan by phone costs an arrangement fee of {econ_fee} of the amount, at least {econ_fee_least}. A bank in person charges none. - Cash flow: money in and out for yesterday, the last {econ_week} days or the last {econ_month}, with the {econ_top} largest items. - A loan from the phone is an ordinary bank loan. Repay it, or change its daily payment, in EconoView. - A number on the app's button means a payment was missed or your grade changed. It goes when you open the app. # More kinds of credit - They are in Finance, under Borrow, below the banks. Under {econ_threshold} none is opened and nothing can be drawn. What you already owe stays owed. - Overdraft: a limit from {econ_od_low} to {econ_od_high} of what the city's banks would lend you, at least {econ_od_least}. If your cash is short of what leaves at midnight, it pays the difference. What is drawn costs the bank's rate for your rating plus {econ_od_points} points a year. Cash above {econ_od_float} pays it back each night. It is free to hold. - Credit card: a limit from {econ_card_low} to {econ_card_high}, at least {econ_card_least}. Drawing cash costs {econ_card_fee}, at least {econ_card_fee_least}. A statement comes every {econ_card_days} days. {econ_card_grace} days later the minimum is taken: {econ_card_min} of the statement, at least {econ_card_min_least}. What you carry over costs the bank's rate plus {econ_card_points} points. A statement paid in full costs no interest. - Business loan: an ordinary bank loan against one of your businesses that has {econ_biz_days} days of takings on record. Up to {econ_biz_multiple} times its average daily profit, at the bank's rate less {econ_biz_points} point. It does not use up what the bank lends you otherwise. EconoView lists it with your other loans. - Car finance: get approved in Finance, then buy a vehicle the usual way. The approval lasts to the end of the day after ({econ_approval_days} day on). The game asks for the whole price in cash, so the approved amount is paid into your cash first. The lender finances the price less your deposit of {econ_car_dep_low} to {econ_car_dep_high}, over {econ_car_term_low} to {econ_car_term_high} days, at the bank's rate plus {econ_car_points} points. What is not used goes back, and all of it if you buy nothing. - Mortgage: the same for a building you buy in BizMan. Deposit {econ_home_dep_low} to {econ_home_dep_high}, {econ_home_term_low} to {econ_home_term_high} days, the bank's rate less {econ_home_points} point, and up to {econ_home_multiple} times what the bank would lend you otherwise. - Consolidate: one new bank loan pays off every loan, your card and your overdraft. The fee is {econ_cons_fee} of what you owe, at least {econ_cons_fee_least}. Finance shows the daily cost, the interest and the days before and after. - Accounts in Finance lists every debt and how it stands. Pay any amount into an account there at any time. Paying early costs nothing. - At midnight the game takes its own loans first. Your other accounts follow. # If you do not pay - Each debt counts the payments missed in a row. A payment made in full puts the count back to nothing. The misses stay on your credit file. {econ_ladder}- The late fee is {econ_late_share} of the payment, at least {econ_late_least}. The penalty rate is {econ_penalty_points} points a year and ends after {econ_penalty_run} payments in a row. - The collections call: pay what is overdue, or spread it over {econ_plan_days} days on top of your payments. One plan per debt. A plan that is broken goes straight to the next step. - A vehicle on finance is taken when you are not in it or near it, and sold for {econ_repo_share} of its price. What is left is still owed, and goes to court if it stands for {econ_unsecured_days} days. A business loan takes {econ_divert} of that business's daily takings until the arrears are paid. A mortgage takes the building's rents. Your home, your businesses and your buildings are not taken. - A court claim is for the balance and the lender's costs: {econ_claim_costs}, at least {econ_claim_costs_least}. It is in your Legal file, where you settle or contest it. - The option How hard not paying hits sets how far this goes, and the presets set the option. Being refused credit does not depend on it. # The private lender - When a bank has refused you, or your rating is under {econ_threshold}, a private lender sends you a text. It becomes a contact on your phone. - It lends {econ_shark_least} to {econ_shark_most}, or up to {econ_shark_days} days of your average income if that is more. Each day adds {econ_shark_rate} of the sum. All of it is due in {econ_shark_due} days. One extension by the same time costs {econ_shark_extend} of what you owe. - What you owe never passes {econ_shark_cap} times the sum. - It is not on your credit file. Paying it does not raise your rating. - If you do not pay: a warning {econ_shark_warn} day late. {econ_shark_assault} days late you are set upon in the street, if you are on foot, and the cash on you is taken against the debt. {econ_shark_damage} days late one of your businesses is damaged, a repair bill of {econ_shark_bill_low} to {econ_shark_bill_high}. Then one or the other again every {econ_shark_repeat} days. On Relaxed there are only warnings. - Nothing happens while you are in custody, in hospital, away on a trip or in the middle of something else. # Ways out of debt - Debt advice is a free contact, offered when something has been overdue for {econ_advice_days} days or a lender has filed a claim. The ways out are in Finance, under Accounts. - Sell and settle: Finance shows your cash, your investments and what your vehicles and property cost. Selling is up to you. - A debt arrangement: every loan and every unsecured account stands still, with no interest, no fees and no further steps. You pay {econ_arr_share} of your average daily income each day, at least {econ_arr_least}, until it is cleared. Your rating is held at {econ_arr_cap} or under while it runs and for {econ_arr_after} days after. Missing {econ_arr_misses} payments ends it. The private lender is not part of it. - Bankruptcy: every loan, the card, the overdraft, car finance and what you owe the private lender are written off. A vehicle on finance goes back. Cash above {econ_bank_keep} goes to the creditors. A mortgage, fines and court debts stay. Your rating goes to {econ_bank_score}, nobody lends for {econ_bank_days} days, and then it rebuilds from {econ_bank_from} by up to {econ_bank_per_day} points a day. Once in {econ_bank_every} days. While the game's own bankruptcy quest is running, use that. # Known limits - The game takes the whole price of a vehicle or a building from your cash, so finance is paid into your cash before you buy. - Nobody walks up to you for the private lender. You are told what happened. - A building is never taken for a mortgage, and a business is never taken for a business loan. - The mod's own accounts do not exist without the mod. "Prepare this save for removing the mod" pays them from your cash as far as it goes and forgives the rest. The game's loans stay, on their own terms.

reallife_text_debt_advice_welcome: Debt advice: this service is free. Call to hear the ways out of debt, with your own figures.

reallife_collect_no_cash: You do not have {amount} in cash. Call back when you do, or ask for a plan.
reallife_collect_plan_agreed: Agreed. {amount} is spread over {days} days: {payment} a day on top of your normal payment. If a day is missed, the plan is off and the matter goes further.
reallife_collect_plan_used: This account has already had its plan. There is no second one.

reallife_lender_lent: {amount} is yours. {back} on day {day}. Do not be late.
reallife_lender_status: You owe {amount}. It is due on day {day}. Each day adds {perDay}, up to {cap}.
reallife_lender_status_late: You owe {amount}. It was due on day {day}. Each day adds {perDay}, up to {cap}. I am not waiting much longer.
reallife_lender_extended: More time, once. It costs you {fee}. You owe {amount} now, on day {day}.
reallife_lender_no_extension: You have had your extra time. Pay.
reallife_text_shark_intro: Heard the banks turned you down. I lend from {least} to {most}, today, no forms. Call this number if you want it.
reallife_text_shark_due: Today is the day. {amount}. Call me.
reallife_text_shark_warn: You are {days} day(s) late with {amount}. Pay, or this gets unpleasant.

reallife_econ_note_shark_damage: {business} was damaged in the night. The repairs cost {amount}. The private lender is still waiting for its money.
reallife_advice_closed: Debt advice. We cannot see your accounts at the moment. Please call again later.
reallife_advice_nothing: Debt advice. You owe nothing, so there is nothing to advise. Goodbye.

reallife_advice_arrange_page: A debt arrangement: your loans and unsecured accounts, {amount} in all, stand still. No interest, no fees, no further steps. reallife_advice_arrange_none: You have no loan and no unsecured account for an arrangement to cover.

reallife_changes_002_0: Money and credit: you have a credit rating from 300 to 850, worked out from how you pay. Under 580 no bank lends. A Finance app on the phone shows your money, your rating and your cash flow, and lets you borrow without going to the bank. There is an overdraft, a credit card, a business loan, car finance and a mortgage, real consequences for not paying, a lender of last resort, and ways out of debt. Getting around: call City Cabs for a taxi to where you are. Every bus stop now stands all the time, and where a street has room a bus pulls into a marked bay so traffic passes it. The bus countdown shows how long the bus will really take. Work: gigs pay about 2.8 times what they did and no two shifts are alike. Cleaning uses the game's own mop and dirt, to 100%. A shift in progress is paid out when a save is loaded. Life: a court's custody is served in the station's cell. Your partner sits down at home, and you can sit on a bench on a walk. More goes on in the street. Family, courts, friends, leisure, the council and the dispatch desk now use the game's own interface. Fixed: hotel reception closed as soon as it opened.

reallife_guide_economy_city: # What it is - The city has an economy of its own. A central bank sets a rate, prices rise or fall, the economy has good and bad times, each district has an income level and wholesale prices move. - It runs while Credit rating and phone loans is on. Switch The city's economy off in the options and every figure is the game's own again. - It is worked out by rule from a number drawn once for your save. - A month is a twelfth of the game's year, {macro_month_least} days at least. # The bank rate - The central bank decides once a month. The paper prints the decision the day before it takes effect. - Its rate is counted in points on top of the banks' own rates, from {macro_base_low} points under them to {macro_base_high} points over. One decision moves it by {macro_move_most} point at most. - It raises the rate when prices rise faster than {macro_target} a year and cuts it when they rise more slowly. A slowdown or a recession makes it cut. With nothing pressing it goes back towards the banks' own rates. - Every bank's offer carries the rate, at the counter and in Finance. A loan or a purchase on finance you already have keeps its rate. An overdraft and a card follow the rate from day to day. # Prices - A price index starts at 100. Each month it moves by a twelfth of the year's inflation, which stays between minus {macro_inflation_low} and {macro_inflation_high} a year. - Rents and wages follow the index, and so do the game's own shops and services at prices of its own: tickets and rides, the hospital and the doctor, gyms, shopping, fit-outs, training and hiring. Each night, after the game has taken rent and paid wages, one line each adjusts them by how far the index is from 100. Every price of the mod's (fares, fines, fees, pay, family costs, trips) is at the same index. Nothing moves while the index is within {macro_adjust_band}% of 100. - Takings follow the index too, and what customers spend in good and bad times. One line a night adjusts the day's takings. - An adjustment never takes more than the cash you have. What cannot be taken is carried to the next day at no cost. - The lines are in Finance under Cash flow and in EconoView, each under its own name. # Good and bad times - The economy is in a boom, steady, in a slowdown or in a recession. A state lasts {macro_state_least} to {macro_state_most} months. The first {macro_opening} months of the economy in a save are steady. - Against a steady economy, at Standard: {macro_states}- With Business events on, rivals undercut more often in a slowdown or a recession, and business troubles come up more often. In a boom they come up less often. # Districts - Each district has an income level from {macro_income_low} to {macro_income_high}, started from the game's own shares of working, middle and upper class there. It drifts a little each month and never moves more than {macro_income_band} points from where it started. - A business gains or loses a tenth of a per cent of its customers for each point its district is over or under 100. - A district bears prices by its income and by the state of the economy. The measure is the game's own price for a product in that district. Up to {macro_over_band}% over what the district bears costs nothing. Past that a business loses {macro_over_loss}% of its customers for each per cent over, {macro_over_most}% at most. At or under what the district bears it gains {macro_under_gain}%. - District, economy and prices together never change a business's customers by more than {macro_footfall_low}% down or {macro_footfall_high}% up. They are worked out each morning. # Wholesale prices - Goods are of six kinds. Each kind's wholesale and import price moves with the season, the weather, what is on in the city and the price index. - Now and then a kind is short or in glut for {macro_shock_days_low} to {macro_shock_days_high} days. The paper says so the day before. Supply alone never takes a kind's price more than {macro_factor_high}% over or {macro_factor_low}% under the usual. # Rivals - A business that has made a profit every day for {macro_copycat_days} days may draw a rival who opens nearby and undercuts it. It is the Business desk's own competitor story with the same answers. It needs Business events switched on and comes at most once in {macro_copycat_rest} days. # What you can do - Read The city in Finance, opened from Overview. It lists the rate, prices, each district, each kind of goods, each of your businesses and what your buildings are worth today. - Borrow before a rise and after a cut. Pay down an overdraft or a card when the rate climbs. - Stock up before a shortage and wait out a glut. - Price for the district. The page marks a business whose prices are over what its district bears. # Strength - How far the economy swings follows the presets. Relaxed swings {macro_swing_relaxed} as far as Standard and never has a recession. Realistic swings {macro_swing_realistic} as far and Hardcore {macro_swing_hardcore}.

reallife_guide_ventures:
# An offer comes to you
- Once every {ven_offer_every} days a tycoon may make an offer for a business that made a profit on {ven_profit_days} of its last {ven_window} days and at least {ven_profit_floor} a day over its last {ven_average_days} days. The chance is {ven_offer_chance}, or {ven_offer_liked} if they like its sector.
- They value the business at {ven_value_days} days of that profit and offer money for a share of each day's profit. The offer waits {ven_lapse_days} days in the Ventures app.
- You can accept, refuse or counter once: {ven_counter_money} more money, or a share {ven_counter_share} smaller. They agree, meet you half way or hold to their terms.

# Going to an investor
- In Ventures, Raise money: pick a business you run, or the kind of business you mean to open and what it will cost, then an investor. Angels back young businesses with small sums. Tycoons and venture firms put in large ones.
- The meeting has {ven_questions_least} to {ven_questions_most} questions from a list of {ven_bank}: figures they can check, your plan, and you. Each answer scores up to {ven_points} points.
- A true figure always scores at least {ven_truth_base}. A figure made to sound better scores as if it were true, unless it is caught. The chance of that is the investor's care with figures times {ven_catch_little} for a figure a little better and {ven_catch_much} for one much better.
- A caught figure ends the meeting. That investor will not see you for {ven_caught_days} days and your name with every investor falls by {ven_caught_name} of 100.
- Answers about the plan have no single right list: each investor wants something different. Answers about you are checked against your businesses, your jobs, your credit file and your record.
- An angel invests from a score of {ven_need_angel} of 100, a tycoon from {ven_need_tycoon}, a venture firm from {ven_need_firm}. The better the score, the more they pay ({ven_pitch_days_least} to {ven_pitch_days_most} days of profit) and the smaller their share.
- For a business not yet open an angel or a venture firm puts in {ven_budget_least} to {ven_budget_most} of its budget, paid when you open one within {ven_pledge_days} days. If you do not, nothing is owed. A tycoon only backs a business that is open.
- An angel backs a business under {ven_young_days} days old with their smallest sum even if it shows no profit.
- One approach to an investor every {ven_cooldown} days.

# What a deal costs you
- Each night the investor takes their share of that day's profit of the business. On a day of loss they take nothing.
- Investors together never take more than {ven_share_cap} of one business's profit.
- They set a target for the recent daily profit. Meet it and they are pleased and may offer a second round. Miss it and you are warned. Miss it again and they make a demand, to be answered within {ven_demand_days} days: a seat on the board ({ven_board_extra} more of the profit for {ven_board_days} days), or a promise to cut daily costs by {ven_cut} within {ven_cut_days} days.
- After a third miss a demanding investor calls their money back: what they put in less {ven_call_kept} of what you have paid them, {ven_call_least} of what they put in at least, paid by the day. After {ven_call_misses} payments missed running the debt goes to court as a civil claim.
- Other investors lose interest after a third miss: they keep taking their share and set no more targets. One who has not had their money back by then will not back you again, and your name with every investor falls by {ven_cold_name} of 100.
- An investor who has had their money back and sees a target met sets no more targets.
{ven_levels}- You can buy an investor out at any time: their share of {ven_buy_out_days} days of recent profit, and never less than {ven_buy_out_floor} of what they put in.
- If you sell or close the business, each investor is owed what they put in less what they have been paid, by the day.

# The stock market
- {ven_companies} companies of the city are listed, the game's own rivals among them. Prices move once a day at midnight: by chance, and by the day's weather, city events, crime and accidents in the paper, council decisions, election results and a rival's moves.
- One day's news moves a company by {ven_news_cap} at most. The Market tab shows each price, its last move and its move over {ven_history} days.
- Every purchase and sale costs {ven_commission} in commission, {ven_commission_least} at least. You can hold {ven_holding} shares of one company.
- Dividends are paid every {ven_dividend_days} market days: {ven_dividend_least} to {ven_dividend_most} of the price, by company.
- Shares can lose value. In the mod's own tests, every company bought and held for ten game years of 60 days returned about 5% a year.
- The game's own investment funds in EconoView are separate: a fund follows its own yearly rate, while a share is one company whose price moves every day.

# Property
- The game already lets the buildings you own. The Property tab shows what each cost, the rent it has brought in, its yield and any mortgage on it. Rents are set in BizMan.

reallife_guide_economy_company: # What it is - Running a business adds what the game leaves out: staff who know the going rate, insurance, campaigns you can measure, a return to file, an accountant, and licences. - It runs while Credit rating and phone loans is on. Each part has its own switch in the options. Off, a part charges nothing and does nothing. - Everything is in the Company app on the phone. The Planner lists what is due, and a business that lost money {co_loss_days} days running. - Every charge is a line of its own in EconoView and in Finance. The game's own wages, tax and marketing are not changed. - Premiums, campaign costs, licence fees and the accountant's fee are given here at a price index of 100. With the city's economy on they follow prices. Penalties, excesses and the most a claim counts are fixed sums. # Staff - The going rate for a job is the game's own wage for that skill, moved by the economy and by the district's income (between {co_market_low}% and {co_market_high}% of it), at today's prices. What staff are paid is counted the same way: the game's wage at today's prices, as the city's cost of living pays it, and any raise you agreed on top. Rising prices make nobody underpaid by themselves. - Only staff at a business that takes money are counted. - At Standard, somebody paid {co_raise_gap}% or more under the going rate for {co_raise_days} days asks for a raise. You have {co_answer_days} days to answer. No answer counts as a refusal. They do not ask again for {co_raise_rest} days. - Agree and they are paid the going rate. Offer less and they get half of what they asked. Refuse and they get nothing. - A raise is paid as a line of its own, Wages, agreed raise, for the hours the game counted. The wage in the game's own staff app does not change. - Standing is this mod's own figure from 0 to 100. It stands beside the game's satisfaction, which is not changed. It starts at {co_stand_start}. Each day underpaid costs a point. Paid fairly it climbs back to {co_stand_calm}. Agreeing adds {co_stand_agree}, offering less takes {co_stand_less} and refusing takes {co_stand_refuse}. - A rival may make an offer to somebody with a skill of {co_poach_skill} or more who is {co_poach_gap}% or more under the going rate. The offer is the going rate and {co_poach_premium}% more. Match it within {co_poach_answer} days or they leave {co_poach_notice} days later, by the game's own resignation. - When {co_strike_share}% of a business's staff stand at {co_strike_standing} or lower they call a strike for the next day. {co_strike_footfall}% of customers stay away while it lasts, and with Business events on the doors are shut for {co_strike_hours} hours each morning. No new strike comes for {co_strike_rest} days afterwards. - End a strike with a raise for all, with one payment of {co_strike_pay_hours} hours' pay each, or sit it out. - When trade is brisk the staff may offer overtime: {co_ot_hours} extra hours a day each at time and a half for {co_ot_days} days, for {co_ot_footfall}% more customers. - The game decides who is off sick and pays them nothing. Your sick pay policy pays nothing, half a day's pay or all of it (half to begin with), and changes their standing by {co_sick_none}, {co_sick_statutory} or {co_sick_generous} a sick day. - By strictness: {co_levels} # Insurance - A policy covers one business against one thing: a fire's repair bill, the stock and repair of a break-in, or a fine from a health or fire safety inspection. - The loss still happens in full, as before. Put the claim in within {co_claim_window} days and the insurer pays it back less the excess. - The premium leaves each night and is fixed for a term of one game year. It is worked out from the kind of cover: {co_covers}- And from the insurer: {co_insurers}- Theft cover is dearer in a poor district. Fire and liability cover are dearer in a rich one. - A claim adds {co_claim_loading}% to the next term's premium. An insurer that declines to renew will not write that cover there again. - A policy lapses when its premium cannot be paid {co_premium_missed} days running. A business may stay uninsured. # Marketing {co_campaigns}- A campaign runs from the day after you book it, one at a time for each business. - It is stronger where the district suits the business and in a boom, and weaker in a recession. The same kind again within {co_repeat_days} days is weaker. No campaign adds more than {co_campaign_most}%. - The customers come through the same figure the game's own marketing uses, on top of it. Together with the city's economy it stays inside what Business events allows, so a campaign in a boom may add less than its figure. - The morning after it ends you get a report: customers, takings and profit on its days against the same number of days before, the cost, the extra profit and the return. The last {co_reports} reports are kept. - The game's own marketing through an agency is a daily budget with no end and no report. It is unchanged, and the two add up. # Tax - The game's own tax is unchanged: once a year, on what your businesses sold, less deductible expenses, if the year's income passes its threshold. - Premiums, campaigns, agreed raises, sick pay, overtime, licence fees and the accountant's fee are marked deductible when they are paid, so the game's tax deducts them itself. - A quarter is three months. When it closes you have {co_return_days} days to file its return in the Company app. It is one button, once the game's own tax bill is not overdue. - A late return costs {co_penalty_share}% of the quarter's takings, between {co_penalty_least} and {co_penalty_most}, and the same again after each further {co_penalty_repeat} days, {co_penalties_most} times at most. {co_late_audit} late returns running bring a tax audit from Business events. - An accountant files the return on the day the quarter closes: {co_accountants}- About {co_error_chance}% of the cheapest one's returns carry an error that costs half a late penalty. # Cash off the books - For each business you may keep {co_hide_steps}% of takings off the books. The tax that share would bear is paid to you each morning. While the year's income is under the game's tax threshold no tax is due and nothing is paid. - Each per cent hidden adds {co_risk_per} points a day to the chance of an audit, up to {co_risk_most}% a day. With nothing hidden it falls by {co_risk_decay} a day. - An audit takes back everything kept back since the last one, with a fine on top: {co_fines}. From {co_court} of back-tax you are also summoned to court for tax evasion, which the credit rating counts as any conviction. - On Relaxed the most is {co_hide_relaxed}% and it never goes to court. - With cash off the books the dearest accountant resigns, the middle one will not file, and the cheapest charges {co_hide_fee}% more. # Licences {co_licences}- Every business needs signage. Food hygiene is for a business that sells food, alcohol for one that sells drink, and late opening for one open past {co_late_hour}:00 or before {co_early_hour}:00 on any day. - A business that already ran when this first appeared in your save holds every licence it needs for a first term, free. A business you open later may trade {co_lic_grace} days before it needs them. - A reminder comes {co_lic_remind} days before one runs out. Each can be set to renew by itself. - Trading without one costs {co_lic_fine} times its fee when an inspector next calls, and for food hygiene or alcohol the doors are shut for {co_lic_hours} hours. Inspectors come from Business events.

reallife_changes_002_1: The city now has an economy of its own. A central bank sets a rate each month, and bank offers, overdrafts and cards follow it. Prices rise or fall, and rents, wages, wholesale prices and takings follow them. There are booms, slowdowns and recessions that change how many customers come and what they spend. Each district has an income level that sets what its customers will pay. Wholesale prices move with the season, the weather and what is on in the city, and the paper announces a shortage or a glut the day before. Finance has a page for all of it, The city. Investors: a tycoon may offer money for a business that does well, and you can pitch to angel investors, tycoons and venture firms yourself. They ask questions, check your figures and take a share of the profit each day. There is a stock market of the city's companies, moved by the day's news. Both are in a new Ventures app, with what your buildings earn. Running a business has an app of its own, Company. Staff have a going rate by job and district: they ask for raises, get offers from rivals and may strike. Each business can be insured against fire, theft and an inspector's fine. Campaigns have a cost, an end and a report of what they brought. A return is filed each quarter, an accountant can file it and find savings, and cash kept off the books saves tax until an audit finds it. Businesses need licences that cost money and run out. The Planner lists what is due.

reallife_guide_economy_rota: # What it is - The Rota tab of the Company app plans the staff of every business you run. It runs while Running a business is on. - The customers are the game's own forecast for each hour of the week, with the business's promotion, satisfaction and marketing in it. A campaign, overtime or a strike of this mod counts on the days it runs. - Nothing is written until you press a button. Only your choice between staff first and lean is kept in the save. # Forecast and opening hours - What a customer brings is taken from the business's books of the last {rota_books_days} days: the takings and the cost of the goods. With fewer than {rota_books_customers} customers on the books it is worked out from what is on sale and its prices, and the page says so. - An hour is worth opening when its customers bring more than the wages of the staff it takes. At a cinema or a theatre the day's licensing fee has to be earned as well. - Opening hours are advised as at most {rota_blocks} blocks a day of at least {rota_block_hours} hours each. - The game sells only at a till with somebody at it. An hour open with nobody there sells nothing, and the game's thieves still come. - While licences are on and the business holds no late opening permit, the hours from {rota_late_hour}:00 on and before {rota_early_hour}:00 are left out of the advice. The page says what the permit would add. - A campaign, a strike or a trouble of business pressure that ends or begins within the week is counted on its own days only. - A headquarters keeps the game's office hours. Where no customers come, the rota covers the hours you keep. A warehouse has no rota: the game gives its drivers their vehicles. # The plans - Each business has a ladder of plans. As it is is the week you have. Best with the people you have is never worse than that: it is the better of a new rota for your hours, your hours without those nobody can keep, and the hours that pay as far as your people can keep them. - Each further plan hires one more person, at the going wage, for the group of stations where that adds most. It is shown only if it adds at least {rota_share_least} per cent and at least {rota_gain_least} a week. The plans stop at the first hire that does not, and never go past {rota_hires_most} hires. - Every plan is valued the same way: what customers served leave, less wages, licensing fees, the game's hourly theft, the risk of a break-in on a night shut, and what unmet demands cost. - An unmet demand takes satisfaction away every hour. At nothing the employee resigns. The planner counts the sales lost while the post stands empty for {rota_replace_days} days, and the worse work on the way. - The hours a week somebody asks for are compulsory at both ends, part-time and full-time alike: in every rota the planner writes they work no fewer than the least and no more than the most. The figures are the game's own for each demand. - Shifts follow the customers. The busiest hours are staffed first, a second till where one cannot serve everybody, and extra hours go to the next busiest. Cleaning is one shift a day around the busy hours. - Where the hours you keep cannot hold everybody's least hours, the plan with the people you have opens the best paying hours beside them until they do, and says which and for whom. Where no hours within the rules can, the person is named with the figures and given no hours rather than too few. - Staff first lets nothing your people ask for give way. Lean lets their other demands of low and medium priority give way to an hour that pays. Left alone, the planner takes whichever comes to more. Your choice is kept for each business. - A plan for the people you have can be written with Use this plan. A plan that takes a hire cannot be written until you have hired: its page says who to look for and what they cost. - Goods are counted where a Delivery Contract or a Logistics Manager brings them. Customers buy a product only while some is on site. The shelves fill again from storage the moment they run empty, a contract delivers at 8 on a Monday, a Logistics Manager tops up at 2 every morning, and a delivery that finds no room goes back. - From the hour a product runs out, a plan counts no sales of it. The page names the goods that run out, when, and what would keep them on the shelves. An Urgent Order is a delivery once, so the plans count a week without it. Goods nothing brings are taken to be restocked by you, and the page says how long they last. # Staff and stations - A till or a service station serves as many customers an hour as the game gives it. A further one is advised only when the customers it adds pay its wage. - A till serves the same number of customers an hour whatever the skill of whoever stands at it. Skill and satisfaction change how well each customer is served. - Cleaning is counted from the dirt each customer brings and from what a cleaner clears in an hour. The week is run hour by hour, and cleaning hours are put where they bring most: cleanliness is a quarter of the satisfaction that decides how much customers buy. - Where the cleaning service of this mod cleans a business, no cleaning shift is planned there. - People to hire are counted at the hours a week each employee's own demand allows, {rota_week} with none. - Where the customers outnumber what the stations can serve, the page says what one more station would serve. # The rota - Fill the rota writes shifts for the hours the business keeps. Use this plan sets that plan's hours first, after telling you the hours open now and after. The game asks before a rota is written over. - No shift is longer than {rota_shift} hours and nobody works more than {rota_day} hours in a day. Nobody is put at a station they have no skill for. - Demands about hours a week, days a week, free days, times of day, cleaning shifts and stations are kept. If hours stay uncovered, demands of low and medium priority give way where that covers them. Demands of high priority never do. The page lists what could not be met and why. - Delivery drivers are left as they are. So is whoever has a desk at a headquarters: only empty desks are filled, so nobody loses the plan the game ties to a desk. - A business with more than {rota_stations_most} stations or {rota_staff_most} staff is not planned, and nothing of its rota is touched. - Put the old rota back restores the opening hours and every shift as they were. It is there until you close the Company app. - A large business is worked out over a few frames. The page says so while it lasts. - The Planner lists a business that is open with nobody at work. - The sums shown are estimates after wages. Rent and other costs are not in them.

reallife_guide_economy_online: # What it is - The Web shop app on the phone opens an online shop for any business you run that takes money, and for a warehouse. It runs while the credit rating does. - Orders come from every district of the city, not from the street outside. The goods are the real stock of the place: every unit sold leaves its storage or its shelves, and you restock as you always do. - You can have {online_shops} online shops, each with up to {online_lines} products. # Setting up - Pick a business in the Shops tab and choose a site. The set-up is paid once and has the first month of hosting in it. Hosting is then taken every month. {online_sites}- If you run a web development agency, your own people build the site: the set-up is {online_agency} cheaper and the shop takes {online_agency_orders} more orders. - Everything the place has in stock goes on the online shop at the shop's own prices. The Catalogue tab takes products off, puts them on and prices them. - If the hosting cannot be paid the site goes offline and takes no orders until it is. # Orders - How many come follows the game's own demand for your products across all districts, the width of the catalogue, your prices, the promise, the rating, marketing, the economy and the season. Most come in the evening. - A price under the going price sells more and one over it sells less, by the square of the difference. At {online_price_ceiling} over the going price nobody orders. - A same-day promise brings {online_same_day} more orders. An order before {online_cutoff}:00 is then due {online_same_hours} hours later, and a later one by {online_next_morning}:00 the next day. A next-day promise is due by {online_next_hour}:00 the next day. - Each further online shop of yours shares the city's orders with the others. - An order is one to three products for one district. # Picking - Orders are picked by staff with the customer service skill during their shifts, {online_pick} orders an hour each. At a warehouse the delivery drivers pick, between {online_warehouse_from}:00 and {online_warehouse_until}:00. - What is not in stock is left out of the order. An order with nothing in stock is cancelled. - With nobody on shift orders wait. A customer gives up {online_wait} hours after the promise. The Planner says so after {online_idle} hours of orders waiting. # Delivery - Your own vans: every van at one of your warehouses with a driver takes rounds between {online_drive_from}:00 and {online_drive_until}:00, one district at a time, as many parcels as it holds. A driver works {online_driver_hours} hours a day, as the game pays them. A round costs {online_van_km} a kilometre. - A courier: collects within the hour and delivers {online_courier_hours} hours later or more by distance, for {online_courier_base} a parcel and {online_courier_km} a kilometre. - A late order has {online_late_refund} of its value refunded. An order packed for a van that none took is refunded in full {online_missing_hours} hours after its promise. # Rating and returns - Every order moves the rating: up for on time and complete, down for short, late, cancelled or lost. Dear prices pull it down and cheap ones lift it. One order moves it {online_rating_move} of a star at most. - At one star a shop takes {online_stars_low} of its orders, at five stars {online_stars_high}. - Some delivered orders come back after {online_return_days} days and are refunded. How many depends on the goods: {online_returns} # Money - A day's takings, refunds and delivery costs are booked when the day ends, each as its own entry in EconoView. Costs are tax deductible. - Online sales are added to the business's daily statement, so the game's tax and your quarterly return count them as the business's takings. - Advertising online costs {online_ad_cost} for {online_ad_days} days and adds about {online_ad_percent}% to the orders. A campaign you run at the business itself helps by half its effect. # Tests - The options page has six test buttons under Troubleshooting, in Test tools. A test order is picked from your real stock and its money really moves. # Known limits - You cannot deliver the orders yourself. - A van's round starts at the business even when the van belongs to a warehouse elsewhere.

reallife_guide_streets_about: People answer your horn, and accidents come from drivers you can watch go wrong.
reallife_guide_streets:
# The horn
- Sound the horn while driving and the people within about {horn_reach} m ahead of the car, or close beside it, react. At most {horn_most} do.
- Somebody in your way who should not be there breaks into a jog and clears the road, or steps back to the kerb. Some lift a hand in apology.
- If your light is red, or they are on a crossing with the light in their favour, they stop, turn to you and glare, then cross at their own pace. A second and a third blast make it longer, and people on the pavement join in.
- People on the pavement may look round.
- Three such blasts in a minute with a police officer or a parked patrol car within {horn_officer} m earn a warning. After a warning the next one costs {horn_fine}.
# Reckless drivers
- Now and then an ordinary car near you is driven badly for {reckless_least} to {reckless_most} seconds: a speeder, a driver who runs a red light, one who brakes late, or at night a drunk who wanders in the lane.
- Most get away with it. Some have a near miss, with horns and people jumping clear.
- If the car meets another, the accident is where it happened. How bad it is follows from the speed they met at: under {crash_minor} km/h a bump, from {crash_severe} km/h a serious crash.
- If it runs somebody down, the driver stops and waits for the police, or drives off and is chased.
- A patrol car that sees a speeder or a red-light runner pulls the driver over, or chases one who will not stop.
- Sometimes a pedestrian steps into the road in front of a car. Usually the driver brakes in time.
- If a reckless driver runs into your car, it is their fault and you pay nothing for it.
- 'How often accidents happen' sets how often all of this happens. With 'Reckless drivers cause the accidents' off, accidents are set up out of view as before.
# People in the road
- With 'Traffic brakes for people in the road' on, a traffic car brakes for anybody in its way, waits while they are there and drives on when they have gone. The cars behind it queue.
- A driver sounds the horn at somebody who steps out close, and again every {solid_horn} seconds at somebody who stands in front of the stopped car. People answer it as they answer your horn.
- Somebody about to step out in front of a car that could not stop waits at the kerb.
- No car is held for long. After {solid_hold} seconds the person is moved on.
- A car touches somebody only at walking pace: they shout at it and nobody falls. The one exception is an accident that is due. Then a driver who cannot stop hits them at the speed that is left, and stops or drives off as a reckless driver does.
- People do not fade out beside a car that is braking for them.
- With the option off, traffic drives through people as it does in the game.

reallife_guide_roommates_about: Somebody to share your flat and the rent, found by a notice or among your friends, with the frictions and comforts of living together.
reallife_guide_roommates: # Finding one - You need a home and somewhere for them to sleep: a second bed, or at least a sofa. Somebody on a sofa pays {rm_sofa} of the share they would pay for a bed. With your partner living in, it has to be a second bed. - Ring the Roommate contact on your phone. Put up a notice costs {rm_fee} and stays up for {rm_ad_days} days. Between {rm_least} and {rm_most} people answer by text over the next day or two. - Ring the contact again to read about each of them: their job and hours, the share of the rent they offer (between {rm_share_least} and {rm_share_most}) and the one thing you can tell about them. Offer the room and they move in that day. You can also take the notice down and choose nobody. - Ask a friend offers the room to a friend from your social life who trusts you enough. You know what a friend is like before they move in. # What they are like - Everybody has two or three of these: tidy or messy, quiet or noisy, an early bird or a night owl, generous or tight with money, reliable or late with rent, cooks or raids the fridge, sociable or keeps to themselves. - You learn the rest by living together: one more every {rm_reveal} days, or sooner when it shows. # Living together - Every {rm_rent_days} days they pay their share of the rent. It appears in your statement as Roommate's share of the rent. If you own your home they are a lodger and pay you the same share of what the home would let for. - Somebody who is late with rent sometimes pays nothing on the day, or part of it, and promises the rest. You can wait, ask for it now, let it go, or give notice. - When their hours say they are in and you are at home, they are in the flat. Walk up to them and press {key_interact} to talk. Asleep, or in their room, they are in the flat but you do not see them. - A messy roommate leaves the flat dirtier and a tidy one cleans it. One who cooks leaves a portion in your fridge some evenings: eat it together, or reheat it at a cooker later. One who raids the fridge takes one item at a time, at most {rm_raids} a week, and never when {rm_raid_leaves} or fewer are left. You can ask them to stop. - A noisy night costs you some mood and some sleep. Company at dinner and a meal together lift your mood. - The Planner shows the next rent day, money they owe you and the day they move out. # Getting on - Talking, shared meals, lending them money and letting a late week go bring you closer. Short answers, rows and unpaid rent do the opposite. - At {rm_friend} out of 100 they become one of the people in your social life, if you have not met your neighbour there yet, and may introduce you to somebody. # Ending it - Either of you can give notice. They move out {rm_notice_days} days later, pay for the days since the last rent day, and their share stops. Nobody leaves of their own accord in the first {rm_stay} days unless things are very bad. - When your partner moves in, a roommate with a bed of their own asks whether to stay. One on the sofa moves out. - When you move home they come along if the new home has room and you get on ({rm_good} out of 100 or more). Otherwise it ends. # Known limits - They never lie down: asleep, they are not shown. - Food is only taken from the fridge while you are at home, or from portions you have put by. - Cooking, the fridge, dirt and sleep need Home life and health to be on.

reallife_guide_economy_cleaning: # What it is - A crew of cleaners who go round several businesses, in place of a cleaner standing in each shop all day. - It runs while Credit rating and phone loans is on, and has its own switch in the options. - Everything is in the Services app on the phone. The Company app's Overview has a button to it. # The crew - Hire cleaners through the game's recruitment. Assign each to a building of yours and give them cleaning shifts there in BizMan. - Those shifts are their working hours. The game pays them for those hours as it always does. - On the Crew tab, put them on the crew. It takes up to {svc_crew_most} cleaners. - While a cleaner is at their own building they clean it as the game has it. While they are out, it does not get their work. - A cleaner who is off sick makes no visit that day. # The round - On the Cleaning tab, add the businesses to look after, up to {svc_clients_most}. Each is served when needed, or at up to {svc_visits} hours a day that you set. - When needed means: a visit is due once cleanliness falls under the threshold you choose. It is {svc_threshold} to begin with. - The round is planned again every hour for the rest of the day. Of all the visits that are due, the one a cleaner can start soonest is given to that cleaner, then the next, until nothing more fits. - A cleaner must reach the place, clean for {svc_visit_least} minutes at least and be back at their own building before their shift ends. No visit is longer than {svc_visit_most} minutes. - The plan looks for the earliest start of each visit, not for the shortest way round. - A shop is visited only on a day it is open and not shut for a time, as the game cleans it only then. # What a visit does - For every minute a cleaner is there, the floor is cleaned as a cleaning shift of theirs would clean it: their skill by their satisfaction, divided by the cleaners the floor needs for its size. - It is written to the game's own floor, so customers, satisfaction and BizMan all see it. - If you are in the shop during a visit and it has a free cleaning station, the cleaner is there with a mop. Without a station the visit still cleans, and the page says when the cleaner was in. # Travel - The way between two doors is the straight line and {svc_street}% more for the streets. - On foot the crew makes {svc_walk} m in a game minute, by van {svc_van} m. A door more than {svc_travel_most} minutes away is on nobody's round. - The van costs {svc_van_cost} a kilometre at a price index of 100. It is charged each morning for the day before. # What the page shows - For each business: the minutes of cleaning a day it needs, what it got today, its cleanliness with the change since the morning, and its next visit. - What a business needs is measured: how much dirtier its worst floor tile gets in a day, averaged over {svc_need_days} days. - For the service: its cost a week, the crew's wages and the van, against one cleaner at each of your shops for the whole hours each needs. # Contracts - With somebody on the crew, other businesses ask for cleaning: about one every {svc_offer_every} days, {svc_offers} open at most, each for {svc_offer_open} days. Up to {svc_contracts} contracts run at once. - A contract pays a weekly fee, {svc_fee_least} at least, and names a cleanliness to keep. - The floor is measured each morning. With more than {svc_days_under} mornings of a week under the standard, the week pays nothing and costs {svc_penalty}% of the fee. After {svc_misses} such weeks running the contract ends. - A client's floor is kept by this mod, since the game keeps none for a business that is not yours. It gets dirtier each morning, more so where there is room for more customers. A visit cleans it by the same sum as your own shops. # Known limits - At their own building a cleaner is still seen at work while they are out on the round.
reallife_guide_economy_sale: # What it is - A business that takes money can be sold for what it is worth, instead of being shut. - It runs while Credit rating and phone loans is on, and has its own switch in the options. - It is on the Sell tab of the Services app. A business's page in the Company app has a button to it. # What a business is worth - The start is {sale_days} days of its recent daily profit: the figure investors value a business by. - That is taken by its kind, by its district's income ({sale_district_least}% to {sale_district_most}%) and by the economy ({sale_boom}% in a boom, {sale_slow}% in a slowdown or a recession). - A business with fewer than {sale_history} days of books counts in proportion. One with no books, or with a loss, has no such value. - Its stock and furniture are added at the price the game itself pays when a lease ends. - Investors with a share of the business are bought out, and business loans secured on it are paid off, out of the price first. The page shows what is left. # The market - Choose an asking price from {sale_asking_least}% to {sale_asking_most}% of the value and put the business on the market. - Offers come from the next day on. At the value there are {sale_gap_value} days between offers and {sale_offers_value} offers in all. A lower price brings more, sooner. A higher price brings fewer, later, and the highest may bring none. - An offer follows the asking price part of the way and is never above it. It stands for {sale_offer_least} to {sale_offer_most} days. - A listing ends by itself after {sale_listing_days} days. # The buyers - A rival owner offers about {sale_rival}% of the value, pays at once, takes on none of the staff and asks you to stay out of that trade in the district for {sale_rival_clause} days. - An investor offers about {sale_investor}%, pays at once and keeps the staff. - Your staff offer about {sale_staff}%, pay in {sale_staff_parts} weekly parts and keep their jobs. - A chain offers about {sale_chain}%, pays at once or in {sale_chain_parts} parts, takes on none of the staff and asks for {sale_chain_clause} days. - You may accept, refuse, or ask for {sale_counter}% more, once. The buyer pays it, meets you half way or refuses. Of the buyers who refuse, {sale_walk}% walk away. - A quick sale pays {sale_quick}% of the value at once. # The sale - The game asks before anything is done. A sale cannot be undone. - You cannot sell while you stand in the building, while a vehicle of yours is kept there, or while a special gift is inside. - Staff the buyer keeps are paid for the day and leave your payroll. Staff the buyer does not keep stay with you, unassigned. - The business is shut as the game shuts one, its stock and furniture go with it, the lease ends and your deposit comes back. - Where the game has a business of that kind for a building of that size, one opens there. Otherwise the building is free to rent. A building you own stays yours. - A price in parts comes every {sale_part_days} days. - If you promised to stay out of the trade and take on a business of that kind in that district in time, you pay {sale_clause_penalty}% of the price, once.
