reallife_guide_economy_brands: # What it is - A brand is a name that several of your shops of one type trade under. It runs while Credit rating and phone loans is on. Off, nothing is paid, no applicant comes and every shop's customers are without it. - Everything is in the Brands app on the phone. The Planner lists an applicant who waits, what a franchisee asks, a renewal and an inspection that is due. - Sums given here are at a price index of 100. With the city's economy on they follow prices. - You can keep {br_brands_most} brands. # Making a brand - Pick a shop on the Shops tab and make it a brand. It takes the shop's name, which you can change. Other shops of the same type can join. - That first shop is the flagship. From the brand's Settings page you can copy its prices and its opening hours to every other member shop. Prices are only changed for products a shop already sells. Shifts are not changed: fill the rotas afterwards. # Standards - A shop's standards run from 0 to 100: {br_w_sat}% the game's customer satisfaction, {br_w_clean}% its cleanliness, {br_w_stock}% the share of its main goods on the shelves, {br_w_skill}% its staff's skill. - The brand's standards are {br_mean}% the mean of all its shops and {br_worst}% its worst shop. One bad shop drags the brand. - You set a required minimum. A franchisee found under it can be warned. # Recognition - Each district has a figure from 0 to 100, and there is one for the whole city. - A district's figure grows each day with the shops there (four count at most), the customers they serve, standards over 50 and campaigns. A gain counts for less the nearer the figure is to 100. - It fades by {br_decay}% of itself a day, and by {br_decay_empty}% where the brand has no shop left. - A brand campaign in one district adds {br_push_local} points a day there. A city-wide one adds {br_push_city} in every district with a shop. - Something the city hears about at a member shop costs recognition in its district: {br_scandals}. The city-wide figure loses a quarter of that. - One shop with good standards settles near 33, two near 44 and four busy ones near 60. Two shops take about 100 days to pass 28. # What a member shop gets - Up to {br_rec_most}% more customers at recognition of 100. With standards under {br_low} the name is worth half. - Of the customers its prices cost it by the city's economy, up to {br_tolerance} points are given back at standards of 100, and nothing at 50 or under. - A brand never adds more than {br_cap}% at a shop. The city's economy, your campaigns and the brand are added up, and the sum is kept to 15% more customers. In a boom with a campaign running the brand adds little on top. # Franchising - A brand can be offered once it has {br_offer_shops} member shops with standards of {br_offer_standards} or more, and recognition of {br_offer_city} city-wide or {br_offer_district} in one district. - Applicants then come. Each waits {br_app_days} days and up to {br_app_most} wait at a time. You see their capital, their years in the trade, their record and their temperament: careful, ambitious, or one who cuts corners. - You pick a building to let in the district they want, and the terms: an entry fee of {br_fees}, a royalty of {br_royalties} of takings, a marketing levy of {br_levies}, the district to themselves or not, and {br_lengths} years. - An applicant refuses terms that ask too much for how well the brand is known. A district to themselves makes harder terms acceptable. - The shop opens as a business of the city's where the game has one of the type that fits the building. It keeps the game's own name and sign, because the game finds such a business by its name. The Brands app and the city map show it under your brand. - Where the game has none that fits, the franchisee takes on a shop of the type that already trades in the district. Failing that, the shop is kept in the Brands app's books only, and takes up to {br_cannibal}% of the customers of each member shop within {br_radius} m, {br_cannibal_most}% in all. - Each day you are paid the royalty and the levy, and you pay support of {br_support_base} and {br_support_share}% of takings for each shop. Franchisees expect the levy spent on brand campaigns: past {br_fund_idle} unspent it is a grievance. - A franchised shop's takings follow the franchisee's ability, the brand's recognition there, the district's income, the economy, its own standards and the brand's other shops in the district. - A franchise brings about 15% of what a shop you run yourself does. It takes none of your capital and little of your time. # Keeping a franchisee to the standards - A franchisee's standards count in the brand's from the first day. You only see them when the shop is inspected. - Stand in the shop to inspect it yourself, free, or send an inspector for {br_inspector}. The Planner asks for an inspection after {br_inspect_due} days. - A shop found under the minimum in the last {br_fresh} days can be warned. A warning lifts its standards for {br_warn_days} days. Retraining costs {br_retrain} and lifts them at once. - After {br_cause} warnings, a fresh inspection that still finds it under the minimum is cause to end the agreement at no cost. - Ending an agreement without cause costs compensation, at least {br_comp_share}% of the entry fee, and {br_unfair} points of recognition in the district. # What a franchisee may do - Close, if the money runs out. That costs {br_failure} points of recognition in the district. - Ask for help when short of cash: a grant of {br_help_days} ordinary days' takings, or the royalty and levy waived for {br_waive} days. - Ask to open a second shop, at {br_second_share}% of the entry fee. - Ask to renew {br_renewal_notice} days before the agreement runs out, for {br_renewal_share}% of the entry fee. - Dispute the terms. With the courts on, the claim is filed there and answered in your Legal file. You can also give way: the royalty goes down a step. - Bid for the brand. If you sell, your member shops trade on under their own names. - What is asked waits {br_ask_days} days for an answer. # A franchise of a city chain - A shop of yours that is under no brand can take a franchise of one of three city chains: {br_chains}- The chain's customers come from the first day, for as long as the shop keeps the chain's standards and prices. - After {br_chain_warn} days outside them the chain writes and its name brings nothing. After {br_chain_fine} days it fines. After {br_chain_end} it ends the agreement. - Leaving costs {br_chain_exit} ordinary days of royalty, and never less than half the fee. # Known limits - Royalties are paid to you and not to one of your businesses, so the game's yearly tax on business sales does not count them. - A franchised shop that is a business of the city's can be closed by the city's own market, like any other. The agreement then ends with nobody at fault. - A franchised shop that is a business of the city's stays in the city while the option is off. Nothing is paid then.

reallife_guide_economy_estate_about: Buy run-down buildings, let them to tenants, improve them and sell them on. Run an estate agency, own a hotel, and hire out your cars.
reallife_guide_economy_estate: # What it is - Property is three businesses in one app, Property, on the phone. Each has its own switch in the options, and all three run while Credit rating and phone loans is on. - The game already lets you buy a building and takes rent for it. This adds a market that moves, tenants you choose, repairs and works, a sale with offers, an estate agency, a hotel and car hire. - Nothing new is built and no building changes its look: this is rules and money over the city as it stands. # The market - A building's price is the game's own value of it, by the property market, prices, its district's income and its condition. The game's own screens show the same price. - About {est_run_down} of the city's buildings are run down. They cost less, let for less and cost money to put right. - The property market moves once a month of the city's economy, by {est_step} at most. A boom takes it towards {est_boom} of its usual level and a recession towards {est_recession}. A high bank rate holds it down. - Rents follow prices, not the property market. A building bought in a boom earns less on its price. - The Market tab lists what is for sale. Its button opens the game's own purchase screen. For a mortgage, arrange it in Finance first. # Letting - A building you own is let by the game, as before, until you press Let it yourself on the Mine tab. It then has one tenant on a lease. - The market's rent is between {est_yield_low} and {est_yield_high} of the game's value a year, by use and district: dear districts yield less. You ask between {est_ask_low} and {est_ask_high} of it. - Up to {est_applicants} applicants wait at a time, for {est_applicant_days} days each. Each offers a rent and has a record of paying. A poorer record offers more, misses more days and wears the place faster. - The game pays the agreed rent each night. On a missed day nothing comes in. A deposit of {est_deposit_days} days' rent is held against what is owed. - With {est_arrears_days} days owed you can serve notice: {est_notice_days} days, more under rent controls. If the tenant stays, the court gives possession {est_court_days} days after you apply, for {est_court_fee}. - In a steady economy a let shop building returns about {est_return_let} a year after empty days, arrears, cover and wear: about {est_return_let_poor} in the poorest district and {est_return_let_rich} in the richest. A shop of your own is taken to return about {est_return_shop}. # Condition and works - Condition falls a little every day. Under {est_poor} applicants stay away, and under {est_unfit} a building cannot be let. - A repair from nothing to new costs {est_repair} of the game's value. Landlord's cover costs {est_cover} of it a year and pays for a fire or a flood, less {est_cover_excess} of the bill. - A refurbishment has {est_levels} levels. All three add {est_level_value} to the value and {est_level_rent} to the rent. In a boom the value added is more than the cost, in a slump less. - A change of use needs the council first: {est_planning_days} days and a fee, with about a {est_planning_chance} chance of permission, more when the council has eased permits. The game's own building type stays as it is. # Selling - Put a building up for sale on the Mine tab at a share of its worth. Offers come by price and by the economy and stand for {est_offer_days} days. - An accepted sale completes {est_completion_days} days later, unless the buyer's own sale fails. The selling fee is {est_agent_fee} of the price, and a gain is taxed at {est_gains} of the game's tax rate. # The agency - Open it on the Agency tab at an office you hold. Staff on that office's rota with the customer service skill are its negotiators. - Owners ask it to sell or let, by district and by its reputation there. You have {est_answer_days} days to take an instruction on, and it holds {est_instructions} at a time. - Taking one on costs its marketing at once. It then needs hours of a negotiator's time, and a deal within {est_lapse_days} days. - A completed sale pays {est_commission_sale} of the price and a letting {est_commission_let} of the first year's rent. A completion raises the reputation in that district. A lost instruction lowers it. # A hotel - The city's hotels are on the Market tab. A hotel costs {est_hotel_years} years of its takings at {est_hotel_occupancy} of rooms sold. Or lease it for a deposit of {est_lease_days} days' lease and a lease every day. - Set each room type's rate between {est_rate_low} and {est_rate_high} of the going rate. A dearer room sells less. - Rooms sold follow the season, the weekend, events in the city, the economy, the district, your rate, your rating and a campaign of {est_campaign_days} days. - Staff come on a contract at three levels. A better one costs more and keeps the place cleaner. The rating is made of cleanliness, staff and price. - An inspector calls every {est_inspection} days and fines a hotel under {est_inspection_pass} clean. A pipe can burst. A group can ask for rooms at {est_group_discount} off. - At a hotel you hold, your own room is free, and the reception has The books. # Car hire - Open a lot on the Car hire tab at a building you hold. It has the building's own vehicle spaces, or {est_hire_spaces} at the kerb, and {est_hire_cars} at most. - A car of yours goes on hire when it stands within {est_hire_metres} m of the lot's door, legally parked and empty. - A hire lasts up to {est_hire_days} days. The customer pays a deposit of {est_hire_deposit} days' hire, which goes back with the car. A hired car is gone from the city until then. - It comes back to the same spot with the distance on its record, less fuel, and worn tyres and brakes. About {est_hire_damage} of hires end with damage and {est_hire_late} a day late. About {est_hire_stolen} of cars do not come back at all. - Fleet cover costs {est_hire_cover} of a car's list price a year and pays {est_hire_pays} of what the deposit does not meet. A hire car returns about {est_return_hire} of its list price a year. # Known limits - No new building, hotel room or showroom can be made. A hotel's rooms are counted, not furnished. - A hotel is held in this mod's books. The game cannot put your employees in a hotel building, so its staff are a contract. - A tenant, a guest and a hirer are not seen in the city. Whoever the game shows in a building's unit stays there. - Each building you let yourself has one tenant, though the game counts many units in it.

reallife_rota_head_your_people: Your people: skills, pay, what they ask for, and what the advised plan gives them

reallife_rota_why_best_same: No change of hours or rota was found that beats the week you have.

reallife_rota_why_best_cut: The hours nobody can stand at a till for are closed. The game sells nothing in them and thieves still come.
reallife_rota_why_best_hours: The hours that pay are opened and the others closed, as far as your people can keep them.
reallife_rota_why_hire: One more for {who} keeps {hours} more hours with the crew there. Customers served a week more: {customers}.

reallife_rota_sum_sales: Customers served leave, after the goods:
reallife_rota_sum_theft: Theft, by the game's hourly rule:

reallife_rota_hire_where: Hire in the MyEmployees app on your phone, or from a job board in the building.
reallife_rota_hire_cost: The game charges nothing to take somebody on unless you offer a signing bonus, so the gain starts in the first week.
reallife_rota_hire_cost_once: Paid once: {amount}. Weeks until the gain has paid it: {weeks}.
reallife_rota_use_after: Use these hours once you have hired

reallife_rota_way_service: The cleaning service could clean here instead.
reallife_rota_way_replace: Somebody who asks for fewer hours would fit this business better.

reallife_changes_002_2: The Company app has a Rota tab. It shows the game's customer forecast for each hour, the opening hours that pay for their staff, and how many people a business needs. One button fills the week's rota by each employee's skills and demands, and another puts the old rota back. A business or a warehouse can now sell online: the new Web shop app opens an online shop, orders come in from the whole city by the hour, and your staff pick them from the real stock. Orders go out with your own vans or a courier. Late and missing deliveries cost refunds and a star rating, and some orders come back. The day's online takings, refunds and delivery costs are booked each night and count as the business's takings for tax. Cleaners can be shared. Put them on a crew in the new Services app and they go round the businesses on its list, when a floor needs it or at hours you set, on foot or by van. Other businesses in the city offer cleaning contracts with a weekly fee and a standard to keep. A business can be sold. The Services app shows what it is worth line by line. Put it on the market and a rival owner, an investor, your staff or a chain make offers with their own terms, or take a quick sale at a discount. Shops of one type can now trade as a brand, with recognition in each district and standards all its shops share: a known, well-kept brand brings its shops up to 12% more customers. A brand can be franchised: applicants open shops under it, pay an entry fee and a share of their takings every day, and need inspecting, warning and sometimes help. One of your own shops can instead take a franchise of a city chain. Hair keeps its own colour against a lamp. With a car's lights behind or beside your head, dark hair stays dark; before, it could glow as bright as skin and look bald. The Tests section has three entries for hair: one says what your hair is made of, one stands a strong lamp beyond your head for 20 seconds, one switches the hair finish off and on. Traffic now sees people in the road: cars brake for anyone in their way, sound the horn at somebody who steps out close or dawdles, wait, and drive on. People no longer fade out beside a braking car. A driver who cannot stop when an accident is due really hits the person, at the speed that is left, and stops or drives off. Cars that collide on the road slide to rest before the scene is set up, a car that loses a bend ends against what stands there, and a reckless driver who calms down drives on without pulling up. Property is a new app on the phone. Buy run-down buildings at prices that move with the economy, let them to tenants you choose, repair and refurbish them, and sell them for offers; or run an estate agency from an office with your own staff. You can also buy or lease one of the city's hotels and set its rates and staff, and put your own cars out on hire from a lot. The rota planner now shows a ladder of plans for each business: the week as it is, the best week your people can keep, and one plan for each further person worth hiring, with what each adds. Plans count what the game counts: nothing sells at an unstaffed till, a till serves a fixed number an hour, cleanliness, theft, and what an unmet demand costs. You can choose staff first or lean for each business; the choice is saved. Every hour a plan opens or closes is listed with its reason. A plan that needs a hire cannot be written until you have hired. A business cleaned by the cleaning service gets no cleaning shift. The options page is in ten groups, from "Start here" to "Troubleshooting". A group opens to short sections, one at a time, and each button says how many of its switches are on. Every option has a short name and one sentence, shown when the pointer rests on its row. A greyed row says which option it needs. Test tools are under Troubleshooting and only on the page while "Show test tools" is on. Fixed: the game froze for seconds when an ambulance crew stepped out. Fixed: a car in the custom shop shot backwards when the shop closed. The driving test now marks only what you could have helped: a tap of the brake, a light that changes on top of you and where the school left the car are no longer faults. People react to your horn: someone in your way who should not be there hurries clear, and someone with the light in their favour stops and glares. Keep it up near a police officer and you are warned, then fined. Accidents now come from drivers you can watch go wrong, such as speeders, red-light runners, late brakers and drunks at night: they may crash where it happens, run somebody down, drive off and be chased, or be pulled over by a patrol car. The minimap now shows the city's buildings and its water under the roads, in the colours of the game's interface. The city is measured for this once for each version of the game, in the first seconds out in the city. Every table in Finance, Ventures, Company and the Planner now sorts when you click a column heading, can be filtered by kind from a list above it, and ends in a line of totals. Accounts, offers, cash flow, investors, shares and staff show more columns, and the box beside them says more about whatever you pick. A bus stop's panel, and every other panel over a door or desk, now stands beside a building's info box and no longer covers it. Fishing, the dance floor and the chess clock show their timing on one of the game's own bars. While another camera mod drives the camera, this mod's cameras stand aside and come back when it stops. With Voogle Route switched on, this mod's route is drawn on the minimap only, and a new option leaves the route to that mod. You can share your flat. Ring the new Roommate contact to put up a notice or ask a friend: with a second bed, or at least a sofa, somebody moves in, pays a share of the rent every week and is at home when their hours say so. Some are tidy, some are noisy, some are late with the rent, and you can talk it over, wait, or give notice. reallife_opt_ask_preset:
{about}

This changes {count} of your options, {switches} of them switches. Camera, picture, clothes, keys and performance stay as they are. Your choices are saved to a file first, so 'Load my choices from the file' brings them back.
reallife_opt_test_layout: Write the options page's layout to Player.log
reallife_opt_test_layout_done: The layout of the options page is in Player.log.
reallife_opt_tip_camera_enabled: The camera follows behind your character. Off, the game's own camera is used.
reallife_opt_tip_camera_mouselook: Move the mouse to look around. The 'Free the cursor' key under Controls gives the pointer back.
reallife_opt_tip_camera_sensitivity: How far the view turns for the same movement of the mouse.
reallife_opt_tip_enter_with_key: The interact keys take you into buildings and into your vehicles without a click.
reallife_opt_tip_camera_indoors: The third-person camera is used inside buildings as well.
reallife_opt_tip_camera_pitch: How steeply the camera looks down. With mouse look on, this is the tilt it starts at.
reallife_opt_tip_camera_distance: How far behind your character the camera stands.
reallife_opt_tip_camera_fov: How wide the view is. A higher number shows more and makes things smaller.
reallife_opt_tip_camera_height: The height on your character that the camera looks at.
reallife_opt_tip_car_camera: A camera that follows behind your car. Hold the look-behind key to look back.
reallife_opt_tip_car_camera_distance: How far behind your car the chase camera stands.
reallife_opt_tip_car_tuning: Every car accelerates and tops out like its kind. Off, the game's own cars.
reallife_opt_tip_car_top_speed: The top speed of every car, as a share of what its kind really reaches.
reallife_opt_tip_car_acceleration: How quickly every car gains speed, as a share of what its kind really does.
reallife_opt_tip_smooth_throttle: The key eases the pedal down, so a tap pulls away gently.
reallife_opt_tip_speedometer: Your speed is shown on screen while you drive.
reallife_opt_tip_camera_follow: With mouse look off, how quickly the camera comes round behind you.
reallife_opt_tip_map_places_shown: Bus stops, hotels, the courthouse, driving schools, custom shops and the mod's other places are marked on the city map, each with its own filter.
reallife_opt_tip_visuals_enabled: The colour, contrast, bloom and detail settings below are applied. Off, the picture is the game's own.
reallife_opt_tip_visuals_contrast: How far light and dark are apart.
reallife_opt_tip_visuals_bloom: The glow round bright lights. At 0 it is the game's own.
reallife_opt_tip_visuals_detail: How far away the game still draws things in full detail.
reallife_opt_tip_character_high_detail: Your character uses the game's detailed model in the city. This changes the picture.
reallife_opt_tip_character_hair: Hair and beards on detailed characters are thicker. This changes the picture.
reallife_opt_tip_character_lighting: Faces are lit more softly in character creation and in shop previews.
reallife_opt_tip_character_skin: A fine grain and a calmer shine on your character's skin when the camera is close.
reallife_opt_tip_character_new_looks: The mod's clothes and shoes can be worn, and hair no longer looks thin from a distance.
reallife_opt_tip_look2_top_m: The top a male character wears.
reallife_opt_tip_look2_top_m_colour: Its colour. A print the top cannot carry shows as a plain colour.
reallife_opt_tip_look2_legs_m: The trousers a male character wears.
reallife_opt_tip_look2_legs_m_colour: Their colour. A print the trousers cannot carry shows as a plain colour.
reallife_opt_tip_look_feet_m: The shoes a male character wears.
reallife_opt_tip_look2_dress_f: A dress for a female character. It replaces the top and the trousers.
reallife_opt_tip_look2_dress_f_colour: Its colour. A print the dress cannot carry shows as a plain colour.
reallife_opt_tip_look2_top_f: The top a female character wears.
reallife_opt_tip_look2_top_f_colour: Its colour. A print the top cannot carry shows as a plain colour.
reallife_opt_tip_look2_legs_f: The trousers or skirt a female character wears.
reallife_opt_tip_look2_legs_f_colour: Their colour. A print the garment cannot carry shows as a plain colour.
reallife_opt_tip_look_feet_f: The shoes a female character wears.
reallife_opt_tip_life_events: Now and then something happens to you: a windfall, a cold, a call from Mom.
reallife_opt_tip_life_frequency: About how many life events come in a week.
reallife_opt_tip_crash_consequences: Crashing your car costs damages and can hurt you.
reallife_opt_tip_traffic_accidents: Other cars crash now and then, and police, ambulances and tow trucks come.
reallife_opt_tip_police: Patrol cars come to accidents and crimes, officers walk the streets, and drivers are pulled over.
reallife_opt_tip_police_presence: How many parked patrol cars and officers you see about. 0 is none.
reallife_opt_tip_police_pursuit: If you hit a car or a person and drive off, the police come after you.
reallife_opt_tip_siren: Police cars, ambulances and fire engines sound their sirens on the way.
reallife_opt_tip_people: Drivers get out after a crash, paramedics work, and officers stand at scenes.
reallife_opt_tip_patrol_officers: Police officers on foot pass near you from time to time.
reallife_opt_tip_ragdolls: A person your car hits is thrown down and can be hurt or killed. Off, cars pass through people.
reallife_opt_tip_player_knockdown: A car that hits you on foot throws you down.
reallife_opt_tip_ped_incidents: Now and then a pedestrian near you is hit by a car, and help comes.
reallife_opt_tip_horn_reactions: People in your way hurry or stop and glare when you sound the horn, and others look round.

reallife_changes_002_3: The rota planner now treats the hours a week an employee asks for as compulsory: never fewer than the least, never more than the most, for cashiers and cleaners alike. Shifts follow the customers: the busiest hours are staffed first and cleaning is one shift a day around them. Where your opening hours cannot hold everybody's hours, the planner opens the best paying hours beside them and says for whom. The more skilled employee is given hours first. Whoever would have no hours is given the quieter hours where the stations have them, and only staff the business has no hours for are left without, named so that you can let them go. In the Company app you can now raise an underpaid employee to the going rate at any time, without waiting for them to ask, and whatever waits for your answer has its buttons at the top of its page. Troubleshooting has a new test tool that says what is blocking you where you stand. The mod can now be read in Brazilian Portuguese: it follows the language the game is set to. Fixed: with the performance option that hides far districts on, a parked car could stand at the kerb unseen and block the pavement; parked cars are never hidden now.

reallife_guide_economy_banks: # What it is - Each of the city's three largest banks has its own app on the phone, under the game's own name for the bank. A city with fewer banks has fewer apps. - An app shows only what you hold with that bank. The Finance app still shows every lender at once. Both read the same records, so a payment made in one shows in the other at once. - It runs while the credit rating is on. # The tabs - Accounts: your current account and an overdraft held there, with a statement of the money that moved with that bank. Your cash is held with the largest bank. - Loans: every loan you owe that bank, the game's own and this mod's. Pick one to pay some of it or all of it. A game loan is paid as EconoView pays it. - Card: a card held there, with its limit, balance, statement, minimum and due day. Pay it or draw cash on it. - Apply: what that bank offers you today: a loan, an overdraft, a card, a business loan, car finance, a mortgage and consolidation. - Rating: what that bank lends at each rating, and what would raise yours. # How the banks differ - The largest bank keeps the usual rates, limits and fees. - The second charges a point more, gives a quarter more on a card, an overdraft and finance, and takes half the usual fee on a loan by phone. - The third charges a point less, gives a fifth less, and takes three quarters of the usual fee. - The game's own loan at the bank counter keeps the bank's own terms. # Limits - You hold one overdraft and one card in all, with the bank that opened them. - Under a rating of {bank_threshold} no bank lends at all, in any app or at the counter. - The apps keep nothing of their own in your save.

Fixed: a car towed near the hospital after a crash (or out of a police impound) could stay where it was to the eye, with its marker on the map, while you walked through it and could not get in; the whole car now goes to the space. Fixed: the game could freeze for two seconds as an ambulance crew got out with the stretcher at an accident; the way they wheel it is now worked out in a moment. Bus stops: Choose a stop now opens the city map, as a subway entrance does. Every stop the buses reach is marked on it, and the game's list of stations beside it lists them with the line, the time and the fare, with a search field. Point at a stop to see it; click it to pick it. Fixed: at a subway entrance the mod's own list of stations had taken the place of the game's subway map. A click on the entrance opens the game's map again, and the mod adds the time of the journey when you come up. A day pass gives the game's fare back. The nightly closure of one station for track work is gone. On the city map, the mod's buildings now light up when their row is ticked, the way the game's own buildings do for theirs: police stations, the courthouse, hotels, driving schools, the buildings with a help-wanted board, polling places and construction sites, each in its row's colour and with its icon. The courthouse's card names it, with its hours. One calendar: a month is now a twelfth of the year you chose for your game (5 days in a 60-day year, 30 in a 365-day one), and the seasons are the weather's everywhere. Car insurance runs a month; childcare and private school are named by that month and paid by the week, at the same cost by the day as before; hotels and property follow the weather's seasons. Wages follow prices once: the city's cost of living pays every wage at today's prices, and the going rate staff compare their pay with is at today's prices too, so rising prices no longer make staff ask for raises on top. The city's wage floor counts any raise you agreed and moves with prices, and every amount of the city government (levies, grants, the licence fee, the ticket and fare changes, donations and shop refits) is at today's prices. Your businesses' books: the wages, marketing and licences of the Company features now show in the game's own daily statement of each business (EconoView, the daily summary), and the game's bank sizes a loan by that profit. Insurance, accountants and hosting, for which the game's statement has no line, stay in the Finance app. Fixed: a parking ticket on a lent car (the driving school's, a hired van) is paid back whole, the city policy's change to it included. The city's business tax share applies only where the game charges income tax at all. The pound charges one fee whatever the car was taken for, and the roadside tow is the hospital tow's. A partner's and a roommate's share of the rent is of what the home costs at today's prices. An online shop's takings follow prices as a shop's takings do. Life events about a credit card or an accountant happen only to somebody who has one.
reallife_changes_002_4: Each of the city's banks has its own app on the phone, under the game's name for it: your current account and statement, the loans you owe that bank with paying part or all of one, your card, what it offers you today and how it sees your rating. The banks' terms differ a little, so choosing one matters, and under a rating of 580 none of them lends. The mod's contacts have real pictures from the game: people show their faces, and services show a logo. Contacts has a search box at the top. Police stations are furnished with the game's own furniture: desks with computers, lockers, a water cooler, plants, a clock, lamps, and a toilet in the cell. Fixed: with all of the mod's apps on, the row of apps at the top of the full screen menu ran under the money and the date and off the screen; it now has pages, centred between the app's name and the money, turned with the wheel or the dots. Fixed: on the city map, a row of the mod's (Courthouse, Custom shops and the rest) could be unticked while its places stayed on the map; the places now follow the tick you see.
